Natural_Language: Accrued benefit cost method means an actuarial cost method under which units of benefits are assigned to each cost accounting period and are valued as they accrue; i.e., based on the services performed by each employee in the period involved. The measure of normal cost under this method for each cost accounting period is the present value of the units of benefit deemed to be credited to employees for service in that period. The measure of the actuarial accrued liability at a plan's inception date is the present value of the units of benefit credited to employees for service prior to that date. (This method is also known as the unit credit cost method without salary projection.)
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_002_def_01_a (units of benefits assigned to each cost accounting period and valued as they accrue based on services performed); P_31_002_def_01_b (normal cost = present value of units of benefit credited for service in that period); P_31_002_def_01_c (actuarial accrued liability at inception = present value of units of benefit credited for service prior to inception); P_31_002_def_01_d (also known as unit credit cost method without salary projection)
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement for "Accrued benefit cost method". Self-contained definition with no conditional structure or cross-references.

Natural_Language: Actual costs means (except for subpart 31.6) amounts determined on the basis of costs incurred, as distinguished from forecasted costs. Actual costs include standard costs properly adjusted for applicable variances.

Natural_Language: Actuarial accrued liability means pension cost attributable, under the actuarial cost method in use, to years prior to the current period considered by a particular actuarial valuation. As of such date, the actuarial accrued liability represents the excess of the present value of future benefits and administrative expenses over the present value of future normal costs for all plan participants and beneficiaries. The excess of the actuarial accrued liability over the actuarial value of the assets of a pension plan is the unfunded actuarial liability. The excess of the actuarial value of the assets of a pension plan over the actuarial accrued liability is an actuarial surplus and is treated as a negative unfunded actuarial liability.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_002_def_03_a (pension cost attributable to years prior to current period under actuarial cost method); P_31_002_def_03_b (represents excess of PV of future benefits/admin expenses over PV of future normal costs); P_31_002_def_03_c (excess of actuarial accrued liability over actuarial value of assets = unfunded actuarial liability); P_31_002_def_03_d (excess of actuarial value of assets over actuarial accrued liability = actuarial surplus = negative unfunded actuarial liability)
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement for "Actuarial accrued liability". Self-contained definition with no conditional structure or cross-references.

Natural_Language: 31.201-3 Determining reasonableness.

Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition on presuming reasonableness. Simple negation. Contractor must affirmatively establish reasonableness; it is not assumed.

Atomic_Propositions: P_31_201_3_b_2_a: Sound business practices; P_31_201_3_b_2_b: Arm's length bargaining; P_31_201_3_b_2_c: Federal and State laws and regulations
Validation_Notes: Second reasonableness factor. Three conjunctive sub-elements: business practices, arm's length standard, and legal compliance.

Atomic_Propositions: P_31_201_3_b_3: Contractor's responsibilities to Government, other customers, business owners, employees, and public
Validation_Notes: Third reasonableness factor. Multi-stakeholder responsibility assessment. Serial comma list is conjunctive: all stakeholder interests are considered.

Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: credit takes form of either cost reduction OR cash refund. Cross-reference to 31.105-6(i)(3) for pension/asset reversion specifics.

Natural_Language: No final cost objective must have allocated to it as an indirect cost any cost, if other costs incurred for the same purpose, in like circumstances, have been included as a direct cost of that or any other final cost objective.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_203_b_2_a: Other costs for same purpose in like circumstances included as direct cost; P_31_203_b_2_b: No such cost shall be allocated as indirect cost to any final cost objective

Validation_Notes: Mandatory cost grouping. 'Must' = mandatory. Two conjunctive requirements: logical grouping AND reason-based consideration.

Validation_Notes: Mandatory allocation base criterion: benefits-based. 'Must' = mandatory. Already atomic.

Validation_Notes: Should' = advisory. 'When' triggers conditional. Practicality override when precision doesn't improve results. HIGH-RISK: implication. PENDING_REVIEW per 'should' override.

Validation_Notes: Comprehensive base inclusion rule. Four conjunctive requirements ensuring no items excluded from bearing their share. G&A example illustrates principle. Prevents contractor from excluding unallowable costs from base to reduce allocation.

Validation_Notes: May' = permissive. Offsite location costs may warrant separate groupings for equity. Tautological consequent. PENDING_REVIEW: HIGH-RISK + discretionary.

Natural_Language: A base period for allocating indirect costs is the cost accounting period during which such costs are incurred and accumulated for allocation to work performed in that period.

Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional for base period. Three conjunctive elements: incurrence, accumulation, and allocation all within same period. Parent for (g)(1)-(3).

Validation_Notes: Conditional allowability for FFP/FP-EPA subcontract costs. Three conjunctive conditions: right contract type, cost analysis performed, and 31.102-compliant negotiation. External dependency to 31.102. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_a_1_a: Must be for current year work; P_31_205_6_a_1_b: Must not be retroactive adjustment; P_31_205_6_a_1_c: Exceptions for (f)(g)(i)(j)(l)(n)

Validation_Notes: Parent for (a)(6) sub-paragraphs covering special consideration individuals.

Natural_Language: For these individuals, compensation must-- (A) Be reasonable for the personal services rendered; and (B) Not be a distribution of profits (which is not an allowable contract cost).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_a_6_ii_A: Compensation reasonable for services; P_31_205_6_a_6_ii_B: Not a profit distribution

Validation_Notes: For identified individuals: two conjunctive requirements. Must be reasonable AND must not be profit distribution.

Natural_Language: Reasonableness. Establishes standards for determining whether compensation is reasonable, covering both labor-management agreement and non-agreement contexts.

Validation_Notes: Parent for reasonableness provisions covering two contexts: labor-management agreements and non-agreement compensation.

Natural_Language: Compensation pursuant to labor-management agreements. Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_b_1_a: LM agreement compensation is allowable/reasonable; P_31_205_6_b_1_b: Exception for unwarranted costs; P_31_205_6_b_1_c: Exception for discriminatory costs
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Presumption of allowability for NLRA-negotiated agreements UNLESS unwarranted or discriminatory. Two exception conditions negate the presumption.

Natural_Language: The terms of a labor-management agreement designed to apply to a given set of circumstances and conditions of employment (e.g., work involving extremely hazardous activities or work not requiring recurrent use of overtime) is unwarranted when applied to a Government contract involving significantly different circumstances and conditions of employment (e.g., work involving less hazardous activities or work continually requiring use of overtime).

Validation_Notes: Defines "unwarranted": agreement designed for one set of circumstances is unwarranted when applied to significantly different Government contract circumstances.

Natural_Language: A cost is discriminatory against the Government if it results in employee compensation, in whatever form, in excess of that being paid for similar non-Government work under comparable circumstances.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_b_1_ii: Cost is discriminatory if compensation exceeds comparable non-Government work

Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_b_2_ii_a: Consider practices of same-size firms; P_31_205_6_b_2_ii_b: Same industry; P_31_205_6_b_2_ii_c: Same geographic area; P_31_205_6_b_2_ii_d: Similar non-Government work

Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_g: Backpay is unallowable except for three enumerated exceptions
Validation_Notes: General prohibition with three disjunctive exceptions. "Except" creates carve-outs.

Natural_Language: Employees resulting from underpaid work actually performed are allowable, if required by a negotiated settlement, order, or court decree.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_g_1: Backpay for underpaid work is allowable if required by settlement/order/decree
Formal_Logic_Statement: Underpaid_Work ^ (Negotiated_Settlement v Order v Court_Decree) -> Allowable_Backpay
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Conditional: underpaid work AND required by settlement/order/decree. Two conjunctive conditions with disjunctive authority source.

Natural_Language: Union employees for the difference in their past and current wage rates for working without a contract or labor agreement during labor management negotiation are allowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_g_2: Union backpay for wage rate difference during no-contract period is allowable
Validation_Notes: Conditional: union employees working without contract during negotiation get backpay for wage difference.

Natural_Language: Nonunion employees based upon results of union agreement negotiation are allowable only if-- (i) or (ii).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_g_3: Nonunion backpay from union negotiation results -- allowable only if one of two conditions met
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: "Only if" with disjunctive conditions. Nonunion backpay allowable only if formal agreement OR established policy.

Natural_Language: A formal agreement or understanding exists between management and the employees concerning these payments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_g_3_i: Formal agreement/understanding exists for nonunion backpay
Validation_Notes: Atomic. One of two conditions for nonunion backpay allowability.

Natural_Language: An established policy or practice exists and is followed by the contractor so consistently as to imply an agreement to make such payments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_g_3_ii: Established policy/practice consistently followed implying agreement
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Second condition for nonunion backpay. Same "consistently as to imply" standard used elsewhere in 31.205-6.

Natural_Language: Compensation based on changes in the prices of corporate securities or corporate security ownership, such as stock options, stock appreciation rights, phantom stock plans, and junior stock conversions is unallowable as follows: (h)(1) through (h)(3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h: Parent -- stock/securities-based compensation is unallowable
Validation_Notes: Parent prohibition on securities-based compensation. Three categories all unallowable.

Natural_Language: Any compensation which is calculated, or valued, based on changes in the price of corporate securities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_1: Compensation based on security price changes is unallowable
Validation_Notes: Flat prohibition. Any compensation calculated or valued based on security price changes.

Natural_Language: Any compensation represented by dividend payments or which is calculated based on dividend payments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2: Dividend-based compensation is unallowable
Validation_Notes: Flat prohibition on dividend-based compensation.

Natural_Language: Contractor payments to an employee in lieu of the employee receiving or exercising a right, option, or benefit that would have been unallowable under this paragraph (h).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_3: Payments in lieu of unallowable security-based rights are also unallowable
Validation_Notes: Anti-circumvention: cannot substitute cash payments for what would be unallowable security-based compensation.

Natural_Language: Pension costs. (Parent for pension cost provisions including defined-benefit, defined-contribution, pay-as-you-go, and early retirement incentive plans.)
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_3_i: Parent for pension cost principles
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: This is 31.205-6(i), not (h)(3)(i). The skeleton parser misidentified paragraph (i) as a sub-paragraph of (h)(3). Actual section is 31.205-6(i) Pension costs. Parent for all pension provisions.

Natural_Language: Pension plans are normally segregated into two types of plans: defined-benefit and defined-contribution pension plans.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_1_v2: Two types of pension plans -- defined-benefit and defined-contribution
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(1). Definitional -- two disjunctive plan types.

Natural_Language: The contractor must measure, assign, and allocate the costs of defined-benefit pension plans and the costs of defined-contribution pension plans in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.412 and 48 CFR 9904.413.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_1_i: Contractor must measure/assign/allocate pension costs per CAS 412 and 413
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(1)(i). Mandatory CAS compliance for all pension costs.

Natural_Language: Pension costs are allowable subject to the referenced standards and the cost limitations and exclusions in this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_1_ii: Pension costs allowable subject to CAS standards and section limitations
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(1)(ii). General allowability subject to dual conditions.

Natural_Language: Defined-benefit pension plans. The cost limitations and exclusions pertaining to defined-benefit plans are as follows: (i) through (v) plus (3) pension adjustments.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_v2: Parent for defined-benefit pension plan cost limitations
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2). Parent for defined-benefit cost limitations and exclusions.

Natural_Language: Defined-benefit plan funding requirements: (A) Qualified plans -- costs assigned to current period but not funded are unallowable in subsequent years (except tax return timing). (B) Nonqualified plans -- allowable costs limited per CAS 9904.412-50(d)(2). (C) Nonqualified pay-as-you-go -- limited per CAS 9904.412-50(d)(3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_i_A: Qualified plan funding timing requirement; P_31_205_6_h_2_i_B: Nonqualified plan cost limit; P_31_205_6_h_2_i_C: Nonqualified PAYG limit
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(i). Three sub-rules (A)(B)(C) covering qualified and nonqualified DB plan funding. Complex multi-part provision.

Natural_Language: Except for nonqualified pension plans, pension costs (see 48 CFR 9904.412-40(a)(1)) assigned to the current accounting period, but not funded during it, are not allowable in subsequent years (except that a payment made to a fund by the time set for filing the Federal income tax return or any extension thereof is considered to have been made during such taxable year).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_1_v3: Qualified pension costs not funded in current period are unallowable later, with tax return filing exception
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(i)(A)(1). Funding timing requirement with tax return exception.

Natural_Language: Any portion of pension costs computed for a cost accounting period, that exceeds the amount required to be funded pursuant to a waiver granted under the provisions of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) (Chapter 18 of title 29, U.S.C.), will be allowable in those future accounting periods in which the funding of such excess amounts occurs (see 48 CFR 9904.412-50(c)(5)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_v3: ERISA-waived excess pension costs allowable when actually funded in future periods
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(i)(A)(2). ERISA waiver provision allows future-period recovery of excess costs.

Natural_Language: Excess funding and future allowability: (A) Amount funded in excess of pension cost assigned to a period is not allowable in that period per CAS 9904.412-50(a)(4). (B) The excess is allowable in the future period to which it is assigned, if not otherwise unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_ii_A: Excess funding not allowable in current period; P_31_205_6_h_2_ii_B: Excess allowable in future assigned period
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(ii). Two-part rule on excess funding timing.

Natural_Language: Increased pension costs from delayed funding: (A) Unallowable if increase caused by delay beyond 30 days after each quarter. (B) Composite rate inequity -- limited to segment-level calculation per CAS 9904.413-50(c). (C) Contractor must determine unallowable costs per actuarial method used.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_iii_A: Delay >30 days after quarter = unallowable increase; P_31_205_6_h_2_iii_B: Composite rate inequity limit; P_31_205_6_h_2_iii_C: Actuarial method for unallowable determination
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(iii). Three-part provision on delayed funding consequences.

Natural_Language: PBGC indemnification: (A) CO will consider allowability of PBGC indemnification costs under ERISA 4062/4064 on case-by-case basis if insurance was required and obtained. (B) Consideration primarily for appraising allocability to Government work. (C) Government will participate despite 31.205-19 if beneficial/equitable relationship exists.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_iv_A: PBGC indemnification case-by-case; P_31_205_6_h_2_iv_B: Allocability focus; P_31_205_6_h_2_iv_C: Government participation if equitable
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(iv). "Will consider" = discretionary. Three-part PBGC provision. Cross-reference to 31.205-19.

Natural_Language: Insurance was required by the PBGC under ERISA section 4023.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_1_v4: PBGC insurance was required under ERISA 4023
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(iv)(A)(1). Atomic condition for PBGC indemnification consideration.

Natural_Language: It was obtained and the indemnification payment is not recoverable under the insurance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_v4: Insurance obtained and indemnification not recoverable
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(iv)(A)(2). Two conjunctive conditions.

Natural_Language: Withdrawal of pension fund assets: (A) Increased costs from asset withdrawal/transfer are unallowable except per advance agreement (see (i)(3) for plan termination). (B) Advance agreement must state Government equitable share and provide credit.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_v_A: Increased costs from asset withdrawal unallowable except advance agreement; P_31_205_6_h_2_v_B: Advance agreement requirements
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(v). Two-part provision on asset withdrawal with advance agreement requirement.

Natural_Language: State the amount of the Government's equitable share in the gross amount withdrawn or transferred.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_1_v5: Advance agreement must state Government equitable share amount
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(v)(B)(1). First advance agreement requirement.

Natural_Language: Provide that the Government receives a credit equal to the amount of the Government's equitable share of the gross withdrawal or transfer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_v5: Advance agreement must provide Government credit for equitable share
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(2)(v)(B)(2). Second advance agreement requirement.

Natural_Language: Pension adjustments and asset reversions. Covers segment closings, plan terminations, curtailment of benefits, and other asset reversions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_3_v2: Parent for pension adjustment and asset reversion rules
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(3). Parent for pension adjustment provisions.

Natural_Language: For segment closings, pension plan terminations, or curtailment of benefits, the amount of the adjustment must be-- (A) For CAS-covered: per CAS 9904.413-50(c)(12). (B) For non-CAS-covered: per CAS 9904.413-50(c)(12) with modified numerator for non-CAS contracts subject to 31.2 or certified cost/pricing data.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_3_i_v2_A: CAS-covered adjustment per 413-50(c)(12); P_31_205_6_h_3_i_v2_B: Non-CAS adjustment with modified numerator
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Segment_Closing v Plan_Termination v Benefit_Curtailment) -> ((Full_CAS -> CAS_413_50_c_12) ^ (~Full_CAS ^ Subject_31_2 -> Modified_CAS_413_50_c_12))
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(3)(i). Complex bifurcated rule based on CAS coverage status.

Natural_Language: Other asset reversions: (A) For all other reversions, contractor must refund or credit Government equitable share of gross withdrawal. (B) Government share reflects participation through certified cost/pricing data contracts or 31.2-subject contracts. (C) Excise taxes on reversions/withdrawals are unallowable per 31.205-41(c)(6).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_3_ii_A: Government option for refund/credit; P_31_205_6_h_3_ii_B: Equitable share basis; P_31_205_6_h_3_ii_C: Excise taxes unallowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(3)(ii). Three-part provision. Cross-reference to 31.205-41(c)(6) for excise tax unallowability.

Natural_Language: Defined-contribution pension plans. In addition to defined-contribution pension plans, this paragraph also covers profit sharing, savings plans, and other such plans, provided the plans fall within the definition of a pension plan.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_4: Parent for defined-contribution plan rules (also covers profit sharing, savings plans)
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(4). Scope extends to profit sharing and savings plans meeting pension definition.

Natural_Language: Defined-contribution allowable cost limits: (A) Limited to net contribution required for cost accounting period after credits. (B) ERISA-waived excess allowable in future periods when funded per CAS 9904.412-50(c)(5).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_4_i_A: Net contribution limit after credits; P_31_205_6_h_4_i_B: ERISA excess in future periods
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(4)(i). Two-part limit on DC plan costs.

Natural_Language: The provisions of paragraphs (i)(2)(ii) and (i)(2)(iv) of this section apply to defined-contribution plans.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_4_ii: DB excess funding and PBGC indemnification rules also apply to DC plans
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(4)(ii). Cross-reference applying DB rules to DC context.

Natural_Language: Pension plans using the pay-as-you-go cost method.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_5: Parent for pay-as-you-go pension rules
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(5). Parent for PAYG pension provisions.

Natural_Language: Pension costs for a pension plan using the pay-as-you-go cost method are allowable to the extent they are not otherwise unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_5_i: PAYG pension costs allowable unless otherwise unallowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(5)(i). General allowability with negative condition.

Natural_Language: When using the pay-as-you-go cost method, the contractor must measure, assign, and allocate the cost of pension plans in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.412 and 9904.413.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_5_ii: PAYG method must still comply with CAS 412 and 413
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(5)(ii). CAS compliance mandatory even for PAYG method.

Natural_Language: Early retirement incentives.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_6: Parent for early retirement incentive provisions
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(6). Parent for early retirement provisions.

Natural_Language: An early retirement incentive is an incentive given to an employee to retire early.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_6_i: Definition -- early retirement incentive
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(6)(i). Definitional.

Natural_Language: Early retirement incentive costs allowable subject to pension cost criteria in (i)(2)(i) through (i)(2)(iv) if-- (1) measured/assigned/allocated per contractor accounting practices, (2) per plan terms, and (3) only for active employees. Excess over annual salary is unallowable. Present value per accounting practices. Unallowable costs per CAS 9904.412-50(a)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_6_ii_a: Three conditions for allowability; P_31_205_6_h_6_ii_b: Annual salary cap; P_31_205_6_h_6_ii_c: Present value and unallowable cost accounting
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(6)(ii). Complex multi-condition allowability with salary cap.

Natural_Language: Contractor measures, assigns, and allocates the costs in accordance with the contractor's accounting practices for pension costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_1_v6: ERI costs measured/assigned/allocated per contractor pension accounting practices
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(6)(ii)(A)(1). First allowability condition for ERI.

Natural_Language: Incentives are in accordance with the terms and conditions of an early retirement incentive plan.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_v6: ERI must conform to plan terms and conditions
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(6)(ii)(A)(2). Second condition.

Natural_Language: Contractor applies the plan only to active employees (i.e., the cost of extending the plan to employees who retired or were terminated before the adoption of the plan is unallowable).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_3_v3: ERI only for active employees; extending to previously retired/terminated is unallowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(6)(ii)(A)(3). Third condition with explicit prohibition on inactive employees.

Natural_Language: The contractor must compute the present value in accordance with its accounting practices for pension costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_1_v7: ERI present value computed per contractor pension accounting practices
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(6)(ii)(B)(1). Present value methodology requirement.

Natural_Language: The contractor must account for any unallowable costs in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.412-50(a)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_h_2_v7: Unallowable ERI costs accounted per CAS 9904.412-50(a)(2)
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(i)(6)(ii)(B)(2). CAS compliance for unallowable cost accounting.

Natural_Language: Deferred compensation other than pensions. The costs of deferred compensation awards are allowable subject to the following: (j)(1) and (j)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_j: Parent -- deferred compensation allowable subject to two conditions
Validation_Notes: Parent for deferred compensation provisions. Both conditions apply.

Natural_Language: The costs must be measured, assigned, and allocated in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.415.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_j_1: Deferred comp costs must comply with CAS 415
Validation_Notes: Mandatory CAS 415 compliance for deferred compensation measurement.

Natural_Language: The costs of deferred compensation awards are unallowable if the awards are made in periods subsequent to the period when the work being remunerated was performed.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_j_2: Deferred comp awards made after the work period are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Anti-retroactivity rule for deferred compensation. Award must be contemporaneous with work.

Natural_Language: Compensation incidental to business acquisitions. The following costs are unallowable: (k)(1) and (k)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_k: Parent -- acquisition-related compensation is unallowable
Validation_Notes: Parent for two categories of unallowable acquisition-related compensation.

Natural_Language: Payments to employees under agreements in which they receive special compensation, in excess of the contractor's normal severance pay practice, if their employment terminates following a change in the management control over, or ownership of, the contractor or a substantial portion of its assets.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_k_1: Golden parachute payments exceeding normal severance after ownership change are unallowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive conditions: special compensation AND exceeds normal AND follows ownership change. "Golden parachute" type payments.

Natural_Language: Payments to employees under plans introduced in connection with a change, whether actual or prospective, in the management control over, or ownership of, the contractor or a substantial portion of its assets in which those employees receive special compensation, which is contingent upon the employee remaining with the contractor for a specified period of time.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_k_2: Retention bonus plans tied to ownership changes are unallowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Retention bonus prohibition: plans introduced for ownership changes with stay-bonus contingency.

Natural_Language: Fringe benefits.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_l: Parent for fringe benefit provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent for fringe benefit provisions.

Natural_Language: Fringe benefits are in addition to regular wages and salaries and are allowances and services provided by the contractor to its employees as compensation (e.g., the cost of vacations, sick leave, holidays, military leave, employee insurance, and supplemental unemployment benefit plans).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_l_1: Definition -- fringe benefits are additional allowances/services beyond regular wages
Validation_Notes: Definitional with illustrative examples. Not exhaustive list.

Natural_Language: Except as provided in subpart 31.2, the costs of fringe benefits are allowable if they are reasonable and required by law, employer-employee agreement, or an established policy of the contractor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_l_2_a: Reasonable; P_31_205_6_l_2_b: Required by law, agreement, or established policy; P_31_205_6_l_2_c: Subject to 31.2 exceptions
Formal_Logic_Statement: Reasonable ^ (Required_By_Law v Required_By_Agreement v Established_Policy) ^ ~Excepted_By_31_2 -> Allowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional: fringe benefits allowable IF reasonable AND required by one of three sources AND not excepted by 31.2.

Natural_Language: Employee rebate and purchase discount plans. Rebates and purchase discounts provided to employees on products or services produced by the contractor or affiliates are unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_m: Employee rebate/discount plan costs are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Flat prohibition. No conditions or exceptions.

Natural_Language: Postretirement benefits (PRB) other than pensions. Covers all benefits other than cash/life insurance paid by pension plans, provided to employees/beneficiaries/dependents post-retirement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_n: Parent for PRB provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent for all PRB provisions.

Natural_Language: PRB covers all benefits, other than cash benefits and life insurance benefits paid by pension plans, provided to employees, their beneficiaries, and covered dependents during the period following the employees' retirement (e.g., postretirement health care; life insurance provided outside a pension plan; and other welfare benefits, such as tuition assistance, day care, legal services, and housing subsidies provided after retirement).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_n_1: Definition -- PRB scope excludes pension-plan cash/life insurance; includes health care, outside life insurance, other welfare benefits
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Scope defined by exclusion (not pension cash/life insurance) and inclusion (illustrative examples).

Natural_Language: To be allowable, PRB costs must be incurred pursuant to law, employer-employee agreement, or an established policy of the contractor, and must comply with the following: (i) through (iii) methods and additional requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_n_2: PRB allowable if incurred per law/agreement/policy AND complies with sub-requirements
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Law v Agreement v Established_Policy) ^ Comply_With_Subreqs -> PRB_Allowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Conditional: PRB allowable IF authorized by one of three sources AND complies with method-specific requirements.

Natural_Language: Pay-as-you-go. PRB costs are not accrued during the working lives of employees. Costs are assigned to the period in which-- (A) Benefits are actually provided; or (B) The costs are paid to an insurer, provider, or other recipient for current year benefits or premiums.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_n_2_i_A: Costs assigned when benefits provided; P_31_205_6_n_2_i_B: Costs assigned when paid to insurer/provider
Validation_Notes: PAYG method: costs assigned to period of benefit delivery or payment. Disjunctive assignment triggers.

Natural_Language: Terminal funding. PRB costs are not accrued during the working lives of the employees. (A) Terminal funding occurs when the entire PRB liability is paid in a lump sum upon the termination of employees (or upon conversion to such a terminal-funded plan) to an insurer or trustee to establish and maintain a fund or reserve for the sole purpose of providing PRB to retirees. (B) Terminal funded costs must be amortized over a period of 15 years.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_n_2_ii_A: Terminal funding = lump sum to insurer/trustee at termination; P_31_205_6_n_2_ii_B: Must amortize over 15 years
Validation_Notes: Terminal funding method: definitional plus mandatory 15-year amortization.

Natural_Language: Accrual basis. PRB costs are accrued during the working lives of employees. Accrued PRB costs must comply with measurement/assignment methods (A), funding (B), actuarial standards (C), prior period adjustments (D), unfunded liability calculation (E), prepayment credit (F), and method change rules (G).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_n_2_iii: Parent for accrual-basis PRB requirements (A through G)
Formal_Logic_Statement: Accrual_PRB -> (Comply_A ^ Comply_B ^ Comply_C ^ Comply_D ^ Comply_E ^ Comply_F ^ Comply_G)
Validation_Notes: Parent for seven accrual-basis requirements. All must be met for allowability.

Natural_Language: Generally accepted accounting principles. However, transitions from the pay-as-you-go method to the accrual accounting method must be handled in accordance with transition rules at (i), (ii), and (iii).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_n_1_v2: GAAP measurement method with PAYG-to-accrual transition rules
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(n)(2)(iii)(A)(1). GAAP method with mandatory transition handling.

Natural_Language: In the year of transition from the pay-as-you-go method to accrual accounting for purposes of Government contract cost accounting, the transition obligation must be the excess of the accumulated PRB obligation over the fair value of plan assets determined in accordance with paragraph (n)(2)(iii)(E); the fair value must be reduced by the prepayment credit as determined in accordance with paragraph (n)(2)(iii)(F).

Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(n)(2)(iii)(A)(1)(i). Transition obligation calculation formula.

Natural_Language: PRB cost attributable to the transition obligation assigned to the current year that is in excess of the amount assignable to accounting periods on the basis of a straight line amortization of the transition obligation over the average remaining working lives of active employees covered by the PRB plan or a 20-year period, whichever period is longer, is unallowable. However, if the plan is comprised of inactive participants only, the PRB cost attributable to the transition obligation assigned to the current year that is in excess of the amount assignable to accounting periods on a straight line amortization of the transition obligation over the average future life expectancy of the participants is unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_n_1_ii_a: Active plan -- excess over SL amortization (longer of avg working lives or 20yr) is unallowable; P_31_205_6_n_1_ii_b: Inactive-only plan -- excess over SL amortization over avg life expectancy is unallowable

Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(n)(2)(iii)(A)(1)(ii). Bifurcated amortization rule based on active vs. inactive plan status. Complex formula.

Natural_Language: For a plan that transitioned from pay-as-you-go to accrual accounting for Government contract cost accounting prior to July 22, 2013, the unallowable amount of PRB cost attributable to the transition obligation amortization must continue to be based on the cost principle in effect at the time of the transition until the original transition obligation schedule is fully amortized.

Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(n)(2)(iii)(A)(1)(iii). Grandfathering provision for pre-2013 transitions.

Natural_Language: Contributions to a welfare benefit fund determined in accordance with applicable Internal Revenue Code. Allowable PRB costs based on such contributions must comply with (i) through (iii).

Natural_Language: Be assigned to accounting periods on the basis of the average working lives of active employees covered by the PRB plan or a 15-year period, whichever period is longer. Natural_Language: Exclude Federal income taxes, whether incurred by the fund or the contractor (including any increase in PRB costs associated with such taxes), unless the fund holding the plan assets is tax-exempt under the provisions of 26 U.S.C. 501(c).

Natural_Language: Present an analysis demonstrating that all costs assigned to prior periods have been accounted for in accordance with paragraphs (n)(2)(iii)(D), (E), and (F) to ensure that no duplicate recovery of costs exists. Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING CORRECTED: Actual section is 31.205-6(n)(2)(iii)(G)(2). Anti-duplicate-recovery with advance agreement option. Cross-reference to 31.110.

Natural_Language: To be allowable, PRB costs must be funded by the time set for filing the Federal income tax return or any extension thereof, or paid to an insurer, provider, or other recipient by the time set for filing the Federal income tax return or extension thereof. PRB costs assigned to the current year, but not funded, paid or otherwise liquidated by the tax return due date as extended are not allowable in any subsequent year.

Natural_Language: Increased PRB costs caused by delay in funding beyond 30 days after each quarter of the year to which they are assignable are unallowable.

Natural_Language: The Government must receive an equitable share of any amount of previously funded PRB costs which revert or inure to the contractor. Validation_Notes: Equitable recovery provision for Government when PRB funds revert. Mirrors pension reversion rules.

Natural_Language: Definitions. As used in this paragraph (o)-- Compensation means total wages, salary, bonuses, deferred compensation, and employer contributions to defined contribution pension plans for the fiscal year. Natural_Language: All employee compensation limit for contracts awarded before June 24, 2014.

Validation_Notes: Broadest applicability: all executive agencies, all contracts on/after June 24 2014, including subcontracts.

Natural_Language: Exceptions. An agency head may establish one or more narrowly targeted exceptions for scientists, engineers, or other specialists upon a determination that such exceptions are needed to ensure that the executive agency has continued access to needed skills and capabilities. In making such a determination, the agency must consider, at a minimum, for each contractor employee in a narrowly targeted excepted position-- (A) The amount of taxpayer funded compensation to be received by each employee; and (B) The duties and services performed by each employee.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_o_4_iii_a: Agency head may grant exceptions; P_31_205_6_o_4_iii_b: For scientists/engineers/specialists; P_31_205_6_o_4_iii_c: Based on skills/capabilities need; P_31_205_6_o_4_iii_d: Must consider taxpayer-funded amount and duties
Formal_Logic_Statement: Agency_Head ^ Skills_Need_Determination ^ (Scientists v Engineers v Specialists) -> (Exception_Granted v ~Exception_Granted) ^ Consider(Taxpayer_Funded_Amount ^ Employee_Duties)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: "May" = discretionary (tautology). Narrowly targeted to specific specialist categories. Mandatory minimum considerations for any exception determination.

Natural_Language: Employee stock ownership plans (ESOP). Covers allowability of ESOP contributions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_p: Parent for ESOP provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent for ESOP provisions: definition, contribution forms, and allowability conditions.

Natural_Language: An ESOP is a stock bonus plan designed to invest primarily in the stock of the employer corporation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_p_1: Definition -- ESOP is a stock bonus plan investing primarily in employer stock
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Two conjunctive elements.

Natural_Language: The contractor's contributions to an Employee Stock Ownership Trust (ESOT) may be in the form of cash, stock, or property.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_p_2: ESOT contributions may be cash, stock, or property
Formal_Logic_Statement: ESOT_Contribution = Cash v Stock v Property
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: three permissible contribution forms. "May" here describes permissible forms, not discretionary authority.

Natural_Language: Costs of ESOPs are allowable subject to the following conditions: (i) through (v).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_p_3: Parent -- ESOP costs allowable subject to five conditions
Validation_Notes: Parent for five ESOP allowability conditions. All must be met.

Natural_Language: The contractor measures, assigns, and allocates costs in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.415.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_p_3_i: ESOP costs must comply with CAS 415
Validation_Notes: CAS 415 compliance mandatory for ESOP cost measurement.

Natural_Language: Contributions by the contractor in any one year that exceed the deductibility limits of the Internal Revenue Code for that year are unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_p_3_ii: ESOP contributions exceeding IRC deductibility limits are unallowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: IRC deductibility cap on ESOP contributions. Excess is unallowable.

Natural_Language: When the contribution is in the form of stock, the value of the stock contribution is limited to the fair market value of the stock on the date that title is effectively transferred to the trust.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_p_3_iii: Stock contributions valued at FMV on title transfer date
Validation_Notes: FMV valuation rule for stock contributions to ESOT. Transfer date determines valuation.

Natural_Language: When the contribution is in the form of cash-- (A) Stock purchases by the ESOT in excess of fair market value are unallowable; and (B) When stock purchases are in excess of fair market value, the contractor must credit the amount of the excess to the same indirect cost pools that were charged for the ESOP contributions in the year in which the stock purchase occurs. However, when the trust purchases the stock with borrowed funds which will be repaid over a period of years by cash contributions from the contractor to the trust, the contractor must credit the excess price over fair market value to the indirect cost pools pro rata over the period of years during which the contractor contributes the cash used by the trust to repay the loan.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_p_3_iv_A: Cash ESOT stock purchases above FMV unallowable; P_31_205_6_p_3_iv_B: Excess credited to indirect cost pools; P_31_205_6_p_3_iv_C: Borrowed fund purchases -- pro rata credit over repayment period
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Multi-part cash contribution rule. Excess over FMV unallowable with credit mechanism. Special treatment for leveraged ESOP (borrowed funds).

Natural_Language: When the fair market value of unissued stock or stock of a closely held corporation is not readily determinable, the valuation will be made on a case-by-case basis taking into consideration the guidelines for valuation used by the IRS.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_6_p_3_v: Non-readily-determinable FMV for unissued/closely-held stock -- case-by-case per IRS guidelines
Validation_Notes: Fallback valuation for non-publicly-traded stock. IRS guidelines provide framework.

Natural_Language: 31.205-7 Contingencies. Parent proposition establishing rules for contingency costs, including definition, historical costing treatment, and categorization of future cost contingencies.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating definition, historical costing rules, and future cost categorization for contingencies. All sub-provisions required for complete coverage.

Natural_Language: Contingency, as used in this subpart, means a possible future event or condition arising from presently known or unknown causes, the outcome of which is indeterminable at the present time.
Validation_Notes: Definitional provision. Three conjunctive elements define the term: future event/condition, known or unknown causation, indeterminable outcome.

Natural_Language: Parent for historical costing treatment of contingency costs.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating general unallowability rule and exception for past period contingency factors.

Natural_Language: Costs for contingencies are generally unallowable for historical costing purposes because such costing deals with costs incurred and recorded on the contractor's books.
Validation_Notes: General prohibition on contingency costs in historical costing context. 'Generally' qualifier noted but the rationale (costs must be incurred and recorded) makes this effectively a prohibition. HIGH-RISK rule 15 used for conditional structure.

Natural_Language: A contingency factor may be recognized when it is applicable to a past period to give recognition to minor unsettled factors in the interest of expediting settlement (e.g., terminations).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive/discretionary. Three conditions must be met (past period applicability, minor unsettled factors, expediting settlement) but recognition remains discretionary.

Natural_Language: In connection with estimates of future costs, contingencies fall into two categories.
Validation_Notes: Parent for two categories of future cost contingencies. Disjunctive: contingencies fall into one or the other category. HIGH-RISK rule 15 for conditional trigger.

Natural_Language: Those that may arise from presently known and existing conditions, the effects of which are foreseeable within reasonable limits of accuracy (e.g., anticipated costs of rejects and defective work). Contingencies of this category are to be included in the estimates of future costs so as to provide the best estimate of performance cost.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_7_c_1_a: Contingency arises from known/existing conditions with foreseeable effects; P_31_205_7_c_1_b: Such contingencies must be included in future cost estimates
Validation_Notes: Category 1 contingencies: foreseeable effects from known conditions. 'Are to be included' = mandatory inclusion. The purpose is best estimate of performance cost.

Natural_Language: Those that may arise from presently known or unknown conditions, the effect of which cannot be measured so precisely as to provide equitable results to the contractor and to the Government (e.g., results of pending litigation). Contingencies of this category are to be excluded from cost estimates under the several items of cost but should be disclosed separately (including the basis upon which the contingency is computed) to facilitate the negotiation of appropriate contractual coverage. (See 31.205-6(f) and 31.205-19.)
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_7_c_2_a: Contingency arises from known or unknown conditions with imprecise effects; P_31_205_7_c_2_b: Such contingencies must be excluded from cost estimates; P_31_205_7_c_2_c: Such contingencies should be disclosed separately with computation basis
Validation_Notes: Category 2 contingencies: imprecise effects. Exclusion is mandatory ('are to be excluded'), but separate disclosure is advisory ('should'). Cross-refs to 31.205-6(f) and 31.205-19. Advisory 'should' noted.

Natural_Language: Contributions or donations, including cash, property and services, regardless of recipient, are unallowable (except see 31.205-1(d)(3)).
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Contribution v Donation) ^ (Cash v Property v Services) -> ~Allowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Blanket prohibition on contributions/donations regardless of form or recipient. Single exception via 31.205-1(d)(3). 'Regardless of recipient' broadens scope significantly.

Natural_Language: [Reserved]
Validation_Notes: Reserved section. No substantive content. Logged and moved on per skeleton notes.

Natural_Language: 31.205-10 Cost of money. Parent proposition establishing that cost of money is an imputed cost allowable under specified conditions, including CAS compliance and identification in proposals.

Natural_Language: Cost of money is an imputed cost that is not a form of interest on borrowings (see 31.205-20).

Validation_Notes: Definitional: cost of money is imputed AND is NOT interest on borrowings. Cross-ref to 31.205-20 for interest rules.

Natural_Language: Cost of money is an incurred cost for cost-reimbursement purposes under applicable cost-reimbursement contracts and for progress payment purposes under fixed-price contracts.

Natural_Language: Cost of money is an incurred cost for cost-reimbursement purposes under applicable cost-reimbursement contracts.

Natural_Language: Cost of money is an incurred cost for progress payment purposes under fixed-price contracts.
Validation_Notes: Cost of money treated as incurred cost for progress payments under fixed-price contracts.

Natural_Language: Cost of money refers to facilities capital cost of money (see 48 CFR 9904.414) and cost of money as an element of the cost of capital assets under construction (see 48 CFR 9904.417).
Validation_Notes: Parent for two CAS-defined cost of money types. Both are conjunctive elements of the definition.

Natural_Language: Facilities capital cost of money (see 48 CFR 9904.414).
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference to CAS 414 for facilities capital cost of money. External dependency on 48 CFR 9904.414.

Natural_Language: Cost of money as an element of the cost of capital assets under construction (see 48 CFR 9904.417).

Natural_Language: It is measured, assigned, and allocated to contracts in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.414 or measured and added to the cost of capital assets under construction in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.417, as applicable.
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: either CAS 414 path (measure, assign, allocate) or CAS 417 path (measure and add), as applicable. External deps on CAS 414 and 417.

Natural_Language: 31.205-11 Depreciation. Natural_Language: Parent for general allowability of depreciation and residual value rules for tangible personal property.

Natural_Language: Depreciation on a contractor's plant, equipment, and other capital facilities is an allowable contract cost, subject to the limitations in this cost principle.
