Natural_Language: Parent for CAS 409 compliance requirements for depreciation.
Validation_Notes: Parent for CAS 409 mandatory compliance and continuation requirements.

Natural_Language: Contractors with contracts subject to 48 CFR 9904.409 must adhere to the requirement of that standard for all fully CAS-covered contracts and may elect to adopt the standard for all other contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_11_b_1_a: Contractors with CAS 409 contracts must adhere for fully CAS-covered contracts; P_31_205_11_b_1_b: Contractors may elect CAS 409 for all other contracts
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Two-part rule: mandatory adherence for fully CAS-covered, permissive election for others. 'May elect' = discretionary per tautology treatment.

Natural_Language: All requirements of 48 CFR 9904.409 are applicable if the election in paragraph (b)(1) of this section is made, and contractors must continue to follow it until notification of final acceptance of all deliverable items under negotiated Government contracts.
Validation_Notes: If election is made under (b)(1), all CAS 409 requirements apply AND contractor must continue until final acceptance. Lock-in provision.

Natural_Language: For contracts that are not subject to 48 CFR 9904.409, allowable depreciation must not exceed the amount used for financial accounting purposes and must be determined in a manner consistent with the depreciation policies and procedures followed in the same segment on non-Government business (except see paragraphs (g) and (h) of this section).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_11_c_a: Allowable depreciation must not exceed financial accounting amount; P_31_205_11_c_b: Depreciation must be consistent with non-Government business policies in same segment
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: For non-CAS-409 contracts: two conjunctive constraints. Must not exceed financial accounting amounts AND must be consistent with same-segment non-Govt policies. Exceptions in (g) and (h).

Natural_Language: Depreciation, rental, or use charges are unallowable on property acquired from the Government at no cost to the contractor or any division, subsidiary, or affiliate of the contractor under common control.
Formal_Logic_Statement: GovtPropertyAtNoCost(Contractor v Division v Subsidiary v Affiliate_CommonControl) -> ~Allowable(Depreciation v Rental v UseCharges)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on depreciation/rental/use charges for no-cost government property. Scope extends to affiliates under common control.

Natural_Language: The depreciation on an item that meets the criteria for allowance at price under 31.205-26(f) may be based on that price, provided the same policies and procedures are used for costing all business of the using division, subsidiary, or organization under common control.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive. Two conditions (meets 31.205-26(f) criteria AND consistent policies) enable but do not mandate price-based depreciation. Cross-ref to 31.205-26(f).

Natural_Language: Parent for rules on fully depreciated property.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating prohibition, agreed charge exception, and charge determination factors for fully depreciated property.

Natural_Language: No depreciation or rental is allowed on property that is fully depreciated by the contractor or by any division, subsidiary, or affiliate of the contractor under common control.
Formal_Logic_Statement: FullyDepreciated(Contractor v Division v Subsidiary v Affiliate_CommonControl) -> ~Allowable(Depreciation v Rental)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on depreciation/rental for fully depreciated property. Common control scope prevents circumvention through related entities.

Natural_Language: A reasonable charge for using fully depreciated property may be agreed upon and allowed (except see 31.110(b)(2)).
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive. A use charge is possible by agreement but not mandated. Exception in 31.110(b)(2). Charge must be 'reasonable.'

Natural_Language: In determining the charge, consideration must be given to cost, total estimated useful life at the time of negotiations, effect of any increased maintenance charges or decreased efficiency due to age, and the amount of depreciation previously charged to Government contracts or subcontracts.
Validation_Notes: Four mandatory consideration factors when determining the use charge. 'Must' = mandatory. All four are conjunctive requirements.

Natural_Language: Whether or not the contract is subject to CAS, the following apply.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Universal applicability regardless of CAS status. The tautological antecedent (CAS or not CAS) means these apply to ALL contracts. Three conjunctive sub-provisions.

Natural_Language: The requirements of 31.205-52.
Validation_Notes: Simple cross-reference requiring compliance with 31.205-52 (asset valuation).

Natural_Language: In the event of a write-down from carrying value to fair value as a result of impairments caused by events or changes in circumstances, allowable depreciation of the impaired assets is limited to the amounts that would have been allowed had the assets not been written down (see 31.205-16(g)). However, this does not preclude a change in depreciation resulting from other causes such as permissible changes in estimates of service life, consumption of services, or residual value.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_11_g_2_a: Impairment write-down limits depreciation to pre-write-down amounts; P_31_205_11_g_2_b: Changes from other causes (service life, consumption, residual value) are not precluded
Validation_Notes: Two-part rule: (1) impairment write-downs do not increase allowable depreciation beyond what would have been allowed without write-down; (2) carve-out for other legitimate depreciation changes. Cross-ref to 31.205-16(g).

Natural_Language: Parent for reacquired property rules in sale-leaseback context.
Validation_Notes: Parent for reacquisition depreciation basis rule and definition of reacquired property.

Natural_Language: In the event the contractor reacquires property involved in a sale and leaseback arrangement, allowable depreciation of reacquired property must be based on the net book value of the asset as of the date the contractor originally became a lessee of the property in the sale and leaseback arrangement, adjusted for any allowable gain or loss determined in accordance with 31.205-16(b), and less any amount of depreciation expense included in the calculation of the amount that would have been allowed had the contractor retained title under 31.205-11(h)(1) and 31.205-36(b)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_11_g_3_i_a: Depreciation based on net book value at original lessee date; P_31_205_11_g_3_i_b: Adjusted for allowable gain/loss per 31.205-16(b); P_31_205_11_g_3_i_c: Less depreciation included in retained-title calculation per 31.205-11(h)(1) and 31.205-36(b)(2)
Validation_Notes: Complex depreciation basis calculation for reacquired sale-leaseback property. Three conjunctive adjustments to net book value. Multiple cross-references: 31.205-16(b), 31.205-11(h)(1), 31.205-36(b)(2).

Natural_Language: As used in this paragraph (g)(3), reacquired property is property that generated either any depreciation expense or any cost of money considered in the calculation of the limitations under 31.205-11(h)(1) and 31.205-36(b)(2) during the most recent accounting period prior to the date of reacquisition.
Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Definitional provision using biconditional. Property qualifies as 'reacquired' if and only if it generated depreciation or cost of money in the limitation calculations during the most recent accounting period before reacquisition. Cross-refs to 31.205-11(h)(1) and 31.205-36(b)(2).

Natural_Language: A finance lease, as defined in Financial Accounting Standards Board's Accounting Standards Codification (FASB ASC) 842, Leases, is subject to the requirements of this cost principle. (See 31.205-36 for Operating Leases.)
Validation_Notes: Finance leases per FASB ASC 842 are subject to depreciation cost principle. Cross-ref to 31.205-36 for operating leases. Parent for sale-leaseback and related-party limitations.

Natural_Language: Lease costs under a sale and leaseback arrangement are allowable only up to the amount that would be allowed if the contractor retained title, computed based on the net book value of the asset on the date the contractor becomes a lessee of the property adjusted for any gain or loss recognized in accordance with 31.205-16(b).
Validation_Notes: Sale-leaseback cost cap: allowable costs limited to what would have been allowed had contractor kept title. Computed from net book value at lessee date, adjusted per 31.205-16(b). 'Only' emphasizes this is a ceiling.

Natural_Language: If it is determined that the terms of the finance lease have been significantly affected by the fact that the lessee and lessor are related, depreciation charges are not allowable in excess of those that would have occurred if the lease contained terms consistent with those found in a lease between unrelated parties.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Related-party limitation: if lease terms are influenced by related-party status, depreciation capped at arm's length equivalent. Three conjunctive conditions trigger the limitation.

Natural_Language: 31.205-12 Economic planning costs. Parent proposition establishing definition, exclusions, and allowability of economic planning costs.
Validation_Notes: Parent for three sub-provisions: definition, exclusion scope, and allowability determination.

Natural_Language: Economic planning costs are the costs of general long-range management planning that is concerned with the future overall development of the contractor's business and that may take into account the eventual possibility of economic dislocations or fundamental alterations in those markets in which the contractor currently does business.
Validation_Notes: Definitional provision. Core elements are conjunctive (general long-range, future development). Consideration of dislocations/alterations is permissive ('may').

Natural_Language: Economic planning costs do not include organization or reorganization costs covered by 31.205-27. (See 31.205-38 for market planning costs other than economic planning costs.)
Validation_Notes: Exclusion scope: organization/reorganization costs are carved out to 31.205-27. Market planning costs carved out to 31.205-38.

Natural_Language: Economic planning costs are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Simple declarative allowability statement. No conditions or limitations beyond definition in (a) and exclusions in (b).

Natural_Language: 31.205-13 Employee morale, health, welfare, food service, and dormitory costs and credits. Parent proposition establishing allowability of employee morale/welfare costs with limitations on gifts, recreation, food/dormitory losses, and employee associations.
Validation_Notes: Parent for six sub-provisions covering allowability, gifts, recreation, food/dormitory losses, employee associations, and contributions.

Natural_Language: Aggregate costs incurred on activities designed to improve working conditions, employer-employee relations, employee morale, and employee performance (less income generated by these activities) are allowable, subject to the limitations in this section. Examples of allowable activities include house publications, health clinics, wellness/fitness centers, employee counseling services, and food and dormitory services.
Validation_Notes: General allowability for morale/welfare activities, net of income. Subject to section limitations. Parent for example list in (1)-(5).

Natural_Language: House publications are an example of allowable employee morale, health, welfare activities.
Validation_Notes: Enumerated example of allowable activity. Not exhaustive.

Natural_Language: Health clinics are an example of allowable employee morale, health, welfare activities.
Validation_Notes: Enumerated example of allowable activity.

Natural_Language: Wellness/fitness centers are an example of allowable employee morale, health, welfare activities.
Validation_Notes: Enumerated example of allowable activity.

Natural_Language: Employee counseling services are an example of allowable employee morale, health, welfare activities.
Validation_Notes: Enumerated example of allowable activity.

Natural_Language: Food and dormitory services for the contractor's employees at or near the contractor's facilities, including operating or furnishing facilities for cafeterias, dining rooms, canteens, lunch wagons, vending machines, living accommodations, and similar types of services.
Validation_Notes: Enumerated example with sub-examples. Parent for types of food/dormitory services.

Natural_Language: Operating or furnishing facilities for cafeterias, dining rooms, canteens, lunch wagons, vending machines, living accommodations.
Formal_Logic_Statement: OperateOrFurnish(Cafeterias ^ DiningRooms ^ Canteens ^ LunchWagons ^ VendingMachines ^ LivingAccommodations)
Validation_Notes: Non-exhaustive list of food/dormitory facility types. Conjunctive enumeration of examples.

Natural_Language: Similar types of services.
Validation_Notes: Catch-all for services similar to those enumerated in (i). Extends scope beyond the explicit list.

Natural_Language: Parent for gift cost rules including prohibition and exception for performance/achievement awards.
Validation_Notes: Parent for gift prohibition and award exception.

Natural_Language: Costs of gifts are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Blanket prohibition on gift costs. Simple negation.

Natural_Language: Gifts do not include awards for performance made pursuant to 31.205-6(e) or awards made in recognition of employee achievements pursuant to an established contractor plan or policy.
Validation_Notes: Definitional carve-out: performance awards per 31.205-6(e) and achievement awards per established plans are NOT gifts. Disjunctive exclusion.

Natural_Language: Costs of recreation are unallowable, except for the costs of employees' participation in company sponsored sports teams or employee organizations designed to improve company loyalty, teamwork, or physical fitness.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_13_c_a: Recreation costs are unallowable; P_31_205_13_c_b: Exception for company-sponsored sports teams/employee organizations improving loyalty, teamwork, or fitness
Justification_Rules: Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: General prohibition with specific exception. Exception requires company sponsorship AND purpose of improving loyalty, teamwork, or fitness.

Natural_Language: Parent for food and dormitory loss allowability rules.
Validation_Notes: Parent for loss allowability criteria and indirect expense allocation requirement.

Natural_Language: The allowability of food and dormitory losses are determined by the following criteria.
Validation_Notes: Parent for three criteria governing food/dormitory loss allowability.

Natural_Language: Losses from operating food and dormitory services are allowable only if the contractor's objective is to operate such services on a break-even basis.
Validation_Notes: Only if' creates biconditional: losses allowable if and only if break-even objective. Contractor intent is the controlling factor.

Natural_Language: Losses sustained because food services or lodging accommodations are furnished without charge or at prices or rates that would not be conducive to the accomplishment of the objective in paragraph (d)(1)(i) of this section are not allowable, except as described in paragraph (d)(1)(iii) of this section.
Validation_Notes: Losses from underpriced or free services are unallowable. Exception in (iii) for unusual circumstances. Links to break-even objective in (i).

Natural_Language: A loss may be allowed if the contractor can demonstrate that unusual circumstances exist such that even with efficient management, operating the services on a break-even basis would require charging inordinately high prices, or prices or rates higher than those charged by commercial establishments offering the same services in the same geographical areas. Examples include: (A) remote locations without adequate commercial facilities; (B) excessive unproductive labor costs if services unavailable; (C) termination/reduction would not yield net cost savings.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive. Contractor must demonstrate unusual circumstances AND efficient management AND pricing impracticality. Three examples provided (remote location, labor costs, no net savings) but list is illustrative. Sub-items (A)-(C) handled via atomic decomposition within this proposition.

Natural_Language: Costs of food and dormitory services must include an allocable share of indirect expenses pertaining to these activities.
Validation_Notes: Mandatory inclusion of allocable indirect expenses in food/dormitory cost calculations. 'Must' = mandatory.

Natural_Language: When the contractor has an arrangement authorizing an employee association to provide or operate a service, such as vending machines in the contractor's plant, and retain the profits, such profits must be treated in the same manner as if the contractor were providing the service (except see paragraph (f) of this section).
Validation_Notes: Employee association profits treated as if contractor-provided. Prevents profit diversion through employee associations. Exception in (f).

Natural_Language: Contributions by the contractor to an employee organization, including funds from vending machine receipts or similar sources, are allowable only to the extent that the contractor demonstrates that an equivalent amount of the costs incurred by the employee organization would be allowable if directly incurred by the contractor.
Validation_Notes: Only to the extent' creates a proportional limitation. Allowability of contributions mirrors what would be allowable if contractor incurred directly. Burden of demonstration on contractor.

Natural_Language: 31.205-14 Entertainment costs. Parent proposition establishing that entertainment costs, club memberships, and associated costs are unallowable, with no cross-principle escape.
Validation_Notes: Parent for three sub-provisions: entertainment costs, membership costs, and anti-circumvention clause.

Natural_Language: Costs of amusement, diversions, social activities, and any directly associated costs, such as tickets to shows or sporting events, meals, lodging, rentals, transportation, and gratuities are unallowable.
Formal_Logic_Statement: ~Allowable(Amusement ^ Diversions ^ SocialActivities ^ AssociatedCosts(Tickets ^ Meals ^ Lodging ^ Rentals ^ Transportation ^ Gratuities))
Validation_Notes: Broad prohibition on entertainment and all directly associated costs. List is illustrative ('such as') but comprehensive.

Natural_Language: Costs of membership in social, dining, country clubs, or other organizations having the same purposes are also unallowable, regardless of whether the cost is reported as taxable income to the employees.
Formal_Logic_Statement: ~Allowable(ClubMemberships(Social v Dining v Country v SimilarPurpose)) ^ RegardlessOfTaxableIncomeReporting
Validation_Notes: Club membership prohibition. 'Regardless of taxable income reporting' closes a potential loophole where costs might be recharacterized as compensation.

Natural_Language: Costs made specifically unallowable under this cost principle are not allowable under any other cost principle.
Validation_Notes: Anti-circumvention clause. Prevents reclassifying entertainment costs under a different cost principle to achieve allowability. Strong lockout provision.

Natural_Language: 31.205-15 Fines, penalties, and mischarging costs. Parent proposition establishing unallowability of fines/penalties from legal violations and mischarging costs.
Validation_Notes: Parent for two sub-provisions: fines/penalties and mischarging costs.

Natural_Language: Costs of fines and penalties resulting from violations of, or failure of the contractor to comply with, Federal, State, local, or foreign laws and regulations, are unallowable except when incurred as a result of compliance with specific terms and conditions of the contract or written instructions from the contracting officer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_15_a_a: Fines/penalties from legal violations are unallowable; P_31_205_15_a_b: Exception when incurred from compliance with contract terms or CO written instructions
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: General prohibition with narrow exception. Fines from law violations are unallowable UNLESS they result from following contract terms or CO instructions. Exception protects contractors acting under government direction.

Natural_Language: Costs incurred in connection with, or related to, the mischarging of costs on Government contracts are unallowable when the costs are caused by, or result from, alteration or destruction of records, or other false or improper charging or recording of costs. Such costs include those incurred to measure or otherwise determine the magnitude of the improper charging, and costs incurred to remedy or correct the mischarging, such as costs to rescreen and reconstruct records.
Formal_Logic_Statement: (MischargingCosts ^ (AlteredRecords v DestroyedRecords v FalseCharging v ImproperRecording)) -> ~Allowable(AllRelatedCosts_Including_Measurement ^ Remediation)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Prohibition encompasses both the mischarging itself AND all costs to investigate and correct it. Broad scope: includes measurement, rescreening, reconstruction costs.

Natural_Language: 31.205-16 Gains and losses on disposition or impairment of depreciable property or other capital assets. Parent proposition establishing treatment of gains/losses from property disposition including sale-leaseback, tangible capital assets, involuntary conversions, depreciation reserve processing, and non-depreciable capital assets.
Validation_Notes: Parent for 8 sub-provisions covering all gain/loss treatment scenarios.

Natural_Language: Parent for general gain/loss inclusion rules and business combination exception.
Validation_Notes: Parent for general timing rule and business combination carve-out.

Natural_Language: Gains and losses from the sale, retirement, or other disposition (except see 31.205-19) of depreciable property must be included in the year in which they occur as credits or charges to the cost grouping(s) in which the depreciation or amortization applicable to those assets was included (except see paragraph (e) of this section).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Timing rule: gains/losses included in year of occurrence. Cost grouping rule: match to where depreciation/amortization was charged. Exceptions for insurance (31.205-19) and involuntary conversions (e).

Natural_Language: No gain or loss must be recognized as a result of the transfer of assets in a business combination (see 31.205-52).
Validation_Notes: Business combination carve-out: no gain/loss recognition on asset transfers. Cross-ref to 31.205-52.

Natural_Language: Notwithstanding paragraph (c) of this section, when costs of depreciable property are subject to the sale and leaseback limitations in 31.205-11(h)(1) or 31.205-36(b)(2), the gain or loss rules in (b)(1) and (b)(2) apply.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Sale-leaseback override of paragraph (c). 'Notwithstanding' establishes priority. Cross-refs to 31.205-11(h)(1) and 31.205-36(b)(2).

Natural_Language: The gain or loss is the difference between the net amount realized and the undepreciated balance of the asset on the date the contractor becomes a lessee.
Validation_Notes: Definitional: gain/loss computation for sale-leaseback. Simple arithmetic formula.

Natural_Language: When the application of paragraph (b)(1) of this section results in a loss, the rules in (b)(2)(i) and (b)(2)(ii) apply.
Validation_Notes: Parent for loss treatment rules when (b)(1) computation yields a loss. Disjunctive: one of two scenarios applies depending on FMV vs. undepreciated balance.

Natural_Language: The allowable portion of the loss is zero if the fair market value exceeds the undepreciated balance of the asset on the date the contractor becomes a lessee.
Validation_Notes: When FMV exceeds undepreciated balance, the sale-leaseback loss is entirely unallowable. Prevents gaming through below-market sale prices when asset has appreciated.

Natural_Language: The allowable portion of the loss is limited to the difference between the fair market value and the undepreciated balance of the asset on the date the contractor becomes a lessee if the fair market value is less than the undepreciated balance of the asset on the date the contractor becomes a lessee.
Validation_Notes: When FMV is below undepreciated balance, allowable loss is limited to that difference. Recognizes genuine economic loss while preventing inflated claims.

Natural_Language: Parent for tangible capital asset disposition treatment.
Validation_Notes: Parent for depreciation adjustment characterization and gain/loss computation.

Natural_Language: Gains and losses on disposition of tangible capital assets, including those acquired under capital leases (also known as a finance lease) (see 31.205-11(h)), must be considered as adjustments of depreciation costs previously recognized.
Validation_Notes: Characterization rule: gains/losses are depreciation adjustments, not independent income/expense items. Includes finance lease assets per 31.205-11(h).

Natural_Language: The gain or loss for each asset disposed of is the difference between the net amount realized, including insurance proceeds from involuntary conversions, and its undepreciated balance.
Validation_Notes: Computation formula for gain/loss per asset. Insurance proceeds explicitly included in net amount realized.

Natural_Language: The gain recognized for contract costing purposes must be limited to the difference between the acquisition cost (or for assets acquired under a finance lease, the value at which the leased asset is capitalized) of the asset and its undepreciated balance, except see paragraph (e) of this section.
Validation_Notes: Gain cap: recognized gain cannot exceed the spread between acquisition cost (or capitalized value for finance leases) and undepreciated balance. Prevents windfall gains from market appreciation being charged to contracts. Exception in (e).

Natural_Language: Special considerations apply to an involuntary conversion when a contractor's property is destroyed by events that are out of the owner's control, such as fire, windstorm, flood, accident, theft, etc., and an insurance award is recovered.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Parent for involuntary conversion rules. Two scenarios based on whether asset is replaced. Events are illustrative ('such as').

Natural_Language: When there is an insurance award and the converted asset is not replaced, gain or loss must be recognized in the period of disposition. The gain recognized for contract costing purposes must be limited to the difference between the acquisition cost of the asset and its undepreciated balance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_16_e_1_a: Gain/loss recognized in period of disposition; P_31_205_16_e_1_b: Gain limited to acquisition cost minus undepreciated balance
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Non-replacement scenario: immediate recognition with gain cap. Two conjunctive requirements: timing and gain limitation.

Natural_Language: When the converted asset is replaced, the contractor must either adjust the depreciable basis of the new asset or recognize the gain/loss in the period of disposition with Government participation.
Validation_Notes: Replacement scenario: contractor must choose one of two approaches. Disjunctive choice but one must be selected ('must either').

Natural_Language: Adjust the depreciable basis of the new asset by the amount of the total realized gain or loss.
Validation_Notes: Option 1: fold gain/loss into new asset's depreciable basis. Defers recognition over the life of the replacement asset.

Natural_Language: Recognize the gain or loss in the period of disposition, in which case the Government must participate to the same extent as outlined in paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
Validation_Notes: Option 2: immediate recognition with mandatory Government participation per (f)(1). Cross-ref creates dependency.

Natural_Language: Gains and losses on the disposition of depreciable property must not be recognized as a separate charge or credit when conditions in (f)(1) or (f)(2) are met.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Parent for two conditions preventing separate gain/loss recognition. Disjunctive: either condition triggers the prohibition.

Natural_Language: Gains and losses are processed through the depreciation reserve account and reflected in the depreciation allowable under 31.205-11.
Validation_Notes: Condition 1: gain/loss absorbed through depreciation reserve mechanism. Cross-ref to 31.205-11.

Natural_Language: The property is exchanged as part of the purchase price of a similar item, and the gain or loss is taken into consideration in the depreciation cost basis of the new item.
Validation_Notes: Condition 2: like-kind exchange where gain/loss is folded into new item's basis.

Natural_Language: Gains and losses arising from mass or extraordinary sales, retirements, or other disposition other than through business combinations must be considered on a case-by-case basis.
Formal_Logic_Statement: (MassSales v ExtraordinarySales v MassRetirements v OtherExtraordinaryDisposition) ^ ~BusinessCombination -> CaseByCase
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Mass/extraordinary dispositions require individual evaluation. No formulaic treatment. Excludes business combinations.

Natural_Language: Gains and losses of any nature arising from the sale or exchange of capital assets other than depreciable property must be excluded in computing contract costs.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Exclusion rule for non-depreciable capital asset gains/losses. Parent for impairment and written-down asset sub-rules.

Natural_Language: With respect to long-lived tangible and identifiable intangible assets held for use, no loss must be allowed for a write-down from carrying value to fair value as a result of impairments caused by events or changes in circumstances (e.g., environmental damage, idle facilities arising from a declining business base, etc.).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on impairment write-down losses for assets held for use. Government does not share in impairment losses. Examples illustrative.

Natural_Language: If depreciable property or other capital assets have been written down from carrying value to fair value due to impairments, gains or losses upon disposition must be the amounts that would have been allowed had the assets not been written down.
Validation_Notes: Disposition after impairment: gain/loss computed as if write-down never occurred. Prevents double-counting of impairment losses and preserving government's share of gains.

Natural_Language: 31.205-17 Idle facilities and idle capacity costs. Parent proposition establishing definitions, allowability rules for idle facilities and idle capacity, and separate agreement requirements.
Validation_Notes: Parent for definitions, idle facilities rules, idle capacity rules, and separate agreement provision.

Natural_Language: Definitions. As used in this section: Costs of idle facilities or idle capacity means costs such as maintenance, repair, housing, rent, and other related costs (e.g., property taxes, insurance, and depreciation). Facilities means plant or any portion thereof (including land integral to the operation), equipment, individually or collectively, or any other tangible capital asset, wherever located, and whether owned or leased by the contractor. Idle capacity means the unused capacity of partially used facilities, the difference between 100% one-shift capacity (less normal delays) and actual usage; a multiple-shift basis may be used if shown to be normally expected. Idle facilities means completely unused facilities that are excess to the contractor's current needs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_17_a_def_1: Costs of idle facilities/capacity defined; P_31_205_17_a_def_2: Facilities defined; P_31_205_17_a_def_3: Idle capacity defined; P_31_205_17_a_def_4: Idle facilities defined
Formal_Logic_Statement: CostsOfIdleFacilitiesOrCapacity = (Maintenance ^ Repair ^ Housing ^ Rent ^ RelatedCosts); Facilities = (Plant v Equipment v TangibleCapitalAsset) ^ (OwnedOrLeased); IdleCapacity = UnusedCapacity(PartiallyUsedFacilities) ^ (100%OneShift - NormalDelays - ActualUsage); IdleFacilities = CompletelyUnused ^ ExcessToCurrentNeeds
Validation_Notes: Four definitions. Costs definition is illustrative ('such as'). Facilities definition is broad (owned or leased, wherever located). Idle capacity uses one-shift default with multi-shift option. Idle facilities = completely unused.

Natural_Language: The costs of idle facilities are unallowable unless the facilities meet conditions in (b)(1) or (b)(2).
Formal_Logic_Statement: IdleFacilityCosts -> (~Allowable ^ ~(P_31_205_17_b_1 v P_31_205_17_b_2)); (P_31_205_17_b_1 v P_31_205_17_b_2) -> Allowable(IdleFacilityCosts)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Default prohibition with two disjunctive exceptions. 'Unless' triggers conditional with negation.

Natural_Language: Idle facilities are necessary to meet fluctuations in workload.
Validation_Notes: Exception 1: workload fluctuation necessity. 'Necessary' requires demonstration of genuine need.

Natural_Language: Were necessary when acquired and are now idle because of changes in requirements, production economies, reorganization, termination, or other causes that could not have been reasonably foreseen. (Costs of idle facilities are allowable for a reasonable period, ordinarily not to exceed one year, depending upon the initiative taken to use, lease, or dispose of the idle facilities (except see 31.205-42)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_17_b_2_a: Facilities were necessary when acquired; P_31_205_17_b_2_b: Now idle due to unforeseeable causes; P_31_205_17_b_2_c: Allowable for reasonable period, ordinarily not exceeding one year; P_31_205_17_b_2_d: Depends on initiative to use, lease, or dispose
Validation_Notes: Exception 2: facilities necessary at acquisition but now idle from unforeseeable changes. Time-limited (ordinarily one year) with mitigation requirement. Cross-ref to 31.205-42. 'Ordinarily' allows flexibility but establishes presumptive cap.

Natural_Language: Costs of idle capacity are costs of doing business and are a factor in the normal fluctuations of usage or overhead rates from period to period. Such costs are allowable when the capacity is necessary or was originally reasonable and is not subject to reduction or elimination by subletting, renting, or sale, in accordance with sound business, economics, or security practices. Widespread idle capacity throughout an entire plant or among a group of assets having substantially the same function may be idle facilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_17_c_a: Idle capacity costs are normal business costs; P_31_205_17_c_b: Allowable when necessary or originally reasonable and not reducible; P_31_205_17_c_c: Widespread idle capacity may be reclassified as idle facilities
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: More permissive than idle facilities. Two conditions: (1) necessary/originally reasonable AND (2) not reducible. Reclassification warning: widespread idle capacity can become idle facilities (subject to stricter rules).

Natural_Language: Any costs to be paid directly by the Government for idle facilities, or idle capacity reserved for defense mobilization production must be the subject of a separate agreement (see 31.110(b)(9)).
Validation_Notes: Separate agreement requirement for direct government payment or defense mobilization reserve. Cross-ref to 31.110(b)(9).

Natural_Language: 31.205-18 Independent research and development and bid and proposal costs. Parent proposition establishing definitions, CAS 420 composition/allocation requirements, allowability, deferred IR&D cost treatment, and cooperative arrangement rules.
Validation_Notes: Parent for five sub-provisions. Largest section in this segment with VERIFY_NESTING entries requiring resolution.

Natural_Language: Definitions. As used in this section: Applied research, Bid and proposal (B&P) costs, Company, Development, Independent research and development (IR&D), and Systems and other concept formulation studies are defined.
Formal_Logic_Statement: AppliedResearch_Def ^ BPCosts_Def ^ Company_Def ^ Development_Def ^ IRD_Def ^ SystemsConceptFormulation_Def
Validation_Notes: Parent for all definitions in this section. Multiple nested numbered lists create the VERIFY_NESTING entries. Six distinct terms defined.

Natural_Language: Applied research means effort that normally follows basic research, but may not be severable from the related basic research.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: First element of applied research definition. 'May not be severable' = permissive acknowledgment of potential inseverability.

Natural_Language: Applied research attempts to determine and exploit the potential of scientific discoveries or improvements in technology, materials, processes, methods, devices, or techniques.
Validation_Notes: Second element of applied research definition. Broad scope of exploitable discoveries/improvements.

Natural_Language: Applied research attempts to advance the state of the art. Applied research does not include efforts whose principal aim is design, development, or test of specific items or services to be considered for sale; these efforts are within the definition of the term development, defined in this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_18_a_3_a: Applied research advances state of the art; P_31_205_18_a_3_b: Does not include design/development/test of specific items for sale (those are 'development')
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Third element with boundary definition: excludes specific-item design/dev/test efforts, which fall under 'development.'

Natural_Language: [VERIFY_NESTING resolved] Development excludes subcontracted technical effort that is for the sole purpose of developing an additional source for an existing product. Actual nesting: This is item (1) under the Development definition's exclusion list, not a sub-paragraph of applied research.
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING resolved: This numbered item belongs to the Development definition's exclusion clause, not under applied research. Exclusion for sole-source development subcontracts.

Natural_Language: [VERIFY_NESTING resolved] Development excludes development effort for manufacturing or production materials, systems, processes, methods, equipment, tools, and techniques not intended for sale. Actual nesting: This is item (2) under the Development definition's exclusion list.
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING resolved: Second exclusion from Development definition. Manufacturing/production development not for sale is carved out.

Natural_Language: [VERIFY_NESTING resolved] IR&D consists of projects falling within basic research. Actual nesting: This is item (1) under the IR&D definition's four areas.
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING resolved: First IR&D project area. Simple enumeration.

Natural_Language: [VERIFY_NESTING resolved] IR&D consists of projects falling within applied research. Actual nesting: This is item (2) under the IR&D definition's four areas.
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING resolved: Second IR&D project area.

Natural_Language: [VERIFY_NESTING resolved] IR&D consists of projects falling within development. Actual nesting: This is item (3) under the IR&D definition's four areas.
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING resolved: Third IR&D project area.

Natural_Language: Systems and other concept formulation studies. The term does not include the costs of effort sponsored by a grant or required in the performance of a contract. IR&D effort must not include technical effort expended in developing and preparing technical data specifically to support submitting a bid or proposal.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_18_a_4_a: Fourth IR&D area is systems/concept formulation studies; P_31_205_18_a_4_b: IR&D excludes grant-sponsored or contract-required effort; P_31_205_18_a_4_c: IR&D must not include technical effort for bid/proposal data
Formal_Logic_Statement: IRD_Area -> SystemsConceptFormulation; IRD -> ~Include(GrantSponsored v ContractRequired); IRD -> ~Include(TechnicalEffort_ForBidProposal)
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]
Validation_Notes: Fourth IR&D area plus two exclusions. Key boundary: bid/proposal technical data prep is B&P, not IR&D.

Natural_Language: Composition and allocation of costs. The requirements of 48 CFR 9904.420 are incorporated in their entirety and must apply as follows.
Validation_Notes: CAS 420 incorporated in entirety. Parent for fully-CAS and modified/non-CAS application rules.

Natural_Language: Fully-CAS-covered contracts. Contracts that are fully-CAS-covered must be subject to all requirements of 48 CFR 9904.420.
Validation_Notes: Full CAS 420 applicability for fully covered contracts. No exceptions.

Natural_Language: Modified CAS-covered and non-CAS-covered contracts. Parent for differentiated CAS 420 application rules.
Validation_Notes: Parent for three sub-provisions covering modified CAS and non-CAS contract treatment.

Natural_Language: Non-CAS-covered contracts or contracts that contain terms or conditions requiring modified CAS coverage must be subject to all requirements of 48 CFR 9904.420 except 48 CFR 9904.420-50(e)(2) and 48 CFR 9904.420-50(f)(2).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Modified application: most of CAS 420 applies except two specific provisions (50(e)(2) and 50(f)(2)).

Natural_Language: Non-CAS-covered contracts or modified CAS-covered contracts awarded when the contractor has CAS-covered contracts requiring compliance with 48 CFR 9904.420, must be subject to all the requirements of 48 CFR 9904.420.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Override provision: if contractor has ANY CAS-covered contracts requiring CAS 420, then ALL contracts (including non-CAS) must comply with full CAS 420. No exceptions.

Natural_Language: When the requirements of 48 CFR 9904.420-50(e)(2) and 48 CFR 9904.420-50(f)(2) are not applicable, the following allocation rules in (A) and (B) apply.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Conditional trigger for alternative allocation rules when CAS 420-50(e)(2) and (f)(2) don't apply. Parent for (A) and (B) sub-provisions.

Natural_Language: [VERIFY_NESTING resolved] IR&D and B&P costs must be allocated to final cost objectives on the same basis of allocation used for the general and administrative (G&A) expense grouping of the profit center (see 31.002) in which the costs are incurred. When IR&D and B&P costs clearly benefit other profit centers or benefit the entire company, those costs must be allocated through the G&A of the other profit centers or through the corporate G&A, as appropriate. Actual nesting: This is sub-paragraph (A) with items (1) and (2) under 31.205-18(b)(2)(iii).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_18_b_1_v2_a: Allocate IR&D/B&P on same basis as G&A of profit center; P_31_205_18_b_1_v2_b: When benefiting other centers or company, allocate through appropriate G&A
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING resolved: Sub-paragraph (A) under (b)(2)(iii). Two allocation rules: (1) default to profit center G&A basis, (2) cross-benefit allocation through appropriate G&A. Cross-ref to 31.002 for profit center definition.

Natural_Language: [VERIFY_NESTING resolved] If allocations of IR&D or B&P through the G&A base do not provide equitable cost allocation, the contracting officer may approve use of a different base. Actual nesting: This is sub-paragraph (B) under 31.205-18(b)(2)(iii).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: VERIFY_NESTING resolved: Sub-paragraph (B) under (b)(2)(iii). 'May' = CO discretion. Only triggered when G&A-based allocation is inequitable.

Natural_Language: Allowability. Except as provided in paragraphs (d) and (e) of this section, costs for IR&D and B&P are allowable as indirect expenses on contracts if those costs are allocable and reasonable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: General allowability rule for IR&D and B&P as indirect costs. Two conditions: allocable and reasonable. Subject to exceptions in (d) deferred costs and (e) cooperative arrangements.

Natural_Language: Deferred IR&D costs. Parent for prior-period IR&D cost rules and documentation requirements.
Validation_Notes: Parent for deferred cost conditions and contract documentation requirements.

Natural_Language: IR&D costs incurred in previous accounting periods are unallowable, except when a contractor has developed a specific product at its own risk in anticipation of recovering the development costs in the sale price of the product and all four conditions in (d)(1)(i) through (d)(1)(iv) are met.
Formal_Logic_Statement: PriorPeriodIRD -> ~Allowable; (SpecificProduct_AtOwnRisk ^ AnticipateRecovery ^ P_31_205_18_d_1_i ^ P_31_205_18_d_1_ii ^ P_31_205_18_d_1_iii ^ P_31_205_18_d_1_iv) -> Allowable(DeferredIRD)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Default prohibition on prior-period IR&D with narrow exception requiring specific product development at own risk plus four conjunctive conditions.

Natural_Language: The total amount of IR&D costs applicable to the product can be identified.
Validation_Notes: First condition for deferred IR&D: cost identifiability. Must be able to quantify total product-specific IR&D.

Natural_Language: The proration of such costs to sales of the product is reasonable.
Validation_Notes: Second condition: reasonable proration to product sales.

Natural_Language: The contractor had no Government business during the time that the costs were incurred or did not allocate IR&D costs to Government contracts except to prorate the cost of developing a specific product to the sales of that product.
Justification_Rules: Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Third condition: disjunctive. Either no govt business during cost period, or IR&D only allocated as specific product proration.

Natural_Language: No costs of current IR&D programs are allocated to Government work except to prorate the costs of developing a specific product to the sales of that product.
Validation_Notes: Fourth condition: current IR&D not allocated to govt except for specific product proration. Mirrors (iii) for current period.

Natural_Language: Parent for contract provision and CO documentation requirements when deferred costs are recognized.
Validation_Notes: Parent for two conjunctive requirements when deferred IR&D costs are recognized.

Natural_Language: When deferred costs are recognized, the contract (except firm-fixed-price and fixed-price with economic price adjustment contracts) will include a specific provision setting forth the amount of deferred IR&D costs that are allocable to the contract.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Contract provision requirement for deferred costs. Excludes FFP and FP-EPA contracts. 'Will' = declarative/mandatory.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must document the circumstances and reason for accepting the deferred costs in the negotiation memorandum.
Validation_Notes: CO documentation duty. 'Must' = mandatory. Both circumstances AND reasons required in negotiation memorandum.

Natural_Language: Cooperative arrangements. Parent for IR&D costs under cooperative arrangements including joint ventures, limited partnerships, teaming, CRDAs, and cost allowability.
Validation_Notes: Parent for four sub-provisions covering cooperative arrangement IR&D treatment.

Natural_Language: IR&D costs may be incurred by contractors working jointly with one or more non-Federal entities pursuant to a cooperative arrangement (e.g., joint ventures, limited partnerships, teaming arrangements, and collaboration and consortium arrangements).
Formal_Logic_Statement: CooperativeArrangement(JointVenture v LimitedPartnership v TeamingArrangement v Collaboration v Consortium) -> (IncurIRDCosts v ~IncurIRDCosts)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive. IR&D costs can be incurred under cooperative arrangements. Examples are illustrative.

Natural_Language: IR&D costs may include costs contributed by contractors in performing cooperative research and development agreements, or similar arrangements, entered into under specified statutory authorities.
Formal_Logic_Statement: CRDA_Costs -> (MayInclude_InIRD v ~MayInclude_InIRD) ^ (P_31_205_18_e_2_i v P_31_205_18_e_2_ii v P_31_205_18_e_2_iii v P_31_205_18_e_2_iv)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: May include' = permissive. CRDA costs can be counted as IR&D. Parent for four statutory authority sources.
Stevenson-Wydler Technology Innovation Act authority for CRDAs.

Natural_Language: 51 U.S.C. 20113(e) for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
Validation_Notes: NASA-specific CRDA authority.

Natural_Language: 10 U.S.C. 4021 for DoD.
Validation_Notes: DoD-specific CRDA authority.

Natural_Language: Other equivalent authority.
Validation_Notes: Catch-all for other equivalent statutory authorities beyond the three specifically named.

Natural_Language: IR&D costs incurred by a contractor pursuant to these types of cooperative arrangements should be considered as allowable IR&D costs if the work performed would have been allowed as contractor IR&D had there been no cooperative arrangement.
Validation_Notes: Should' = advisory, not binding. Allowability test: would the work qualify as IR&D if done independently? Noted as advisory per modal verb mapping.

Natural_Language: Costs incurred in preparing, submitting, and supporting offers on potential cooperative arrangements are allowable if they are allocable, reasonable, and not otherwise unallowable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Standard three-part allowability test for cooperative arrangement offer costs. Fourth condition (~otherwise unallowable) adds catch-all constraint.

Natural_Language: 31.205-19 Insurance and indemnification. Parent proposition establishing rules for insurance (purchased and self-insurance) and indemnification cost allowability, including captive insurer treatment, CAS 416 compliance, and specific cost limitations.
Validation_Notes: Parent for five sub-provisions: scope (a), captive insurer treatment (b), self-insurance limitations (c), purchased insurance limitations (d), and cost limitations (e).

Natural_Language: Insurance by purchase or by self-insuring includes coverage the contractor is required to carry under contract terms and any other coverage maintained in connection with general business conduct.
Validation_Notes: Parent defining scope of insurance: required coverage plus voluntary business coverage.

Natural_Language: Coverage the contractor is required to carry or to have approved, under the terms of the contract.
Validation_Notes: Contract-mandated insurance coverage. Disjunctive: required to carry OR required to have approved.

Natural_Language: Any other coverage the contractor maintains in connection with the general conduct of its business.
Validation_Notes: Voluntary business insurance coverage. Broad scope ('any other').

Natural_Language: Parent for captive insurer treatment rules.
Validation_Notes: Parent for captive insurer default treatment and competition exception.

Natural_Language: For purposes of applying the provisions of this section, the Government considers insurance provided by captive insurers (i.e., insurers owned by or under control of the contractor) as self-insurance.
Validation_Notes: Default rule: captive insurer = self-insurance treatment. Prevents circumvention of self-insurance limits through related-party insurers.

Natural_Language: If the captive insurer also sells insurance to the general public in substantial quantities and it can be demonstrated that the charge to the contractor is based on competition, the Government will consider the insurance as purchased insurance.
Validation_Notes: Exception to captive insurer default. Three conjunctive conditions: (1) sells to public, (2) in substantial quantities, (3) demonstrated competition-based pricing. 'Will' = declarative.

Natural_Language: Whether or not the contract is subject to CAS, self-insurance charges are allowable subject to paragraph (e) of this section and the following limitations.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Universal applicability (CAS or not). Self-insurance allowable but subject to (e) limitations plus four specific constraints. Tautological antecedent.

Natural_Language: The contractor must measure, assign, and allocate costs in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.416.
Validation_Notes: CAS 416 compliance mandatory for self-insurance. Three conjunctive requirements. External dependency on CAS 416.

Natural_Language: The contractor must comply with part 28; however, approval of a contractor's insurance program in accordance with part 28 does not constitute a determination as to the allowability of the program's cost.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Part 28 compliance required but its approval is not an allowability determination. Separates insurance program approval from cost allowability.

Natural_Language: If purchased insurance is available, any self-insurance charge plus insurance administration expenses in excess of the cost of comparable purchased insurance plus associated insurance administration expenses is unallowable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Cost cap: self-insurance plus admin cannot exceed comparable purchased insurance plus admin. Prevents self-insurance premium over market.

Natural_Language: Self-insurance charges for risks of catastrophic losses are unallowable (see 28.308(e)).
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on self-insuring catastrophic losses. Cross-ref to 28.308(e).

Natural_Language: Purchased insurance costs are allowable, subject to paragraph (e) of this section and the following limitations.
Validation_Notes: General allowability of purchased insurance subject to (e) limitations and three specific constraints.

Natural_Language: For contracts subject to full CAS coverage, the contractor must measure, assign, and allocate costs in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.416.
Validation_Notes: CAS 416 compliance for purchased insurance under fully CAS-covered contracts. Same CAS requirement as self-insurance (c)(1) but scoped to full CAS only.

Natural_Language: For all contracts, premiums for insurance purchased from fronting insurance companies (insurance companies not related to the contractor but who reinsure with a captive insurer of the contractor) are unallowable to the extent they exceed the sum of the amount that would have been allowed had the contractor insured directly with the captive insurer and reasonable fronting company charges for services rendered.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Anti-fronting provision: premiums capped at direct-captive equivalent plus reasonable fronting fees. Prevents inflating costs through intermediary arrangement.

Natural_Language: The amount that would have been allowed had the contractor insured directly with the captive insurer.
Validation_Notes: First component of fronting premium cap: direct captive insurance equivalent.

Natural_Language: Reasonable fronting company charges for services rendered.
Validation_Notes: Second component of fronting premium cap: reasonable service charges.

Natural_Language: Actual losses are unallowable unless expressly provided for in the contract, except losses under nominal deductibles and minor losses in ordinary course of business.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Default prohibition on actual losses with two exceptions: contract provision and specific carved-out loss types in (i) and (ii).

Natural_Language: Losses incurred under the nominal deductible provisions of purchased insurance, in keeping with sound business practice, are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Exception 1: nominal deductible losses allowable if consistent with sound business practice. Two conjunctive conditions.

Natural_Language: Minor losses, such as spoilage, breakage, and disappearance of small hand tools that occur in the ordinary course of business and that are not covered by insurance, are allowable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Exception 2: minor uninsured business losses allowable. Three conjunctive conditions. Examples illustrative ('such as').

Natural_Language: Self-insurance and purchased insurance costs are subject to the following cost limitations.
Validation_Notes: Parent for seven cost limitations applicable to both self-insurance and purchased insurance.

Natural_Language: Costs of insurance required or approved pursuant to the contract are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Contract-required or approved insurance is allowable. Disjunctive trigger.

Natural_Language: Costs of insurance maintained by the contractor in connection with the general conduct of its business are allowable subject to the following limitations.
Formal_Logic_Statement: GeneralBusinessInsurance -> Allowable_SubjectTo(P_31_205_19_e_2_i ^ P_31_205_19_e_2_ii ^ P_31_205_19_e_2_iii ^ P_31_205_19_e_2_iv ^ P_31_205_19_e_2_v)
Validation_Notes: General business insurance allowable with five specific limitations. Parent for (i)-(v).

Natural_Language: Types and extent of coverage must follow sound business practice, and the rates and premiums must be reasonable.
Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive requirements: sound business practice for coverage scope AND reasonable rates/premiums.

Natural_Language: Costs allowed for business interruption or other similar insurance must be limited to exclude coverage of profit.
Validation_Notes: Business interruption insurance cannot include profit coverage. Government does not insure contractor profits.

Natural_Language: The cost of property insurance premiums for insurance coverage in excess of the acquisition cost of the insured assets is allowable only when the contractor has a formal written policy assuring that in the event the insured property is involuntarily converted, the new asset must be valued at the book value of the replaced asset plus or minus adjustments for differences between insurance proceeds and actual replacement cost. If the contractor does not have such a formal written policy, the cost of premiums for insurance coverage in excess of the acquisition cost of the insured asset is unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_19_e_2_iii_a: Excess coverage premiums allowable with formal written replacement policy; P_31_205_19_e_2_iii_b: Without such policy, excess coverage premiums are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Only when' creates biconditional. Formal written policy is both necessary and sufficient for excess coverage premium allowability. Policy must specify book-value replacement valuation.

Natural_Language: Costs of insurance for the risk of loss of Government property are allowable to the extent that the contractor is liable for such loss, the contracting officer has not revoked the Government's assumption of risk (see 45.104(b)), and the insurance does not cover loss from willful misconduct or lack of good faith by managerial personnel (see FAR 52.245-1(h)(1)(ii)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_19_e_2_iv_a: Contractor is liable for loss; P_31_205_19_e_2_iv_b: CO has not revoked risk assumption; P_31_205_19_e_2_iv_c: Insurance does not cover willful misconduct/lack of good faith
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive conditions for government property insurance allowability. Cross-refs to 45.104(b) and FAR 52.245-1(h)(1)(ii). Sub-items (A)-(C) in source text handled via atomic decomposition.

Natural_Language: Costs of insurance on the lives of officers, partners, proprietors, or employees are allowable only to the extent that the insurance represents additional compensation (see 31.205-6).
Formal_Logic_Statement: LifeInsurance(Officers v Partners v Proprietors v Employees) -> Allowable_OnlyAsAdditionalCompensation
Validation_Notes: Only to the extent' = proportional limitation. Key person life insurance allowable only as compensation. Cross-ref to 31.205-6 compensation rules.

Natural_Language: The cost of insurance to protect the contractor against the costs of correcting its own defects in materials and workmanship is unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on insuring against own quality failures. Government does not pay for contractor to insure against its own defective work.

Natural_Language: The cost of insurance to cover fortuitous or casualty losses resulting from defects in materials or workmanship are allowable as a normal business expense.
Validation_Notes: Distinction from (e)(3): insurance against fortuitous/casualty losses from defects IS allowable, unlike insurance against correction costs. Key difference: insuring outcomes vs. insuring remediation.

Natural_Language: Premiums for retroactive or backdated insurance written to cover known losses that have occurred are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on retroactive insurance for known losses. Insurance by definition covers future risk; covering known losses is not genuine insurance.

Natural_Language: The Government is obligated to indemnify the contractor only to the extent authorized by law, as expressly provided for in the contract, except as provided in paragraph (d)(3) of this section.
Validation_Notes: Government indemnification limited to legal authorization AND express contract provision. Exception for actual losses under (d)(3). Two conjunctive conditions for indemnification.

Natural_Language: Late premium payment charges related to employee deferred compensation plan insurance incurred pursuant to 29 U.S.C. 1307 or 29 U.S.C. 1323 are unallowable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on late payment charges for ERISA-related insurance. Contractor should not pass penalty for tardy payments to Government.

Natural_Language: 31.205-20 Interest and other financial costs. [Reserved]

Validation_Notes: Reserved section. No operative text to convert. Placeholder only.

Validation_Notes: Costs aimed at persuading employees on collective bargaining rights are categorically unallowable. EO 13494 is an external authority reference. HIGH-RISK rule 15 used for conditional structure. Sub-items (1)-(4) are examples, not exhaustive.

Natural_Language: Hiring or consulting legal counsel or consultants.

Natural_Language: Meetings (including paying the salaries of the attendees at meetings held for this purpose); and

Natural_Language: Planning or conducting activities by managers, supervisors, or union representatives during work hours.
