Natural_Language: 31.205-22 Lobbying and political activity costs. Costs of lobbying and political activities are generally unallowable (paragraph (a)), with specific exceptions (paragraph (b)), and procedural requirements for identification, recordkeeping, and dispute resolution (paragraphs (c)-(e)).
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating all paragraphs of 31.205-22. Conjunctive: all sub-requirements apply simultaneously.

Natural_Language: Costs associated with the following activities are unallowable: (1) influencing elections, (2) political organizations, (3) influencing legislation, (4) legislative liaison for unallowable purposes, (5) improperly influencing Executive branch.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive antecedent: any one of the five listed activities triggers unallowability. Each sub-item independently sufficient to render costs unallowable.

Natural_Language: Attempts to influence the outcomes of any Federal, State, or local election, referendum, initiative, or similar procedure, through in-kind or cash contributions, endorsements, publicity, or similar activities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_a_1: Costs of attempting to influence outcomes of any Federal, State, or local election, referendum, initiative, or similar procedure through contributions, endorsements, publicity, or similar activities are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Broad scope: covers all levels of government elections and similar procedures. Methods listed (contributions, endorsements, publicity) are illustrative via 'or similar activities'.

Natural_Language: Establishing, administering, contributing to, or paying the expenses of a political party, campaign, political action committee, or other organization established for the purpose of influencing the outcomes of elections.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_a_2: Costs of establishing, administering, contributing to, or paying expenses of political parties, campaigns, PACs, or similar organizations aimed at influencing elections are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Covers full lifecycle of political organization involvement: establishment through ongoing financial support. Disjunctive activities (establishing OR administering OR contributing OR paying) all trigger unallowability.

Natural_Language: Any attempt to influence the introduction of Federal, state, or local legislation, or enactment or modification of any pending Federal, state, or local legislation, through methods in (i) and (ii).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Parent for legislative influence prohibition. Two methods specified in sub-items (i) and (ii). Covers both introduction and modification of legislation at all government levels.

Natural_Language: Through communication with any member or employee of the Congress or state legislature including efforts to influence state or local officials to engage in similar lobbying activity, or with any government official or employee in connection with a decision to sign or veto enrolled legislation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_a_3_i: Influencing legislation through direct communication with legislators, legislative employees, or government officials regarding signing/vetoing legislation is unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Covers direct lobbying: communication with Congress members/staff, state legislators, and officials involved in sign/veto decisions. Also covers indirect lobbying via influencing state/local officials to lobby.

Natural_Language: By preparing, distributing or using publicity or propaganda, or by urging members of the general public or any segment thereof to contribute to or participate in any mass demonstration, march, rally, fund raising drive, lobbying campaign or letter writing or telephone campaign.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_a_3_ii: Influencing legislation through publicity/propaganda or grassroots mobilization (demonstrations, rallies, fundraising drives, letter/phone campaigns) is unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Covers grassroots lobbying: publicity, propaganda, and public mobilization activities. Broad list of grassroots methods is illustrative.

Natural_Language: Legislative liaison activities, including attendance at legislative sessions or committee hearings, gathering information regarding legislation, and analyzing the effect of legislation, when such activities are carried on in support of or in knowing preparation for an effort to engage in unallowable activities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_a_4: Costs of legislative liaison activities (attending sessions/hearings, gathering/analyzing legislative information) are unallowable when carried on in support of or in knowing preparation for unallowable lobbying activities.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Critical conditional: legislative liaison is only unallowable WHEN done in support of or knowing preparation for other unallowable activities. Same activities could be allowable if not connected to prohibited purposes. The 'when' clause is determinative.

Natural_Language: Costs incurred in attempting to improperly influence (see 3.401), either directly or indirectly, an employee or officer of the Executive branch of the Government to give consideration to or act regarding a regulatory or contract matter.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_a_5: Costs of attempting to improperly influence Executive branch employees/officers regarding regulatory or contract matters, directly or indirectly, are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Cross-references FAR 3.401 for definition of 'improperly influence'. Covers both direct and indirect influence attempts on Executive branch regarding regulatory or contract matters.

Natural_Language: Costs associated with the following activities are excepted from paragraph (a) of this section: (1) technical/factual presentations, (2) lobbying to reduce contract cost, (3) statutorily authorized activities.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Exception clause: three types of activities are carved out from the general prohibition in (a). Disjunctive: any one exception independently sufficient. The exception negates application of (a), not the underlying cost characterization.

Natural_Language: Providing a technical and factual presentation of information on a topic directly related to the performance of a contract through a hearing testimony, statements, or letters to the Congress or a state legislature, or subdivision, member, or cognizant staff member thereof, in response to a documented request (including a Congressional Record notice requesting testimony or statements for the record at a regularly scheduled hearing) made by the recipient member, legislative body, or subdivision, or a cognizant staff member thereof, provided such information is readily obtainable and can be readily put in deliverable form; and provided that costs under this section for transportation, lodging or meals are unallowable unless incurred for the purpose of offering testimony at a regularly scheduled Congressional hearing pursuant to a written request for such presentation made by the Chairman or Ranking Minority Member of the Committee or Subcommittee conducting such hearing.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_b_1_a: Technical/factual presentation directly related to contract performance; P_31_205_22_b_1_b: Made through testimony/statements/letters to Congress or state legislature; P_31_205_22_b_1_c: In response to documented request; P_31_205_22_b_1_d: Information readily obtainable and deliverable; P_31_205_22_b_1_e: Transportation/lodging/meals unallowable unless for testimony at regularly scheduled Congressional hearing per written request from Chairman or Ranking Minority Member
Formal_Logic_Statement: (TechnicalFactualPresentation ^ DirectlyRelatedToContract ^ DocumentedRequest ^ ReadilyObtainable) -> ExceptedFromProhibition; TransportLodgingMeals -> ~Allowable UNLESS (RegularlyScheduledHearing ^ WrittenRequestChairmanOrRanking)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex multi-condition exception. Four conjunctive requirements for the exception to apply. Additional nested restriction on travel costs: only allowable for regularly scheduled Congressional hearings with written request from committee leadership. HIGH-RISK: multiple conditionals interacting.

Natural_Language: Any lobbying made unallowable by paragraph (a)(3) of this section to influence state or local legislation in order to directly reduce contract cost, or to avoid material impairment of the contractor's authority to perform the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_b_2: Lobbying to influence state/local legislation is excepted from (a)(3) prohibition when done to directly reduce contract cost or avoid material impairment of contractor's performance authority.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Exception limited to state/local legislation lobbying (not federal). Disjunctive purpose: cost reduction OR avoiding material impairment. 'Directly' narrows the cost-reduction justification.

Natural_Language: Any activity specifically authorized by statute to be undertaken with funds from the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_b_3: Activities specifically authorized by statute to use contract funds are excepted from the (a) prohibition.
Validation_Notes: Broad statutory carve-out. Requires specific statutory authorization, not general permissiveness. External dependency: specific authorizing statutes not identified.

Natural_Language: When a contractor seeks reimbursement for indirect costs, total lobbying costs must be separately identified in the indirect cost rate proposal, and thereafter treated as other unallowable activity costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_c: When seeking indirect cost reimbursement, contractor must separately identify total lobbying costs in indirect cost rate proposal and treat them as unallowable activity costs.
Validation_Notes: Procedural requirement triggered by seeking indirect cost reimbursement. Two mandatory actions: separate identification AND treatment as unallowable. Cross-reference to indirect cost rate proposal process.

Natural_Language: Contractors must maintain adequate records to demonstrate that the certification of costs as being allowable or unallowable (see 42.703-2) pursuant to this section complies with the requirements of this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_d: Contractors must maintain adequate records demonstrating that cost allowability/unallowability certifications under this section comply with section requirements.
Validation_Notes: Mandatory recordkeeping requirement. Cross-references FAR 42.703-2 for certification requirements. 'Must' = mandatory. Records must be adequate to demonstrate compliance.

Natural_Language: Existing procedures should be utilized to resolve in advance any significant questions or disagreements concerning the interpretation or application of this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_22_e: Existing procedures should be used to resolve in advance significant questions or disagreements about interpretation or application of this section.
Validation_Notes: Should' = advisory, not mandatory. PENDING_REVIEW per methodology for advisory language. Encourages proactive dispute resolution but does not mandate it.

Natural_Language: Losses on other contracts, including the contractor's contributed portion under cost-sharing contracts, are unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_23: Losses on other contracts (including contractor's contributed portion under cost-sharing contracts) are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition. Covers all losses on other contracts including cost-sharing portions. No exceptions stated. Simple conditional: if the cost is a loss on another contract, it is unallowable.

Natural_Language: [Reserved]
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_24: Reserved section with no current regulatory content.
Validation_Notes: Reserved section. No operative text to convert. Placeholder only.

Natural_Language: 31.205-25 Manufacturing and production engineering costs. Certain manufacturing and production engineering costs are allowable (paragraph (a)), certain activities are excluded from this cost principle (paragraph (b)), and capitalized costs are governed by 31.205-11 (paragraph (c)).
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Three paragraphs operate conjunctively: allowable costs, exclusions, and capitalization rule.

Natural_Language: The following costs of manufacturing and production engineering effort are allowable: (1) new/improved materials and techniques, (2) pilot production lines, (3) improving production functions, (4) producibility analysis.
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive list of allowable manufacturing/production engineering costs. Each type independently sufficient to be allowable.

Natural_Language: Developing and deploying new or improved materials, systems, processes, methods, equipment, tools and techniques that are, or are expected to be, used in producing products or services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_25_a_1: Costs of developing and deploying new or improved production materials, systems, processes, methods, equipment, tools, and techniques (used or expected to be used in production) are allowable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive conditions: must be developing/deploying AND new/improved AND used or expected to be used in production. 'Expected to be' broadens beyond current use.

Natural_Language: Developing and deploying pilot production lines.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_25_a_2: Costs of developing and deploying pilot production lines are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Straightforward allowability for pilot production line development and deployment costs.

Natural_Language: Improving current production functions, such as plant layout, production scheduling and control, methods and job analysis, equipment capabilities and capacities, inspection techniques, and tooling analysis (including tooling design and application improvements).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_25_a_3: Costs of improving current production functions (plant layout, scheduling, methods analysis, equipment capabilities, inspection, tooling) are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Allowable production improvement costs. 'Such as' list is illustrative. Broad scope covering various production function improvements.

Natural_Language: Material and manufacturing producibility analysis for production suitability and to optimize manufacturing processes, methods, and techniques.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_25_a_4: Costs of material and manufacturing producibility analysis (for production suitability and process optimization) are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Allowable producibility analysis costs. Dual purpose: production suitability assessment and manufacturing optimization.

Natural_Language: This cost principle does not cover: (1) basic and applied research related to new technology (see 31.205-18), and (2) development for manufacturing items intended for sale (see 31.205-18).
Validation_Notes: Scope exclusion. Two categories excluded conjunctively. Both redirect to 31.205-18 (Independent research and development costs).

Natural_Language: Basic and applied research effort related to new technology, materials, systems, processes, methods, equipment, tools and techniques (see 31.205-18).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_25_b_1: Basic and applied research related to new technology/materials/systems/processes/methods/equipment/tools/techniques is excluded from this cost principle and governed by 31.205-18.
Validation_Notes: Scope exclusion redirecting to 31.205-18. Distinguishes research (excluded) from production engineering (covered by this section).

Natural_Language: Development effort for manufacturing or production materials, systems, processes, methods, equipment, tools and techniques that are intended for sale (see 31.205-18).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_25_b_2: Development of manufacturing/production capabilities intended for sale is excluded from this cost principle and governed by 31.205-18.
Validation_Notes: Key distinction: development FOR SALE goes to 31.205-18, not this section. Production engineering for internal use stays here.

Natural_Language: Where manufacturing or production development costs are capitalized or required to be capitalized under the contractor's capitalization policies, allowable cost will be determined in accordance with the requirements of 31.205-11.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_25_c: When manufacturing/production development costs are capitalized or required to be capitalized, allowability is determined per 31.205-11.
Validation_Notes: Conditional redirect: capitalization triggers application of 31.205-11 (Depreciation) instead of this section. Disjunctive trigger: actually capitalized OR required to capitalize.

Natural_Language: 31.205-26 Material costs. Rules for determining allowable material costs, including definitions (a), adjustments (b), inventory adjustments (c), charging methods (d), interorganizational transfers (e), and commercial item pricing (f).
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Six paragraphs operate conjunctively covering different aspects of material cost allowability.

Natural_Language: Material costs definitions and computation requirements (paragraphs (a)(1) and (a)(2)).
Validation_Notes: Sub-parent aggregating definition of material costs and computation requirement. Both apply.

Natural_Language: Material costs include the costs of items, such as raw materials, parts, subassemblies, components, and manufacturing supplies, whether purchased or manufactured by the contractor, and may include collateral items such as inbound transportation and in-transit insurance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_a_1_a: Material costs include costs of items (raw materials, parts, subassemblies, components, manufacturing supplies) whether purchased or manufactured; P_31_205_26_a_1_b: Material costs may include collateral items (inbound transportation, in-transit insurance)
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Definitional. 'Such as' list is illustrative. 'May include' for collateral items = permissive (tautology per methodology). Covers both purchased and contractor-manufactured items.

Natural_Language: In computing material costs, the contractor must consider reasonable overruns, spoilage, or defective work (unless otherwise provided in any contract provision relating to inspecting and correcting defective work).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_a_2: When computing material costs, contractor must consider reasonable overruns, spoilage, or defective work, unless contract provides otherwise for inspection/correction of defective work.
Formal_Logic_Statement: ComputingMaterialCosts -> MustConsider(ReasonableOverruns v Spoilage v DefectiveWork); ContractProvisionForDefectiveWork -> ~ThisRequirement
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Must' = mandatory. Disjunctive list of factors to consider. 'Unless' clause creates exception when contract has specific defective work provisions. 'Reasonable' is a qualifying judgment term.

Natural_Language: The contractor must adjust material costs for credits and properly handle income credits, per (b)(1) and (b)(2).
Validation_Notes: Parent 'must' requirement with two mandatory sub-obligations. Both must be performed.

Natural_Language: Adjust the costs of material for income and other credits, including available trade discounts, refunds, rebates, allowances, and cash discounts, and credits for scrap, salvage, and material returned to vendors.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_b_1: Contractor must adjust material costs for income and other credits including trade discounts, refunds, rebates, allowances, cash discounts, scrap credits, salvage credits, and vendor return credits.
Validation_Notes: Mandatory adjustment requirement. 'Including' list is illustrative of credit types that must be accounted for. Broad scope covering various credit and discount types.

Natural_Language: Credit such income and other credits either directly to the cost of the material or allocate such income and other credits as a credit to indirect costs. When the contractor can demonstrate that failure to take cash discounts was reasonable, the contractor does not need to credit lost discounts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_b_2_a: Credits must be applied either directly to material cost or allocated as indirect cost credit; P_31_205_26_b_2_b: When failure to take cash discounts was demonstrably reasonable, lost discounts need not be credited.
Justification_Rules: Addition (Add): Rule 8; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two parts: (1) disjunctive crediting methods (direct OR indirect), (2) conditional exception for lost cash discounts when failure to take them was reasonable. 'Can demonstrate' places burden on contractor.

Natural_Language: Reasonable adjustments arising from differences between periodic physical inventories and book inventories may be included in arriving at costs when such adjustments relate to the period of contract performance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_c: Reasonable inventory adjustments (physical vs. book) may be included in costs when adjustments relate to the contract performance period.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive (tautology). Two conditions: adjustments must be reasonable AND relate to contract performance period. Inventory variance inclusion is discretionary when conditions met.

Natural_Language: Material charging methods for contract-specific purchases (d)(1) and store-issued materials (d)(2).
Validation_Notes: Sub-parent. Two methods for charging materials to contracts depending on procurement method.

Natural_Language: When materials are purchased specifically for and are identifiable solely with performance under a contract, the actual purchase cost of those materials should be charged to the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_d_1: When materials are purchased specifically for and identifiable solely with a contract, actual purchase cost should be charged to that contract.
Validation_Notes: Should' = advisory. Two conjunctive conditions: purchased specifically for AND identifiable solely with the contract. PENDING_REVIEW per methodology for 'should' language.

Natural_Language: If material is issued from stores, any generally recognized method of pricing such material is acceptable if that method is consistently applied and the results are equitable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_d_2: For store-issued material, any generally recognized pricing method is acceptable if consistently applied and producing equitable results.
Validation_Notes: Four conjunctive conditions for acceptability: issued from stores, recognized method, consistent application, and equitable results. Flexible on method choice but strict on consistency and equity.

Natural_Language: Allowance for materials, supplies and services that are sold or transferred between any divisions, subdivisions, subsidiaries, or affiliates of the contractor under a common control must be on basis of cost (e)(1) or may be at price when conditions met (e)(2).
Validation_Notes: Interorganizational transfer pricing. Disjunctive: cost basis (default) OR price basis (when conditions met). Scope: divisions, subdivisions, subsidiaries, affiliates under common control.

Natural_Language: Must be on the basis of cost incurred in accordance with this subpart.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_e_1: Interorganizational transfers must be priced on cost basis per Subpart 31.2.
Validation_Notes: Must' = mandatory default. Cost basis is the standard requirement for interorganizational transfers. Cross-references Subpart 31.2 for cost determination.

Natural_Language: May be at price when conditions in (i) and (ii) are met.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive (tautology). Both conditions (i) and (ii) must be met conjunctively for price-basis option to be available.

Natural_Language: It is the established practice of the transferring organization to price interorganizational transfers at other than cost for commercial work of the contractor or any division, subsidiary or affiliate of the contractor under a common control.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_e_2_i: The transferring organization must have an established practice of pricing interorganizational transfers at other than cost for commercial work.
Validation_Notes: First condition for price-basis transfers. Requires established practice (not ad hoc) for commercial work specifically. Organization must already price commercial interorg transfers at other than cost.

Natural_Language: The item being transferred qualifies for an exception under 15.403-1(b) and the contracting officer has not determined the price to be unreasonable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_e_2_ii: The transferred item must qualify for a 15.403-1(b) exception AND the contracting officer must not have determined the price unreasonable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Second condition for price-basis transfers. Two conjunctive requirements: exception qualification AND no unreasonableness determination. Cross-references FAR 15.403-1(b).

Natural_Language: When a commercial product or commercial service under paragraph (e) of this section is sold or transferred at a price based on a catalog or market price, the contractor should/may make adjustments per (f)(1) and (f)(2).
Validation_Notes: Conditional on commercial product/service transferred at catalog/market price. Triggers two adjustment considerations. Cross-references paragraph (e).

Natural_Language: Should adjust the price to reflect the quantities being acquired.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_f_1: Contractor should adjust catalog/market price to reflect acquisition quantities.
Validation_Notes: Should' = advisory. PENDING_REVIEW per methodology. Quantity adjustments are expected but not strictly mandatory.

Natural_Language: May adjust the price to reflect the actual cost of any modifications necessary because of contract requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_26_f_2: Contractor may adjust price to reflect actual cost of modifications required by contract.
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive (tautology). Adjustment for contract-required modifications is discretionary, not mandatory.

Natural_Language: 31.205-27 Organization costs. Expenditures for organization/reorganization and capital raising are generally unallowable (paragraph (a)), with exception for compensation-related stock activities (paragraph (b)).
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. General prohibition with compensation exception.

Natural_Language: Organization cost prohibitions and clarifications (paragraphs (a)(1) through (a)(3)).
Validation_Notes: Sub-parent aggregating prohibition scope, expenditure types, and reorganization cost clarification.

Validation_Notes: Prohibition with exception carve-out for paragraph (b). Three disjunctive categories of unallowable expenditures. 'Except as provided' creates conditional: prohibition applies unless (b) exception triggered.

Natural_Language: Planning or executing the organization or reorganization of the corporate structure of a business, including mergers and acquisitions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_27_a_1_i: Expenditures for planning or executing corporate organization/reorganization (including M&A) are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Covers both planning and execution phases. 'Including mergers and acquisitions' broadens scope. Subject to (b) exception.

Natural_Language: Resisting or planning to resist the reorganization of the corporate structure of a business or a change in the controlling interest in the ownership of a business.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_27_a_1_ii: Expenditures for resisting or planning to resist corporate reorganization or ownership changes are unallowable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Anti-takeover defense costs are unallowable. Covers both actual resistance and planning for resistance. Disjunctive: either activity triggers unallowability.

Natural_Language: Raising capital (net worth plus long-term liabilities).

Natural_Language: Such expenditures include incorporation fees and costs of attorneys, accountants, brokers, promoters and organizers, management consultants and investment counselors, whether or not employees of the contractor.

Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_28_a: Registry and transfer charges from ownership changes in contractor-issued securities are allowable recurring business costs.
Validation_Notes: Specific allowable business cost. Limited to changes in ownership of contractor's own securities.

Natural_Language: Cost of shareholders' meetings.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_28_b: Costs of shareholders' meetings are allowable recurring business costs.
Validation_Notes: Straightforward allowability for shareholder meeting costs.

Natural_Language: Normal proxy solicitations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_28_c: Costs of normal proxy solicitations are allowable recurring business costs.
Validation_Notes: Normal' qualifier implies extraordinary proxy solicitations (e.g., proxy fights) may not be covered. Routine proxy activities are allowable.

Natural_Language: Preparing and publishing reports to shareholders.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_28_d: Costs of preparing and publishing shareholder reports are allowable recurring business costs.
Validation_Notes: Covers both preparation and publication of shareholder reports.

Natural_Language: Preparing and submitting required reports and forms to taxing and other regulatory bodies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_28_e: Costs of preparing and submitting required reports/forms to taxing and regulatory bodies are allowable recurring business costs.
Validation_Notes: Required' qualifier limits to mandatory filings. Voluntary submissions may not be covered.

Natural_Language: Incidental costs of directors' and committee meetings.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_28_f: Incidental costs of directors' and committee meetings are allowable recurring business costs.
Validation_Notes: Incidental' qualifier limits scope. Major or extraordinary meeting costs may require separate analysis.

Natural_Language: Other similar costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_28_g: Other costs similar to those listed in (a)-(f) are allowable recurring business costs.
Validation_Notes: Catch-all provision. 'Similar' requires analogy to listed cost types. Provides flexibility for unlisted but comparable recurring business costs.

Natural_Language: 31.205-29 Plant protection costs. Allowable plant protection costs include (a) wages/uniforms/equipment of protection personnel, (b) depreciation on protection capital assets, (c) military compliance expenses.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Disjunctive: each type of plant protection cost independently allowable.

Natural_Language: Wages, uniforms, and equipment of personnel engaged in plant protection.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_29_a: Wages, uniforms, and equipment costs for plant protection personnel are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive list of allowable cost types for protection personnel: wages AND uniforms AND equipment.

Natural_Language: Depreciation on plant protection capital assets.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_29_b: Depreciation on plant protection capital assets is allowable.
Validation_Notes: Allowability of depreciation on protection-related capital assets. Cross-reference to 31.205-11 for depreciation methodology implied.

Natural_Language: Necessary expenses to comply with military requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_29_c: Necessary expenses for compliance with military requirements for plant protection are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Necessary' qualifier requires expenses to be genuinely needed for military compliance, not merely convenient.

Natural_Language: 31.205-30 Patent costs. Certain patent costs are allowable when required by Government contract (paragraph (a)), general patent counseling is allowable (paragraph (b)), and non-required patent costs are unallowable (paragraph (c)).
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Three paragraphs: contract-required patent costs (allowable), general counseling (allowable), non-required patent costs (unallowable).

Natural_Language: The following patent costs are allowable when incurred as a requirement of a Government contract (except see 31.205-33): (1) invention disclosures, (2) art searches, (3) patent filing/prosecution where Government gets title or royalty-free license.
Formal_Logic_Statement: GovernmentContractRequirement ^ ~P_31_205_33_exception -> (P_31_205_30_a_1 v P_31_205_30_a_2 v P_31_205_30_a_3) -> Allowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional allowability: must be a Government contract requirement. Cross-references 31.205-33 as exception. Three disjunctive types of allowable patent costs.

Natural_Language: Costs of preparing invention disclosures, reports, and other documents.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_30_a_1: Costs of preparing invention disclosures, reports, and related documents are allowable when required by Government contract.
Validation_Notes: Allowability contingent on Government contract requirement (from parent). Covers disclosures, reports, and related documentation.

Natural_Language: Costs for searching the art to the extent necessary to make the invention disclosures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_30_a_2: Art search costs necessary for invention disclosures are allowable when required by Government contract.
Validation_Notes: To the extent necessary' limits allowability to searches needed for disclosures, not broader patent landscape searches.

Natural_Language: Other costs in connection with the filing and prosecution of a United States patent application where title or royalty-free license is to be conveyed to the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_30_a_3: Patent filing/prosecution costs for US patent applications where Government receives title or royalty-free license are allowable when required by Government contract.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive conditions: contract-required AND US patent AND Government receives title or royalty-free license. Disjunctive on Government benefit: title OR license.

Natural_Language: General counseling services relating to patent matters, such as advice on patent laws, regulations, clauses, and employee agreements, are allowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_30_b: General patent counseling services (advice on patent laws, regulations, clauses, employee agreements) are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Allowable regardless of specific Government contract requirement. 'General counseling' is key qualifier. 'Such as' list is illustrative.

Natural_Language: Other than those for general counseling services, patent costs not required by the contract are unallowable (see 31.205-37).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_30_c: Patent costs not required by contract and not for general counseling services are unallowable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Residual prohibition. Two negative conditions: not required by contract AND not general counseling. Cross-references 31.205-37 (Royalties and other costs for use of patents).

Natural_Language: 31.205-31 Plant reconversion costs. Defines reconversion costs (paragraph (a)), declares them generally unallowable with exception (paragraph (b)), and allows additional costs when equity dictates (paragraph (c)).
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Three paragraphs: definition, general prohibition with exception, equity-based additional allowance.

Natural_Language: Plant reconversion costs are those incurred in restoring or rehabilitating the contractor's facilities to approximately the same condition that existed immediately prior to the start of the Government contract, with the exception of reasonable wear and tear.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_31_a: Plant reconversion costs are defined as costs to restore/rehabilitate contractor facilities to pre-Government-contract condition, excluding reasonable wear and tear.
Validation_Notes: Definitional provision. Two key qualifiers: 'approximately the same condition' (not perfect restoration) and exclusion of reasonable wear and tear.

Natural_Language: Reconversion costs are unallowable except for the cost of removing Government property and the restoration or rehabilitation costs caused by such removal.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_31_b: Reconversion costs are unallowable, except costs of removing Government property and restoration costs caused by that removal.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: General prohibition with narrow exception. Only Government property removal and its consequential restoration costs are allowable. All other reconversion costs are unallowable.

Natural_Language: In circumstances, where equity so dictates, additional costs may be allowed to the extent agreed upon before costs are incurred. Care should be exercised to avoid duplication of costs through allowance as contingencies, additional profit or fee, or in other contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_31_c_a: Where equity dictates, additional reconversion costs may be allowed if agreed upon before incurrence; P_31_205_31_c_b: Care should be exercised to avoid cost duplication through contingencies, profit/fee, or other contracts.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive (tautology). Two conjunctive conditions: equity dictates AND pre-agreement. 'Should' advisory on avoiding duplication. Equity is a judgment call. PENDING_REVIEW for both 'may' and 'should'.

Natural_Language: Precontract costs are costs incurred before the effective date of the contract directly pursuant to the negotiation and in anticipation of the contract award when such incurrence is necessary to comply with the proposed contract delivery schedule. These costs are allowable to the extent that they would have been allowable if incurred after the date of the contract (see 31.110).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_32_a: Precontract costs are costs incurred before contract effective date, directly pursuant to negotiation, in anticipation of award, when necessary for proposed delivery schedule; P_31_205_32_b: Such costs are allowable to the extent they would have been allowable if incurred post-contract.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Hypothetical Syllogism (HS): Rule 3
Validation_Notes: Complex multi-condition allowability. Four conjunctive conditions for cost characterization as precontract. Allowability test: hypothetical -- would the cost be allowable if incurred after contract? Cross-references 31.110. HIGH-RISK: nested conditionals.

Natural_Language: 31.205-33 Professional and consultant service costs. Definition (a), general description (b), allowability conditions (c), unallowable circumstances (d), allowability determination factors (e), and retainer fee rules (f).
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Six paragraphs covering full scope of professional/consultant service cost allowability.

Natural_Language: Professional and consultant services, as used in this section, means services provided by persons who are members of a particular profession or possess a special skill and who are not officers or employees of the contractor (e.g., services acquired by contractors or subcontractors in order to enhance their legal, economic, financial, or technical positions).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_a: Professional and consultant services are defined as services from non-employee professionals or specialists (e.g., to enhance legal, economic, financial, or technical positions).
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Two disjunctive qualifications (profession member OR special skill) AND one exclusion (not officer/employee). Example list is illustrative.

Natural_Language: Professional and consultant services are generally acquired to obtain information, advice, opinions, alternatives, conclusions, recommendations, training, or direct assistance, such as for studies, analyses, evaluations, liaison with Government officials, or other forms of representation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_b: Professional/consultant services are generally acquired for information, advice, opinions, alternatives, conclusions, recommendations, training, or direct assistance.
Formal_Logic_Statement: ProfConsultantServices -> GenerallyFor(Information v Advice v Opinions v Alternatives v Conclusions v Recommendations v Training v DirectAssistance)
Validation_Notes: Descriptive provision. 'Generally' acknowledges exceptions. Disjunctive list of service purposes. Not a requirement, but context for applying the section.

Natural_Language: Costs of professional and consultant services are allowable subject to this section when reasonable in relation to the services rendered and when not contingent upon recovery of the costs from the Government (except see 31.205-30 and 31.205-47).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_c: Professional/consultant service costs are allowable when: (1) reasonable in relation to services rendered, (2) not contingent on Government cost recovery (except per 31.205-30 and 31.205-47), and (3) subject to this entire section's requirements.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive conditions for allowability. Contingency fee prohibition with two cross-reference exceptions (31.205-30 patent costs, 31.205-47 costs related to legal proceedings). 'Subject to this section' incorporates all other paragraphs.

Natural_Language: Costs of professional and consultant services performed under any of the following circumstances are unallowable: (1)-(4).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive list of unallowable circumstances. Any one independently triggers unallowability.

Natural_Language: Services to improperly obtain, distribute, or use information or data protected by law or regulation (e.g., 52.215-1(e), Restriction on Disclosure and Use of Data).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_d_1: Costs of services to improperly obtain, distribute, or use legally protected information/data are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Improperly' is the key qualifier. Proper use of protected data is not targeted. Cross-references FAR 52.215-1(e).

Natural_Language: Services that are intended to improperly influence the contents of solicitations, the evaluation of proposals or quotations, or the selection of sources for contract award, whether award is by the Government, or by a prime contractor or subcontractor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_d_2: Costs of services intended to improperly influence solicitation contents, proposal/quotation evaluation, or source selection (Government or prime/sub award) are unallowable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Broad anti-corruption provision. Covers influence on solicitations, evaluations, and source selection. Applies regardless of whether award is Government, prime, or subcontract level. 'Intended to improperly influence' is the trigger.

Natural_Language: Any other services obtained, performed, or otherwise resulting in violation of any statute or regulation prohibiting improper business practices or conflicts of interest.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_d_3: Costs of services violating statutes/regulations prohibiting improper business practices or conflicts of interest are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Catch-all for statutory/regulatory violations. Covers services obtained, performed, or resulting in violations. Broad scope: any statute or regulation on improper practices or conflicts.

Natural_Language: Services performed that are inconsistent with the purpose and scope of the services contracted for or otherwise agreed upon.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_d_4: Costs of services inconsistent with the contracted purpose and scope are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Scope limitation. Services must match what was contracted for. 'Or otherwise agreed upon' covers informal agreements beyond formal contract.

Natural_Language: In determining the allowability of costs (including retainer fees), no single factor or combination of factors is necessarily determinative; therefore, the contracting officer must consider the following factors: (1)-(8).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Multi-factor test. CO must consider ALL eight factors conjunctively. No single factor is determinative. 'Must consider' = mandatory analysis, but outcome is judgment-based. Includes retainer fees.

Natural_Language: The nature and scope of the service rendered in relation to the service required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_e_1: CO must consider the nature and scope of service rendered vs. service required.
Validation_Notes: Factor 1 of 8. Compares actual service delivery against what was needed. Judgment-based assessment.

Natural_Language: The necessity of contracting for the service, considering the contractor's capability in the particular area.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_e_2: CO must consider whether contracting for the service was necessary given the contractor's in-house capability.
Validation_Notes: Factor 2 of 8. Make-or-buy analysis: was external service genuinely needed or could contractor do it in-house?

Natural_Language: The past pattern of acquiring such services and their costs, particularly in the years prior to the award of Government contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_e_3: CO must consider the contractor's historical pattern of acquiring such services, especially pre-Government-contract years.
Validation_Notes: Factor 3 of 8. Historical comparison. 'Particularly' pre-Government-contract years suggests scrutiny of whether Government contract drove increased consulting costs.

Natural_Language: The impact of Government contracts on the contractor's business.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_e_4: CO must consider the impact of Government contracts on the contractor's overall business.
Validation_Notes: Factor 4 of 8. Assesses whether Government contracting creates additional consulting needs.

Natural_Language: Whether the proportion of Government work to the contractor's total business is such as to influence the contractor in favor of incurring the cost, particularly when the services rendered are not of a continuing nature and have little relationship to work under Government contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_e_5: CO must consider whether the Government work proportion influences the contractor to incur costs, especially for non-continuing services with little Government contract relationship.
Validation_Notes: Factor 5 of 8. Cost-shifting scrutiny: are consulting costs incurred primarily because Government will pay? 'Particularly' flags non-continuing, low-relevance services for extra scrutiny.

Natural_Language: Whether the service can be performed more economically by employment rather than by contracting.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_e_6: CO must consider whether hiring would be more economical than contracting for the service.
Validation_Notes: Factor 6 of 8. Cost-effectiveness comparison between employment and outsourcing.

Natural_Language: The qualifications of the individual or concern rendering the service, and the customary fee charged, especially on non-Government contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_e_7: CO must consider the service provider's qualifications and customary fees, especially non-Government fees.
Validation_Notes: Factor 7 of 8. Two sub-factors: qualifications AND fee reasonableness. Non-Government fee comparison helps detect Government-inflated pricing.

Natural_Language: Adequacy of the contractual agreement for the service (e.g., description of the service, estimate of time required, rate of compensation, termination provisions).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_e_8: CO must consider adequacy of the service agreement (service description, time estimate, compensation rate, termination provisions).
Validation_Notes: Factor 8 of 8. Contractual documentation quality. 'E.g.' list is illustrative of agreement elements to evaluate.

Natural_Language: Retainer fees are allowable when supported by evidence that (1) services are necessary and customary, (2) past services justify fee amount, (3) fee is reasonable vs. in-house capability, (4) actual services are documented per (i)-(ii).
Validation_Notes: Four conjunctive evidence requirements for retainer fee allowability. All must be supported. Evidence-based test, not a brightline rule.

Natural_Language: The services covered by the retainer agreement are necessary and customary.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_f_1: Evidence must show services under retainer are necessary and customary.
Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive requirements: necessary AND customary. Both must be demonstrated.

Natural_Language: The level of past services justifies the amount of the retainer fees (if no services were rendered, fees are not automatically unallowable).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_f_2: Past service levels must justify retainer fee amount; however, absence of services rendered does not automatically make fees unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Two-part test. General rule: past services must justify fees. Exception: no-service periods don't automatically disqualify. Protects legitimate retainer arrangements with intermittent service needs.

Natural_Language: The retainer fee is reasonable in comparison with maintaining an in-house capability to perform the covered services, when factors such as cost and level of expertise are considered.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_f_3: Retainer fee must be reasonable compared to in-house capability costs, considering cost and expertise level.
Validation_Notes: Make-or-buy reasonableness test for retainer fees. Multi-factor comparison: cost and expertise at minimum.

Natural_Language: The actual services performed are documented in accordance with the following: (i) fees supported by evidence, (ii) evidence of propriety and legality.
Validation_Notes: Documentation requirement with two sub-requirements. Both must be satisfied.

Natural_Language: Fees for services rendered are allowable only when supported by evidence of the nature and scope of the service furnished (see also 31.205-38(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_33_f_4_i: Service fees allowable only when supported by evidence of nature and scope of service furnished.
Validation_Notes: Only when' = necessary condition. No evidence of service nature/scope means fees are not allowable. Cross-references 31.205-38(c) for selling costs.

Natural_Language: Evidence necessary to determine that work performed is proper, does not violate law or regulation, and includes: (A) details of all agreements with service providers, (B) invoices/billings with sufficient detail, (C) work products and related documents.
Validation_Notes: Evidence must demonstrate propriety and legality. Three conjunctive documentation requirements (A-C). Note: sub-items A, B, C may need skeleton ID additions during Phase 3 atomic decomposition per known skeleton notes.

Natural_Language: 31.205-34 Recruitment costs. Certain recruitment costs are allowable (paragraph (a)), and help-wanted advertising is unallowable under specific conditions (paragraph (b)).
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Allowable recruitment costs and unallowable advertising conditions.

Natural_Language: The following costs are allowable: (1) employment agencies, (2) employment offices, (3) testing programs, (4) recruiter travel, (5) applicant travel, (6) help-wanted advertising.
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive list of allowable recruitment costs. Each independently allowable. Note: (6) help-wanted advertising subject to (b) restrictions.

Natural_Language: Costs for employment agencies, not in excess of standard commercial rates.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_34_a_1: Employment agency costs are allowable when not exceeding standard commercial rates.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Allowable with rate cap: must not exceed standard commercial rates. Excess above standard rates would be unallowable.

Natural_Language: Costs of operating an employment office needed to secure and maintain an adequate labor force.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_34_a_2: Costs of operating an employment office to secure and maintain adequate labor force are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Needed' qualifier requires the office to be genuinely necessary for labor force adequacy.

Natural_Language: Costs of operating an aptitude and educational testing program.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_34_a_3: Costs of aptitude and educational testing programs are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Straightforward allowability for recruitment-related testing programs.

Natural_Language: Travel costs of employees engaged in recruiting personnel.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_34_a_4: Travel costs of employees engaged in recruiting are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Allowable travel costs for employees performing recruitment duties.

Natural_Language: Travel costs of applicants for interviews.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_34_a_5: Applicant interview travel costs are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Allowable travel costs for job applicants attending interviews.

Natural_Language: Costs of help-wanted advertising.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_34_a_6: Help-wanted advertising costs are allowable (subject to restrictions in paragraph (b)).
Validation_Notes: Generally allowable but subject to (b) restrictions. Must be read in conjunction with (b).

Natural_Language: Help-wanted advertising costs are unallowable if the advertising (1) does not describe specific positions or classes of positions, or (2) includes irrelevant recruitment material.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive disqualifiers for help-wanted advertising. Either condition independently makes the advertising cost unallowable.

Natural_Language: Does not describe specific positions or classes of positions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_34_b_1: Help-wanted advertising that does not describe specific positions or position classes is unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Advertising must be position-specific. Generic brand advertising disguised as recruitment is unallowable.

Natural_Language: Includes material that is not relevant for recruitment purposes, such as extensive illustrations or descriptions of the company's products or capabilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_34_b_2: Help-wanted advertising containing irrelevant non-recruitment material (e.g., extensive product/capability descriptions) is unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Prevents using recruitment advertising as disguised corporate advertising. 'Such as' list is illustrative. Key test: relevance to recruitment purpose.

Natural_Language: 31.205-35 Relocation costs. Defines allowable relocation costs (a), allowability criteria (b), unallowable costs (c), refund requirement (d), mass/special movements (e), and contract-specific employee relocation (f).
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Six paragraphs covering all aspects of relocation cost allowability.

Natural_Language: Relocation costs are costs incident to the permanent change of assigned work location (for a period of 12 months or more) of an existing employee or upon recruitment of a new employee. The following types of relocation costs are allowable: (1)-(12).
Formal_Logic_Statement: PermanentRelocation(>=12months) ^ (ExistingEmployee v NewRecruit) -> (P_31_205_35_a_1 v P_31_205_35_a_2 v ... v P_31_205_35_a_12) -> Allowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Definition of relocation costs (permanent change >= 12 months) and disjunctive list of 12 allowable cost types. Threshold trigger: permanent assignment change. Each sub-type independently allowable.

Natural_Language: Costs of travel of the employee and members of the employee's immediate family (see 31.205-46) and transportation of household items and personal effects to the new location.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_1: Travel costs for employee and immediate family, plus transportation of household goods/personal effects, are allowable relocation costs.
Validation_Notes: Two cost categories: personal travel and household goods transportation. Cross-references 31.205-46 for travel cost standards.

Natural_Language: Costs of finding a new home, such as advance trips by the employee and/or the spouse, to locate living quarters, and temporary lodging during the transition period for the employee and members of the employee's immediate family.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_2: House-hunting costs (advance trips for employee/spouse to locate housing) and temporary lodging during transition are allowable relocation costs.
Validation_Notes: Two cost categories: house-hunting trips and transition-period temporary lodging. 'Such as' indicates illustrative examples. Family included in temporary lodging.

Natural_Language: Closing costs incident to the disposition of the actual residence owned by the employee when notified of the transfer (e.g., brokerage fees, legal fees, appraisal fees, points, and finance charges), except that these costs, when added to the costs described in paragraph (a)(4) of this section, must not exceed 14 percent of the sales price of the property sold.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_3: Closing costs for selling employee's residence upon transfer notification are allowable, except total of (a)(3) plus (a)(4) costs must not exceed 14% of sales price.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Allowable with cap. The 14% cap is combined with (a)(4) continuing ownership costs. 'E.g.' list of closing cost types is illustrative. 'Actual residence' limits to primary residence.

Natural_Language: Continuing costs of ownership of the vacant former actual residence being sold, such as maintenance of building and grounds (exclusive of fixing up expenses), utilities, taxes, property insurance, and mortgage interest, after the settlement date or lease date of a new permanent residence, except that these costs, when added to the costs described in paragraph (a)(3) of this section, must not exceed 14 percent of the sales price of the property sold.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_4: Continuing ownership costs of vacant former residence after settling into new residence are allowable (excluding fixing-up expenses), subject to combined 14% cap with (a)(3).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Multiple conditions: vacant former residence, after new settlement, excludes fixing-up expenses. Combined 14% cap with (a)(3). 'Such as' list is illustrative. Triggered after new residence settlement/lease date.

Natural_Language: The cost of a mortgage title policy is allowable if it is a cost incident to acquiring a home in a new location.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_5: Mortgage title policy costs are allowable when incident to acquiring a home in the new location.
Validation_Notes: Conditional allowability: must be incident to new home acquisition. Title policies for other purposes not covered.

Natural_Language: Other necessary and reasonable expenses normally incident to relocation, such as disconnecting and connecting household appliances; automobile registration; driver's license and use taxes; cutting and fitting rugs, draperies, and curtains; forfeited utility fees and deposits; and purchase of insurance against damage to or loss of personal property while in transit.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_6: Other necessary and reasonable miscellaneous relocation expenses are allowable (e.g., appliance connect/disconnect, auto registration, forfeited deposits, in-transit insurance).
Validation_Notes: Three qualifying conditions: necessary AND reasonable AND normally incident. 'Such as' list is illustrative catch-all. Subject to lump-sum alternative in (b)(5).

Natural_Language: Costs incident to acquiring a home in the new work location, except that (i) not allowable for non-homeowners, (ii) total must not exceed 5% of purchase price.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Allowable with two exceptions as restrictive conditions. Must satisfy both: was a homeowner AND within 5% cap.

Natural_Language: These costs are not allowable for existing employees or newly recruited employees who were not homeowners before the relocation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_7_i: Home acquisition costs at new location are not allowable for employees (existing or new) who were not homeowners before relocation.
Validation_Notes: Pre-relocation homeownership is a prerequisite. First-time homebuyers cannot claim these costs as allowable relocation expenses.

Natural_Language: The total costs must not exceed 5 percent of the purchase price of the new home.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_7_ii: Total home acquisition costs in new location must not exceed 5% of the new home's purchase price.
Validation_Notes: Hard cap at 5% of new home purchase price. 'Must not exceed' = mandatory ceiling.

Natural_Language: Mortgage interest differential payments, except that these costs are not allowable for existing or newly recruited employees who, before the relocation, were not homeowners and the total payments are limited to an amount determined as follows: (i) calculation method, (ii) lump-sum adjustment.
Validation_Notes: Allowable with same homeownership prerequisite as (a)(7)(i). Payment amount limited by formula in (i) and subject to pro-rata adjustment per (ii).

Natural_Language: The difference between the mortgage interest rates of the old and new residences times the current balance of the old mortgage times 3 years.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_8_i: Mortgage differential payment limit = (old rate - new rate) x old mortgage balance x 3 years.
Validation_Notes: Mathematical formula for calculating maximum mortgage differential payment. Three-year multiplier caps the benefit period.

Natural_Language: When mortgage differential payments are made on a lump-sum basis and the employee leaves or is transferred again in less than 3 years, the amount initially recognized must be proportionately adjusted to reflect payments only for the actual time of the relocation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_8_ii: When lump-sum mortgage differential payments are made and employee leaves/transfers within 3 years, the amount must be proportionately adjusted to actual relocation time.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Clawback mechanism. Three conjunctive triggers: lump-sum basis AND departure/transfer AND within 3 years. 'Must' = mandatory pro-rata adjustment.

Natural_Language: Rental differential payments covering situations where relocated employees retain ownership of a vacated home in the old location and rent at the new location. The rented quarters at the new location must be comparable to those vacated, and the allowable differential payments may not exceed the actual rental costs for the new home, less the fair market rent for the vacated home times 3 years.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_9: Rental differential payments are allowable when employee retains old home and rents at new location, limited to (new rent - old home FMR) x 3 years, with comparable quarters requirement.
Formal_Logic_Statement: RetainOldHome ^ RentAtNew ^ ComparableQuarters -> RentalDifferentialAllowable; DiffPayment -> ~Exceed((NewRent - OldFMR) * 3)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Three conditions: retain old home, rent at new, comparable quarters. Payment cap formula: (actual new rent - FMR of vacated home) x 3 years. Comparable quarters is a judgment standard.

Natural_Language: Costs of canceling an unexpired lease.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_10: Costs of canceling an unexpired lease due to relocation are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Straightforward allowability for lease cancellation costs incident to relocation.

Natural_Language: Payments for increased employee income or Federal Insurance Contributions Act (26 U.S.C. chapter 21) taxes incident to allowable reimbursed relocation costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_11: Tax gross-up payments (income taxes and FICA) on allowable reimbursed relocation costs are allowable.
Validation_Notes: Allowable only when incident to 'allowable reimbursed' relocation costs. Tax gross-ups on unallowable relocation costs would not qualify.

Natural_Language: Payments for spouse employment assistance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_a_12: Spouse employment assistance payments are allowable relocation costs.
Validation_Notes: Straightforward allowability for spouse employment assistance in relocation context.

Natural_Language: The costs in paragraph (a) of this section must meet the following criteria to be considered allowable: (1) employer benefit, (2) established policy, (3) not otherwise unallowable, (4) actual expense limit, (5) miscellaneous lump-sum, (6) lump-sum reimbursement options.
Validation_Notes: Four mandatory conjunctive criteria (b)(1)-(4) that all (a) costs must meet. (b)(5) and (b)(6) provide additional procedural options/modifications. 'Must meet' = all required.

Natural_Language: The move must be for the benefit of the employer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_b_1: Relocation must be for employer's benefit to be allowable.
Validation_Notes: Must' = mandatory prerequisite. Employee-initiated moves for personal reasons would not satisfy this criterion.

Natural_Language: Reimbursement must be in accordance with an established policy or practice that is consistently followed by the employer and is designed to motivate employees to relocate promptly and economically.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_b_2: Reimbursement must follow an established, consistently applied policy designed to motivate prompt and economical relocation.
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive requirements: established policy, consistent application, and design purpose (prompt and economical). Ad hoc or inconsistent reimbursement fails this test.

Natural_Language: The costs must not be otherwise unallowable under subpart 31.2.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_b_3: Relocation costs must not be separately unallowable under Subpart 31.2.
Validation_Notes: Cross-check requirement against all other cost principles in Subpart 31.2. A cost cannot become allowable merely because it is incident to relocation if it is separately prohibited.

Natural_Language: Amounts to be reimbursed must not exceed the employee's actual expenses, except as provided for in paragraphs (b)(5) and (b)(6) of this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_b_4: Reimbursement must not exceed actual expenses, except as modified by (b)(5) and (b)(6).
Justification_Rules: Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Actual expense ceiling with two exceptions: (b)(5) miscellaneous lump-sum and (b)(6) specific lump-sum options. 'Must not exceed' = hard cap absent exceptions.

Natural_Language: For miscellaneous costs of the type discussed in paragraph (a)(6) of this subsection, a lump-sum amount, not to exceed $5,000, may be allowed in lieu of actual costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_b_5: For miscellaneous relocation costs per (a)(6), a lump-sum up to $5,000 may be allowed instead of actual costs.
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive (tautology). $5,000 cap on lump-sum alternative for (a)(6) miscellaneous costs. Simplifies administration but is discretionary.

Natural_Language: Lump-sum reimbursement options for certain relocation costs when adequately supported, per (i) and (ii).
Validation_Notes: Sub-parent for lump-sum reimbursement rules. Both (i) scope and (ii) adjustment prohibition apply.

Natural_Language: Reimbursement on a lump-sum basis may be allowed for any of the following relocation costs when adequately supported by data on the individual elements (e.g., transportation, lodging, and meals) comprising the build-up of the lump-sum amount to be paid based on the circumstances of the particular employee's relocation: (A) finding a new home per (a)(2), (B) travel to new location per (a)(1) (excluding household goods), (C) temporary lodging per (a)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_b_6_i: Lump-sum reimbursement may be allowed for (A) house-hunting, (B) travel to new location (not household goods), (C) temporary lodging, when supported by element-level data.
Formal_Logic_Statement: AdequateDataSupport -> (LumpSumForHouseHunting v LumpSumForTravel v LumpSumForTempLodging) -> (MayAllow v ~MayAllow)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: May' = permissive. Key requirement: adequate data support showing element-level build-up. Three specific cost types eligible. Household goods excluded from (B). Sub-items (A), (B), (C) are captured within this proposition rather than separate skeleton IDs.

Natural_Language: When reimbursement on a lump-sum basis is used, any adjustments to reflect actual costs are unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_b_6_ii: When lump-sum reimbursement is used, adjustments to reflect actual costs are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Anti-cherry-picking rule. Once lump-sum is chosen, cannot later adjust to actual costs (whether higher or lower). Election is binding.

Natural_Language: The following types of costs are unallowable: (1) loss on home sale, (2) certain home acquisition costs at new location, (3) continuing mortgage payments, (4) employee loan costs.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive list of categorically unallowable relocation costs. Each independently unallowable.

Natural_Language: Loss on the sale of a home.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_c_1: Loss on the sale of an employee's home due to relocation is unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition. Government does not bear market risk on employee home values.

Natural_Language: Costs incident to acquiring a home in the new location as follows: (i)-(vi).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Six types of unallowable home acquisition costs. Disjunctive: each independently unallowable. Note distinction from (a)(7) which allows some acquisition costs with caps.

Natural_Language: Real estate brokers' fees and commissions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_c_2_i: Real estate broker fees and commissions for new home acquisition are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Unallowable for new home acquisition. Note: broker fees for selling old home may be allowable under (a)(3) closing costs.

Natural_Language: Costs of litigation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_c_2_ii: Litigation costs for new home acquisition are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition on litigation costs in new home acquisition context.

Natural_Language: Real and personal property insurance against damage or loss of property.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_c_2_iii: Property insurance (real and personal) for new home is unallowable as acquisition cost.
Validation_Notes: Covers both real property and personal property insurance at new location.

Natural_Language: Mortgage life insurance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_c_2_iv: Mortgage life insurance for new home is unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition on mortgage life insurance as relocation cost.

Natural_Language: Owner's title policy insurance when such insurance was not previously carried by the employee on the old residence.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_c_2_v: Owner's title policy insurance is unallowable when employee did not carry it on old residence.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional prohibition. If employee had title insurance on old home, new home title insurance may be allowable (compare (a)(5)). Only unallowable when it represents a new expense the employee didn't previously carry.

Natural_Language: Property taxes and operating or maintenance costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_c_2_vi: Property taxes and operating/maintenance costs for new home acquisition are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Ongoing costs of new home ownership are unallowable as relocation costs. These are normal living expenses.

Natural_Language: Continuing mortgage principal payments on a residence being sold.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_c_3: Continuing mortgage principal payments on residence being sold are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Mortgage principal payments are equity-building, not relocation costs. Note: mortgage interest on old home may be allowable under (a)(4).

Natural_Language: Costs incident to furnishing equity or nonequity loans to employees or making arrangements with lenders for employees to obtain lower-than-market rate mortgage loans.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_c_4: Costs of providing employee loans or arranging below-market mortgage rates are unallowable.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Two disjunctive unallowable cost types: direct employee loans and below-market mortgage arrangements. Prevents subsidized financing from being charged as relocation.

Natural_Language: If relocation costs for an employee have been allowed as an allocable indirect or direct cost, and the employee resigns within 12 months for reasons within the employee's control, the contractor must refund or credit the relocation costs to the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_d: When relocation costs were allowed and employee resigns within 12 months for controllable reasons, contractor must refund/credit those costs to Government.
Validation_Notes: Clawback provision. Three conjunctive triggers: costs were allowed AND resignation within 12 months AND employee-controlled reasons. 'Must' = mandatory refund/credit. Key: 'within the employee's control' excludes involuntary departures.

Natural_Language: Subject to the requirements of this section, the costs of family movements and of personnel movements of a special or mass nature are allowable. The cost, however, should be assigned on the basis of work (contracts) or time period benefited.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_e_a: Family movements and special/mass personnel movements are allowable subject to this section; P_31_205_35_e_b: Cost allocation should be based on work/contracts or time period benefited.
Validation_Notes: Two parts: (1) allowability for family/mass movements subject to section requirements, (2) advisory cost allocation method. 'Should' = advisory for allocation method. PENDING_REVIEW for advisory language.

Natural_Language: Relocation costs (both outgoing and return) of employees who are hired for performance on specific contracts or long-term field projects are allowable if conditions (1)-(4) are met. (5) addresses return costs for released employees.
Validation_Notes: Four conjunctive conditions for contract-specific employee relocation. All four must be met. (5) provides an additional rule for return costs. Covers both outgoing and return relocation.

Natural_Language: Term of employment is 12 months or more.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_f_1: Employment term must be 12 months or more for contract-specific relocation to be allowable.
Validation_Notes: Minimum duration threshold. Consistent with (a) definition of permanent relocation.

Natural_Language: Employment agreement specifically limits the duration of employment to the time spent on the contract or field project for which the employee is hired.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_f_2: Employment agreement must specifically limit employment duration to the contract/project period.
Validation_Notes: Specifically limits' requires explicit contractual language, not implied limitation.

Natural_Language: Employment agreement provides for return relocation to the employee's permanent and principal home immediately prior to the outgoing relocation, or other location of equal or lesser cost.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_f_3: Employment agreement must provide for return relocation to employee's pre-relocation home or equivalent/lesser-cost location.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Two-part condition: agreement must provide return relocation AND destination must be original home or equal/lesser-cost alternative. Prevents relocation cost escalation.
