Natural_Language: Relocation costs are determined in accordance with this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_f_4: Relocation costs must comply with all requirements of section 31.205-35.
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference condition ensuring all other section requirements apply to contract-specific relocations.

Natural_Language: The costs to return employees, who are released from employment upon completion of field assignments pursuant to their employment agreements, are not subject to the refund or credit requirement of paragraph (d) of this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_35_f_5: Return relocation costs for employees released upon field assignment completion per their agreements are exempt from the (d) refund/credit requirement.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Exception to (d) clawback. Two conditions: released upon completion AND per employment agreement. Protects employees who leave as contractually planned.

Natural_Language: Rental costs. This section establishes cost principles for rental costs, covering operating leases, sale-leaseback arrangements, interorganizational charges, and unexpired lease terminations.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating applicability, allowable rental costs, and termination lease costs. All subsections collectively define the rental cost principle.

Natural_Language: This section is applicable to the cost of renting or leasing real or personal property acquired under operating leases as defined in Financial Accounting Standards Board's Accounting Standards Codification (FASB ASC) 842, Leases. (See 31.205-11 for capital leases.)
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_a_a: Section applies to operating lease rental/leasing costs for real or personal property as defined by FASB ASC 842; P_31_205_36_a_b: Capital leases are addressed under 31.205-11
Validation_Notes: Scope-setting provision. Defines coverage as operating leases per FASB ASC 842. Cross-reference to 31.205-11 for capital leases establishes mutual exclusivity of coverage.

Natural_Language: The following costs are allowable--
Validation_Notes: Parent for allowable rental cost categories. All four subcategories are independently allowable when their respective conditions are met.

Natural_Language: Rental costs under operating leases, when the rates are reasonable at the time of the lease decision, after consideration of rental costs of comparable property, market conditions, property type/life/condition/value, alternatives available, and other agreement provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_b_1 = P_31_205_36_b_1_a: Operating lease rental costs are allowable when rates are reasonable at lease decision time; P_31_205_36_b_1_b: Reasonableness requires consideration of factors in (i)-(v)
Validation_Notes: Conditional allowability tied to reasonableness at time of lease decision. The five subfactors are conjunctive considerations (all must be evaluated). HIGH-RISK: implication used to link factor consideration to reasonableness determination.

Natural_Language: Rental costs of comparable property, if any;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_b_1_i: Consideration of rental costs of comparable property as factor in reasonableness determination
Validation_Notes: Atomic factor for reasonableness evaluation. "If any" qualifier acknowledges comparable property may not always exist.

Natural_Language: Market conditions in the area;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_b_1_ii: Consideration of market conditions in the area as factor in reasonableness determination
Validation_Notes: Atomic factor for reasonableness evaluation. Local market conditions must be assessed.

Natural_Language: The type, life expectancy, condition, and value of the property leased;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_b_1_iii: Consideration of property type, life expectancy, condition, and value as factor in reasonableness determination
Validation_Notes: Atomic factor. Four property attributes (type, life expectancy, condition, value) are conjunctive sub-considerations within this single factor.

Natural_Language: Alternatives available; and
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_b_1_iv: Consideration of available alternatives as factor in reasonableness determination
Validation_Notes: Atomic factor for reasonableness evaluation. Requires consideration of lease alternatives.

Natural_Language: Other provisions of the agreement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_b_1_v: Consideration of other agreement provisions as factor in reasonableness determination
Validation_Notes: Catch-all factor. Allows consideration of any other lease agreement provisions bearing on reasonableness.

Natural_Language: Rental costs under a sale and leaseback arrangement only up to the amount the contractor would be allowed if the contractor retained title, and the computation of which is based on the net book value of the asset on the date the contractor becomes a lessee of the property adjusted for any gain or loss recognized in accordance with 31.205-16(b).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_b_2_a: Sale-leaseback rental costs are allowable; P_31_205_36_b_2_b: Limited to the amount allowable had contractor retained title; P_31_205_36_b_2_c: Computation based on net book value at lessee date adjusted per 31.205-16(b)
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive requirement: allowability capped at retained-title equivalent, computed from net book value with gain/loss adjustment per 31.205-16(b). Prevents contractors from inflating costs through sale-leaseback structures.

Natural_Language: Charges in the nature of rent for property between any divisions, subsidiaries, or organization under common control, to the extent that they do not exceed normal ownership costs and provided no duplication of other allowed costs.
Validation_Notes: Parent for interorganizational rental charges. Both conditions (cost ceiling and no duplication) must be satisfied conjunctively.

Natural_Language: To the extent that they do not exceed the normal costs of ownership, such as depreciation, taxes, insurance, facilities capital cost of money, and maintenance (excluding interest or other unallowable costs pursuant to part 31);
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_b_3_i_a: Interorg rental charges allowable up to normal ownership costs; P_31_205_36_b_3_i_b: Normal ownership costs include depreciation, taxes, insurance, facilities capital cost of money, maintenance; P_31_205_36_b_3_i_c: Interest and other Part 31 unallowable costs excluded
Validation_Notes: Cost ceiling set at normal ownership costs. Enumerated examples are illustrative. Interest and Part 31 unallowable costs explicitly excluded via negation.

Natural_Language: Provided that no part of such costs must duplicate any other allowed cost.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_b_3_ii: No duplication of any other allowed cost is permitted
Validation_Notes: Anti-duplication provision. Mandatory prohibition ("must") on cost duplication.

Natural_Language: Rental cost of personal property leased from any division, subsidiary, or affiliate of the contractor under common control, that has an established practice of leasing the same or similar property to unaffiliated lessees must be allowed in accordance with paragraph (b)(1) of this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_b_4_a: Personal property leased from related entity under common control; P_31_205_36_b_4_b: Related entity has established practice of leasing to unaffiliated lessees; P_31_205_36_b_4_c: Must be allowed per (b)(1) reasonableness standards
Validation_Notes: Conditional: when related entity has established leasing practice, the (b)(1) reasonableness test applies (not the (b)(3) ownership-cost ceiling). HIGH-RISK implication. This carves out an exception to (b)(3) for entities that are genuine leasing businesses.

Natural_Language: The allowability of rental costs under unexpired leases in connection with terminations is subject to 31.205-42(e).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_36_c: Unexpired lease rental costs related to contract terminations governed by 31.205-42(e)
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference delegation. Rental costs under unexpired leases in termination context are entirely governed by 31.205-42(e). HIGH-RISK: implication used for cross-reference dependency.

Natural_Language: Royalties and other costs for use of patents. This section establishes cost principles for royalties on patents and patent rights, including conditions for allowability, reasonableness considerations for less-than-arms-length transactions, and limitations on formerly owned patents.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating allowability rules, reasonableness considerations, and formerly-owned patent limitations.

Natural_Language: Royalties on a patent or amortization of the cost of purchasing a patent or patent rights necessary for the proper performance of the contract and applicable to contract products or processes are allowable unless the Government has a license or right to free use, the patent has been adjudicated/administratively determined invalid, the patent is considered unenforceable, or the patent is expired.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_37_a_a: Royalties/amortization on patents necessary for contract performance and applicable to contract products/processes are allowable; P_31_205_37_a_b: Subject to exceptions in (a)(1)-(4)
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Default allowability with disjunctive exceptions. Any one of the four exceptions triggers unallowability. "Unless" maps to negated disjunction.

Natural_Language: The Government has a license or the right to a free use of the patent;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_37_a_1: Government has license or right to free use of the patent
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive exception: either a license OR a right to free use triggers unallowability of the royalty.

Natural_Language: The patent has been adjudicated to be invalid, or has been administratively determined to be invalid;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_37_a_2: Patent adjudicated invalid or administratively determined invalid
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive exception: judicial or administrative invalidity finding either suffices.

Natural_Language: The patent is considered to be unenforceable; or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_37_a_3: Patent is considered unenforceable
Validation_Notes: Atomic exception. Unenforceability determination makes royalty unallowable.

Natural_Language: The patent is expired.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_37_a_4: Patent is expired
Validation_Notes: Atomic exception. Expired patent royalties are unallowable.

Natural_Language: Care should be exercised in determining reasonableness when the royalties may have been arrived at as a result of less-than-arm's-length bargaining, including royalties paid to affiliated persons, paid to unaffiliated parties under agreements in contemplation of Government contract award, or paid under post-award agreements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_37_b_a: Care should be exercised in determining reasonableness for less-than-arms-length royalties; P_31_205_37_b_b: Includes scenarios in (b)(1)-(3)
Validation_Notes: Advisory provision ("should"). Less-than-arms-length bargaining triggers heightened reasonableness scrutiny. HIGH-RISK implication. "Should" = advisory, not binding, per modal verb mapping.

Natural_Language: Paid to persons, including corporations, affiliated with the contractor;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_37_b_1: Royalties paid to persons/corporations affiliated with the contractor
Validation_Notes: Atomic scenario triggering heightened reasonableness scrutiny. Affiliated party payments.

Natural_Language: Paid to unaffiliated parties, including corporations, under an agreement entered into in contemplation that a Government contract would be awarded; or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_37_b_2: Royalties paid to unaffiliated parties under agreement contemplating Government contract award
Validation_Notes: Atomic scenario. Pre-award agreements with unaffiliated parties in anticipation of Government work.

Natural_Language: Paid under an agreement entered into after the contract award.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_37_b_3: Royalties paid under post-award agreement
Validation_Notes: Atomic scenario. Post-award royalty agreements warrant heightened scrutiny.

Natural_Language: The royalty amount allowed for a patent formerly owned by a contractor should not exceed the cost that would have been allowed had the contractor retained title.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_37_c: Royalty for formerly owned patent limited to cost allowable had contractor retained title
Validation_Notes: Advisory limitation ("should"). Prevents windfall from divesting then licensing back a patent. Cost ceiling = what depreciation/amortization would have been. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Selling costs. This section establishes cost principles for selling costs, categorizing selling activities and their respective allowability rules, with a specific provision for seller/agent compensation.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating scope/unallowability rule, selling activity categories, and seller compensation provision.

Natural_Language: Parent for selling cost scope and default unallowability rule.
Validation_Notes: Parent for (a)(1) scope definition and (a)(2) default unallowability.

Natural_Language: Selling encompasses all efforts to market the contractor's products or services, some of which are addressed in other sections of 31.205.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_38_a_1: Selling = all efforts to market contractor products/services; some addressed in other 31.205 sections
Validation_Notes: Definitional/scope. Establishes that selling is broadly defined and cross-references other cost principles.

Natural_Language: The costs of any selling efforts other than those addressed in this cost principle are unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_38_a_2: Selling costs not addressed in 31.205-38 are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Default unallowability for selling costs not covered by this section. Strong gatekeeper provision. HIGH-RISK: double negation in implication.

Natural_Language: Selling activity includes the following broad categories: Advertising, Corporate image enhancement, Bid and proposal costs, Market planning, Direct selling.
Validation_Notes: Parent categorizing five selling activity types. Each delegates to its own allowability provision.

Natural_Language: Advertising. Advertising is defined at 31.205-1(b), and advertising costs are subject to the allowability provisions of 31.205-1(d) and (f).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_38_b_1_a: Advertising defined at 31.205-1(b); P_31_205_38_b_1_b: Advertising costs subject to 31.205-1(d) and (f)
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference delegation. Definition and allowability both governed by 31.205-1.

Natural_Language: Corporate image enhancement. Corporate image enhancement activities, including broadly targeted sales efforts, other than advertising, are included within the definition of public relations at 31.205-1(a), and the costs of such efforts are subject to the allowability provisions at 31.205-1(e) and (f).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_38_b_2_a: Corporate image enhancement (non-advertising broadly targeted sales) defined as public relations per 31.205-1(a); P_31_205_38_b_2_b: Costs subject to 31.205-1(e) and (f)
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference delegation to public relations cost principle. Distinguishes corporate image enhancement from advertising.

Natural_Language: Bid and proposal costs. Bid and proposal costs are defined at 31.205-18 and are subject to the allowability provisions of that section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_38_b_3: B&P costs defined and governed by 31.205-18
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference delegation. B&P costs entirely governed by 31.205-18.

Natural_Language: Market planning. Market planning involves market research and analysis and general management planning concerned with development of the contractor's business. Long-range market planning costs are subject to the allowability provisions of 31.205-12. Other market planning costs are allowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_38_b_4_a: Market planning = market research/analysis and general management planning for business development; P_31_205_38_b_4_b: Long-range market planning costs subject to 31.205-12; P_31_205_38_b_4_c: Other market planning costs are allowable
Validation_Notes: Bifurcated treatment: long-range market planning governed by 31.205-12 (IR&D/B&P), other market planning is directly allowable.

Natural_Language: Direct selling. Direct selling efforts are those acts or actions to induce particular customers to purchase particular products or services of the contractor. Direct selling is characterized by person-to-person contact and includes such efforts as familiarizing a potential customer with the contractor's products or services, conditions of sale, service capabilities, etc. It also includes negotiation, liaison between customer and contractor personnel, technical and consulting efforts, individual demonstrations, and any other efforts having as their purpose the application or adaptation of the contractor's products or services for a particular customer's use. The cost of direct selling efforts is allowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_38_b_5_a: Direct selling = acts to induce particular customers to purchase particular products/services; P_31_205_38_b_5_b: Characterized by person-to-person contact; P_31_205_38_b_5_c: Cost of direct selling efforts is allowable
Validation_Notes: Definitional provision with direct allowability conclusion. Direct selling is broadly defined with enumerated examples. HIGH-RISK: implication links definition to allowability.

Natural_Language: Notwithstanding any other limitation of this section, seller or agent compensation, fees, commissions, percentages, retainer or brokerage fees, whether or not contingent upon the award of contracts, are allowable only when paid to bona fide employees or established commercial or selling agencies maintained by the contractor for the purpose of securing business.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_38_c_a: Seller/agent compensation (fees, commissions, percentages, retainer, brokerage fees) whether or not contingent on award; P_31_205_38_c_b: Allowable only when paid to bona fide employees or established commercial/selling agencies maintained for securing business
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Override provision ("notwithstanding"). "Only when" = biconditional: allowable if and only if paid to bona fide employees or established agencies. HIGH-RISK: complex logic with biconditional. Anti-corruption provision preventing payments to sham entities.

Natural_Language: Service and warranty costs. This section defines service and warranty costs and establishes their allowability when consistent with contract terms.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating definition and allowability provisions.

Natural_Language: Service and warranty costs include those arising from the fulfillment of any contractual obligation of a contractor to provide services, such as installation, training, correcting defects in the products, replacing defective parts, and making refunds in the case of inadequate performance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_39_a: Service/warranty costs = costs from fulfilling contractual obligations for services (installation, training, defect correction, part replacement, refunds for inadequate performance)
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Enumerated examples are illustrative ("such as"), not exhaustive.

Natural_Language: When consistent with the terms of the contract, service and warranty costs are allowable. However, care should be exercised to avoid duplication of the allowance as an element of both estimated product cost and risk.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_39_b_a: Service/warranty costs allowable when consistent with contract terms; P_31_205_39_b_b: Care should be exercised to avoid duplication in both estimated product cost and risk
Validation_Notes: Conditional allowability plus advisory anti-duplication caution. "Should" in second clause = advisory. HIGH-RISK: implication for conditional allowability. The duplication warning prevents double-counting in both cost estimation and risk assessment.

Natural_Language: Special tooling and special test equipment costs. This section establishes cost principles for special tooling and test equipment, including allocation requirements, depreciation limitations, and adaptation costs.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating general allowability/allocation, depreciation limitation, and adaptation cost provisions.

Natural_Language: Except as provided in paragraph (b), the cost of special tooling and special test equipment used in performing one or more Government contracts is allowable and must be allocated to the specific Government contract or contracts for which it is acquired.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_40_a_a: Cost of special tooling/test equipment for Government contracts is allowable (except per (b)); P_31_205_40_a_b: Must be allocated to the specific Government contract(s) for which acquired
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: General rule with exception carve-out for (b). Allowability is default, but allocation to specific contracts is mandatory. HIGH-RISK: negated exception in antecedent.

Natural_Language: Depreciation or amortization is the only allowable cost for special tooling and special test equipment acquired or replaced before contract effective date (whether or not altered/adapted) or specifically excluded in the contract schedule.
Validation_Notes: Limitation: "only allowable cost" restricts to depreciation/amortization for two disjunctive scenarios. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Acquired or replaced by the contractor before the effective date of the contract, whether or not altered or adapted for use in performing the contract; or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_40_b_1: Special tooling/test equipment acquired or replaced before contract effective date, regardless of alteration/adaptation
Validation_Notes: Atomic condition. Pre-contract acquisition triggers depreciation-only limitation. "Whether or not" clause eliminates alteration as a distinguishing factor.

Natural_Language: Specifically excluded in the contract schedule.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_40_b_2: Special tooling/test equipment specifically excluded in the contract schedule
Validation_Notes: Atomic condition. Contract-specific exclusion triggers depreciation-only limitation.

Natural_Language: The cost to adapt contractor-owned special tooling or special test equipment for use under a contract is an allowable cost. The cost to return the equipment to its prior configuration is also an allowable cost.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_40_c_a: Cost to adapt contractor-owned special tooling/test equipment for contract use is allowable; P_31_205_40_c_b: Cost to return equipment to prior configuration is also allowable
Validation_Notes: Two independent allowability declarations. Both adaptation and restoration costs are allowable. Does not conflict with (b) because (b) addresses the equipment cost itself, not the adaptation cost.

Natural_Language: Taxes. This section establishes cost principles for tax costs, defining exemptions, specifying allowable and unallowable tax categories, allocation rules for property taxes, and refund/credit handling.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating definition, allowable taxes, unallowable taxes, allocation rules, and refund provisions.

Natural_Language: Definition. Exemption, as used in this section, means freedom from taxation, in whole or in part, and includes a tax abatement or reduction resulting from mode of assessment, method of calculation, or otherwise.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_a: "Exemption" defined as freedom from taxation (whole or partial), including abatements or reductions from assessment mode, calculation method, or otherwise
Validation_Notes: Definitional provision. Broad definition of "exemption" encompassing full and partial tax relief regardless of mechanism.

Natural_Language: The following types of costs are allowable:
Validation_Notes: Parent for allowable tax cost categories. Four independent allowable categories.

Natural_Language: Federal, State, and local taxes (see part 29) that are required to be and are paid or accrued in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_b_1_a: Federal, State, and local taxes; P_31_205_41_b_1_b: Required to be paid or accrued; P_31_205_41_b_1_c: In accordance with GAAP
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive requirement: taxes must be (1) federal/state/local, (2) legally required, and (3) GAAP-compliant in payment/accrual. Cross-reference to Part 29.

Natural_Language: Taxes otherwise allowable under paragraph (b)(1) of this section, but upon which a claim of illegality or erroneous assessment exists, are allowable provided the contractor, before paying such taxes, promptly requests instructions from the contracting officer and takes all directed action.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_b_2_a: Taxes allowable under (b)(1) with illegality/erroneous assessment claim; P_31_205_41_b_2_b: Allowable if contractor meets (i) and (ii) before paying
Validation_Notes: Conditional chain: disputed taxes allowable if contractor satisfies both procedural steps before payment. HIGH-RISK: nested implication via exportation.

Natural_Language: Promptly requests instructions from the contracting officer concerning such taxes; and
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_b_2_i: Contractor promptly requests CO instructions concerning the disputed taxes
Validation_Notes: Procedural requirement. "Promptly" introduces timeliness obligation. Must occur before tax payment.

Natural_Language: Takes all action directed by the contracting officer arising out of paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section or an independent decision of the Government as to the existence of a claim of illegality or erroneous assessment, to determine the legality of the assessment or secure a refund of such taxes.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_b_2_ii_a: Contractor takes all CO-directed action from (b)(2)(i) or independent Government decision; P_31_205_41_b_2_ii_b: Action purpose: determine legality (A) or secure refund (B)
Validation_Notes: Contractor must comply with CO direction. Disjunctive purpose: either legality determination or refund pursuit. Sub-paragraphs (A) and (B) captured as atomic disjuncts within this proposition.

Natural_Language: Interest or penalties incurred by the contractor for non-payment of any tax at the direction of the contracting officer or by reason of the failure of the contracting officer to ensure timely direction after a prompt request.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_b_3_a: Interest/penalties for non-payment at CO direction are allowable; P_31_205_41_b_3_b: Interest/penalties from CO failure to provide timely direction after prompt request are allowable
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive allowability: either CO-directed non-payment or CO failure to respond timely. Protects contractor from penalties caused by Government action/inaction.

Natural_Language: The Environmental Tax, also known as the Superfund Tax, (section 59A of the Internal Revenue Code).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_b_4: Environmental/Superfund Tax (IRC 59A) is allowable
Validation_Notes: Specific tax explicitly declared allowable.

Natural_Language: The following types of costs are not allowable:
Validation_Notes: Parent for unallowable tax cost categories. Eight independently unallowable tax types.

Natural_Language: Federal income and excess profits taxes.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_c_1: Federal income and excess profits taxes are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition. Federal income taxes and excess profits taxes both unallowable.

Natural_Language: Taxes in connection with financing, refinancing, refunding operations, or reorganizations (see 31.205-20 and 31.205-27).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_c_2: Taxes related to financing, refinancing, refunding, or reorganization are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition with cross-references to interest (31.205-20) and organization costs (31.205-27).

Natural_Language: Taxes from which exemptions are available to the contractor directly, or available to the contractor based on an exemption afforded the Government, except when the contracting officer determines that the administrative burden incident to obtaining the exemption outweighs the corresponding benefits accruing to the Government. When partial exemption from a tax is attributable to Government contract activity, taxes charged to such work in excess of that amount resulting from application of the preferential treatment. These provisions intend that the tax preference attributable to the Government contract activity be realized by the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_c_3_a: Taxes for which contractor has direct or Government-based exemption are unallowable; P_31_205_41_c_3_b: Exception when CO determines admin burden outweighs exemption benefit; P_31_205_41_c_3_c: Partial exemptions attributable to Government work must benefit the Government
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Complex provision with exception to the exception. Default: if exemption available, tax unallowable. Exception: CO cost-benefit override. Plus partial exemption pass-through rule. HIGH-RISK: nested conditional with negation. Policy intent: Government should benefit from tax preferences attributable to Government work.

Natural_Language: Special assessments on land that represent capital improvements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_c_4: Special assessments on land representing capital improvements are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition. Special assessments treated as capital, not operating costs.

Natural_Language: Taxes (including excises) on real or personal property, or on the value, use, possession or sale of such property, which is used solely in connection with work other than on Government contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_c_5: Property taxes/excises on property used solely for non-Government work are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Conditional: sole non-Government use triggers unallowability. Reasonable allocation principle. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Any excise tax in subtitle D, Chapter 43 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, which includes excise taxes imposed in connection with qualified pension plans, welfare plans, deferred compensation plans, or other similar types of plans.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_c_6: IRC Chapter 43 excise taxes (pension, welfare, deferred comp plans) are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition. These excise taxes typically arise from plan compliance failures, making them penalty-like.

Natural_Language: Income tax accruals designed to account for the tax effects of differences between taxable income and pretax income as reflected by the books of account and financial statements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_c_7: Income tax accruals for book-tax differences are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition. Deferred tax accruals (timing differences between book and tax income) are not allowable contract costs.

Natural_Language: Any tax imposed under 26 U.S.C. 5000C.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_c_8: Tax under 26 U.S.C. 5000C is unallowable
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition. 26 U.S.C. 5000C imposes tax on foreign persons receiving specified Federal procurement payments.

Natural_Language: Taxes on property used solely in connection with non-Government or Government work should be considered directly applicable to the respective category of work unless the amounts involved are insignificant or comparable results would otherwise be obtained.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_d_a: Property taxes for sole-use property should be directly charged to the respective work category; P_31_205_41_d_b: Exception if amounts insignificant or comparable results obtained otherwise
Validation_Notes: Advisory allocation rule ("should"). Direct charge is default for sole-use property taxes. Materiality exception with disjunctive triggers. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Taxes on contractor-owned work-in-process that is used solely in connection with non-Government work should be allocated to such work;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_d_1: WIP taxes for sole non-Government use should be allocated to non-Government work
Validation_Notes: Advisory ("should"). Direct allocation of WIP taxes to non-Government work. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Taxes on contractor-owned work-in-process inventory (and Government-owned work-in-process inventory when taxed) used solely in connection with Government work should be charged to such work; and
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_d_2: WIP taxes (contractor-owned and Government-owned when taxed) for sole Government use should be charged to Government work
Validation_Notes: Advisory ("should"). Parenthetical extends to Government-owned WIP when taxed. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: The cost of taxes incurred on property used in both Government and non-Government work must be apportioned to all such work based upon the use of such property on the respective final cost objectives.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_d_3: Taxes on dual-use property must be apportioned based on use on respective final cost objectives
Validation_Notes: Mandatory ("must"). Mixed-use property taxes apportioned by usage. Stronger obligation than (d)(1) and (d)(2) which use "should". HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Any taxes, interest, or penalties that were allowed as contract costs and are refunded to the contractor must be credited or paid to the Government as directed by the contracting officer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_e_a: Refunded taxes/interest/penalties previously allowed as contract costs; P_31_205_41_e_b: Must be credited or paid to Government per CO direction
Validation_Notes: Mandatory refund pass-through. Government recovers refunded amounts previously reimbursed. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: If a contractor or subcontractor obtains a foreign tax credit that reduces its Federal income tax return because of the payment of any tax or duty allowed as contract costs, and if those costs were reimbursed by a foreign government, the amount of the reduction must be paid to the United States Treasury at the time the Federal income tax return is filed.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_e_1_a: Foreign tax credit reduces Federal income tax from allowed contract cost taxes/duties; P_31_205_41_e_1_b: Those costs were reimbursed by foreign government; P_31_205_41_e_1_c: Reduction amount must be paid to US Treasury at filing time
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive antecedent: both conditions must be met. Prevents double recovery from both foreign government reimbursement and US tax credit. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Any interest actually paid or credited to a contractor incident to a refund of tax, interest, or penalty must be paid or credited to the Government only to the extent that such interest accrued over the period during which the contractor had been reimbursed by the Government for the taxes, interest, or penalties.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_41_e_2_a: Interest from tax/penalty refund must be paid/credited to Government; P_31_205_41_e_2_b: Limited to interest accrued during period of Government reimbursement
Validation_Notes: Mandatory pass-through with temporal limitation. Government only recovers interest for the period it was carrying the cost. Equitable result. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Termination costs. The following cost principles apply to contract terminations and are used in conjunction with the other cost principles in this subpart.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating eight termination cost subcategories. Used in conjunction with other Subpart 31.2 principles.

Natural_Language: Common items. The contracting officer should consider the contractor's plans and orders for current and planned production when determining if items can reasonably be used on other work of the contractor.
Validation_Notes: Parent with advisory guidance ("should"). CO must evaluate whether common items can be diverted to other contractor work.

Natural_Language: The costs of items reasonably usable on the contractor's other work must not be allowable unless the contractor submits evidence that the items could not be retained at cost without sustaining a loss.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_a_1_a: Items reasonably usable on other work are unallowable; P_31_205_42_a_1_b: Exception if contractor shows items cannot be retained at cost without loss
Validation_Notes: Default unallowability with loss-evidence exception. "Must not be allowable unless" = prohibition with escape clause. HIGH-RISK: conditional with negation.

Natural_Language: Contemporaneous purchases of common items by the contractor must be regarded as evidence that such items are reasonably usable on the contractor's other work.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_a_2: Contemporaneous purchases of common items are evidence of reasonable usability on other work
Validation_Notes: Evidentiary presumption. "Must be regarded" = mandatory inference. Creates rebuttable presumption that buying the same items means they are usable elsewhere. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Any acceptance of common items as allocable to the terminated portion of the contract should be limited to the extent that the quantities of such items on hand, in transit, and on order are in excess of the reasonable quantitative requirements of other work.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_a_3: Allocation of common items to terminated contract limited to quantities exceeding other work requirements
Validation_Notes: Advisory ("should"). Only excess quantities allocable to terminated contract. Items needed for other work cannot be charged to termination. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Costs continuing after termination.
Validation_Notes: Parent for continuing costs: allowable if unavoidable, unallowable if from negligence/willfulness.

Natural_Language: Despite all reasonable efforts by the contractor, costs that cannot be discontinued immediately after the effective date of termination are generally allowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_b_1_a: Contractor made all reasonable efforts; P_31_205_42_b_1_b: Costs cannot be immediately discontinued; P_31_205_42_b_1_c: Such costs generally allowable
Validation_Notes: Conditional allowability. "Generally" introduces qualification. Both reasonable effort and inability to discontinue required. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Costs continuing after the effective date of the termination due to the negligent or willful failure of the contractor to discontinue the costs must be unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_b_2: Continuing costs from negligent or willful failure to discontinue are unallowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Mandatory unallowability ("must"). Disjunctive trigger: negligence OR willfulness. Counterpart to (b)(1). HIGH-RISK: implication with negation.

Natural_Language: Initial costs. Initial costs, including starting load and preparatory costs, are allowable as follows:
Validation_Notes: Parent for initial/startup costs in termination. Five provisions covering definitions, constraints, and allocation.

Natural_Language: Starting load costs, not fully absorbed because of termination, are nonrecurring labor, material, and related overhead costs incurred in the early part of production and result from factors such as excessive spoilage, idle time, training, and lack of familiarity.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_c_1_a: Starting load costs not fully absorbed due to termination; P_31_205_42_c_1_b: Defined as nonrecurring labor, material, and overhead in early production; P_31_205_42_c_1_c: Result from factors in (i)-(iv)
Validation_Notes: Definitional provision. "Such as" = illustrative factors (disjunctive). Starting load costs are a specific category of initial costs.

Natural_Language: Excessive spoilage due to inexperienced labor;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_c_1_i: Excessive spoilage from inexperienced labor as starting load factor
Validation_Notes: Atomic illustrative factor for starting load costs.

Natural_Language: Idle time and subnormal production due to testing and changing production methods;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_c_1_ii: Idle time and subnormal production from testing/changing production methods as starting load factor
Validation_Notes: Atomic illustrative factor for starting load costs.

Natural_Language: Training; and
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_c_1_iii: Training as starting load factor
Validation_Notes: Atomic illustrative factor for starting load costs.

Natural_Language: Lack of familiarity or experience with the product, materials, or manufacturing processes.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_c_1_iv: Lack of product/material/process familiarity as starting load factor
Validation_Notes: Atomic illustrative factor for starting load costs.

Natural_Language: Preparatory costs incurred in preparing to perform the terminated contract include such costs as those incurred for initial plant rearrangement and alterations, management and personnel organization, and production planning. They do not include special machinery and equipment and starting load costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_c_2_a: Preparatory costs include initial plant rearrangement/alterations, management/personnel organization, production planning; P_31_205_42_c_2_b: Excludes special machinery/equipment and starting load costs
Validation_Notes: Definitional with explicit exclusions. Preparatory costs are distinct from (c)(1) starting load costs and from special equipment.

Natural_Language: When initial costs are included in the settlement proposal as a direct charge, such costs must not be included in overhead. Initial costs attributable to only one contract must not be allocated to other contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_c_3_a: Direct-charged initial costs must not be in overhead; P_31_205_42_c_3_b: Single-contract initial costs must not be allocated to other contracts
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Two mandatory anti-duplication rules. Prevents double-counting of initial costs. HIGH-RISK: dual implications with negations.

Natural_Language: If initial costs are claimed and they have not been segregated on the contractor's books, they must be segregated for settlement purposes from cost reports and schedules reflecting that high unit cost incurred during the early stages of the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_c_4: Unsegregated initial costs must be segregated from cost reports/schedules for settlement
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Mandatory ("must"). Conjunctive antecedent triggers segregation requirement. HIGH-RISK: implication with negation.

Natural_Language: If the settlement proposal is on the inventory basis, initial costs should normally be allocated on the basis of total end items called for by the contract immediately before termination; however, if the contract includes end items of a diverse nature, some other equitable basis may be used, such as machine or labor hours.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_c_5_a: Inventory-basis settlement: initial costs allocated by total end items pre-termination; P_31_205_42_c_5_b: Diverse end items: other equitable basis may be used (e.g., machine/labor hours)
Validation_Notes: Advisory ("should" / "may"). Default allocation by end items with discretionary alternative for diverse items. "May" = permissive tautology. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Loss of useful value. Loss of useful value of special tooling, and special machinery and equipment is generally allowable, provided the conditions in (d)(1)-(3) are met.
Validation_Notes: Conditional allowability. "Generally" qualified by "provided." All three conditions conjunctively required. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Special tooling, or special machinery and equipment is not reasonably capable of use in the other work of the contractor;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_d_1: Special tooling/machinery/equipment not reasonably capable of use on other contractor work
Validation_Notes: Atomic condition. Equipment must have no reasonable alternative use. Mirrors (a) common items analysis.

Natural_Language: Government's interest is protected by transfer of title or by other means deemed appropriate by the contracting officer; and
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_d_2: Government interest protected via title transfer or other CO-approved means
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive condition. Government protection required through title transfer or alternative mechanism at CO discretion.

Natural_Language: Loss of useful value for any one terminated contract is limited to that portion of the acquisition cost, which bears the same ratio to the total acquisition cost as the terminated portion of the contract bears to the entire terminated contract, and other Government contracts for which the special tooling, or special machinery and equipment was acquired.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_d_3: Loss limited to proportional acquisition cost (terminated portion / total contract + other Government contracts)
Validation_Notes: Mathematical limitation. Pro-rata formula prevents claiming full acquisition cost when only part of the contract was terminated or when equipment served multiple contracts.

Natural_Language: Rental under unexpired leases. Rental costs under unexpired leases, less the residual value of such leases, are allowable when reasonably necessary for the performance of the terminated contract, if conditions in (e)(1) and (e)(2) are met.
Validation_Notes: Conditional allowability. Three conjunctive requirements: reasonable necessity plus both sub-conditions. Net of residual value. HIGH-RISK: implication. Cross-referenced by 31.205-36(c).

Natural_Language: The amount of rental claimed does not exceed the reasonable use value of the property leased for the period of the contract and such further period as may be reasonable; and
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_e_1: Rental claim limited to reasonable use value for contract period plus reasonable extension
Validation_Notes: Cost ceiling based on reasonable use value. Temporal scope includes contract period plus reasonable additional time.

Natural_Language: The contractor makes all reasonable efforts to terminate, assign, settle, or otherwise reduce the cost of such lease.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_e_2: Contractor must make all reasonable efforts to mitigate lease costs (terminate, assign, settle, or reduce)
Validation_Notes: Mitigation obligation. Disjunctive methods (terminate, assign, settle, or reduce) but effort itself is mandatory.

Natural_Language: Alterations of leased property. The cost of alterations and reasonable restorations required by the lease may be allowed when the alterations were necessary for performing the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_f_a: Alteration and reasonable restoration costs required by lease; P_31_205_42_f_b: May be allowed when necessary for contract performance
Validation_Notes: "May" = permissive/discretionary. Contract necessity is a prerequisite condition but does not guarantee allowability. HIGH-RISK: implication with tautology for "may."

Natural_Language: Settlement expenses.
Validation_Notes: Parent for settlement expense provisions: allowable categories and segregation requirement.

Natural_Language: Settlement expenses, including the following, are generally allowable:
Validation_Notes: Parent for three categories of generally allowable settlement expenses. "Generally" qualifies allowability.

Natural_Language: Accounting, legal, clerical, and similar costs reasonably necessary for the preparation and presentation of settlement claims to the contracting officer, and the termination and settlement of subcontracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_g_1_i_a: Accounting/legal/clerical costs for preparing/presenting settlement claims to CO; P_31_205_42_g_1_i_b: Costs for termination/settlement of subcontracts
Validation_Notes: Two purposes captured in atomic decomposition corresponding to sub-paragraphs (A) and (B). "Reasonably necessary" qualifier applies to both.

Natural_Language: Reasonable costs for the storage, transportation, protection, and disposition of property acquired or produced for the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_g_1_ii: Reasonable costs for storage, transportation, protection, and disposition of contract property
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Four conjunctive cost types (storage, transportation, protection, disposition) all allowable when reasonable.

Natural_Language: Indirect costs related to salary and wages incurred as settlement expenses in paragraphs (g)(1)(i) and (g)(1)(ii); normally, such indirect costs must be limited to payroll taxes, fringe benefits, occupancy costs, and immediate supervision costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_g_1_iii_a: Indirect costs related to (g)(1)(i) and (g)(1)(ii) salary/wages are allowable; P_31_205_42_g_1_iii_b: Normally limited to payroll taxes, fringe benefits, occupancy, immediate supervision
Validation_Notes: Allowable with limitation. "Normally" suggests standard practice, with potential exceptions. Four enumerated indirect cost types.

Natural_Language: If settlement expenses are significant, a cost account or work order must be established to separately identify and accumulate them.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_g_2: Significant settlement expenses must be separately tracked via cost account or work order
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandatory requirement. "Significant" is not defined, requiring judgment. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Subcontractor claims.
Validation_Notes: Parent for subcontractor claim provisions: general allowability and indirect expense allocation.

Natural_Language: Subcontractor claims, including the allocable portion of the claims common to the contract and to other work of the contractor, are generally allowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_h_1: Subcontractor claims, including allocable common portions, are generally allowable
Validation_Notes: General allowability. "Generally" qualifies. Allocable portion of shared claims is included.

Natural_Language: An appropriate share of the contractor's indirect expense may be allocated to the amount of settlements with subcontractors provided that the amount allocated is reasonably proportionate to the relative benefits received and is otherwise consistent with 31.201-4 and 31.203(d). The indirect expense so allocated must exclude the same and similar costs claimed directly or indirectly as settlement expenses.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_42_h_2_a: Indirect expense may be allocated to subcontractor settlements; P_31_205_42_h_2_b: Must be proportionate to benefits received and consistent with 31.201-4 and 31.203(d); P_31_205_42_h_2_c: Must exclude costs already claimed as settlement expenses
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7

Natural_Language: The imposition of a monetary penalty, or an order issued by the agency head to the contractor or subcontractor to take corrective action under 41 U.S.C. 4712 or 10 U.S.C. 4701, where the proceeding does not involve an allegation of fraud or similar misconduct; or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_b_2_ii: Monetary penalty or corrective action order in non-fraud proceeding

Natural_Language: A final decision by an appropriate official of an executive agency to debar or suspend the contractor, rescind or void a contract, or terminate for default by reason of law/regulation violation.

Natural_Language: Debar or suspend the contractor;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_b_3_i: Agency decision to debar or suspend contractor
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: debarment or suspension.

Natural_Language: Rescind or void a contract; or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_b_3_ii: Agency decision to rescind or void a contract
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: rescission or voiding.

Natural_Language: Terminate a contract for default by reason of a violation or failure to comply with a law or regulation; or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_b_3_iii: Termination for default due to law/regulation violation or noncompliance
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Default termination specifically for legal noncompliance (not performance issues).

Natural_Language: Disposition of the matter by consent or compromise if the proceeding could have led to any of the outcomes listed in paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section (but see paragraphs (c) and (d) of this section); or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_b_4: Consent/compromise disposition where proceeding could have led to (b)(1)-(3) outcomes, subject to (c) and (d) exceptions

Natural_Language: Not covered by paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section, but where the underlying alleged contractor misconduct was the same as that which led to a different proceeding whose costs are unallowable by reason of paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) of this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_b_5: Proceeding with same underlying misconduct as another proceeding with unallowable costs under (b)(1)-(3)
Validation_Notes: Anti-circumvention provision. Prevents splitting proceedings to allow costs on one while disallowing on another with same underlying misconduct. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Parent for consent/compromise cost recovery exceptions.
Validation_Notes: Parent for two exception provisions to (b) unallowability for consent/compromise situations.

Natural_Language: To the extent costs are not otherwise unallowable, costs incurred in connection with any proceeding commenced by the United States (see paragraph (b) of this section) that is resolved by consent or compromise pursuant to an agreement entered into between the contractor and the United States, and which are unallowable (solely because of paragraph (b) of this section), may be allowed if specifically provided in such agreement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_c_1_a: Costs from US-commenced proceeding resolved by consent/compromise; P_31_205_47_c_1_b: Unallowable solely due to (b); P_31_205_47_c_1_c: May be allowed if specifically provided in the settlement agreement

Validation_Notes: Permissive exception ("may"). Four conjunctive conditions. Agreement must specifically provide for cost recovery. "May" = Government discretion in negotiating settlement terms. HIGH-RISK: complex conditional with tautology.

Natural_Language: Parent for third-party settlement and whistleblower disposition exceptions.
Validation_Notes: Parent for two sub-exceptions: False Claims Act third-party settlements and whistleblower reprisal dispositions.

Natural_Language: In the event of a settlement of any proceeding brought by a third party under the False Claims Act in which the United States did not intervene, reasonable costs incurred by the contractor in connection with such a proceeding that are not otherwise unallowable by regulation or by separate agreement with the United States may be allowed if the contracting officer, in consultation with legal, determines that there was very little likelihood that the third party would have been successful on the merits.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_c_2_i_a: FCA third-party proceeding where US did not intervene, settled; P_31_205_47_c_2_i_b: Reasonable costs not otherwise unallowable; P_31_205_47_c_2_i_c: May be allowed if CO (consulting legal) determines very little likelihood of success on merits
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Complex permissive exception. Six conjunctive conditions. CO must consult legal and make merit determination. "Very little likelihood" = high bar for contractor. HIGH-RISK: highly complex conditional.

Natural_Language: In the event of disposition, by consent or compromise of a proceeding brought by a whistleblower for alleged reprisal in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 4712 or 10 U.S.C. 4701, reasonable costs incurred by a contractor or subcontractor in connection with such a proceeding that are not otherwise unallowable by regulation, or by agreement with the United States, may be allowed if the contracting officer, in consultation with legal, determines that there was very little likelihood that the claimant would have been successful on the merits.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_c_2_ii_a: Whistleblower reprisal proceeding (41 U.S.C. 4712 / 10 U.S.C. 4701) resolved by consent/compromise; P_31_205_47_c_2_ii_b: Reasonable costs not otherwise unallowable; P_31_205_47_c_2_ii_c: May be allowed if CO (consulting legal) determines very little likelihood of success on merits
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Parallel to (c)(2)(i) for whistleblower reprisal proceedings. Same "very little likelihood" standard. HIGH-RISK: highly complex conditional.

Natural_Language: To the extent that the costs are not otherwise unallowable, costs incurred in connection with a proceeding under paragraph (b) of this section commenced by a State, local, or foreign government may be allowable when the contracting officer determines that the costs were incurred either as a direct result of a Government contract term/condition or compliance with CO written direction.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Permissive exception for state/local/foreign proceedings. CO discretion with two disjunctive bases. "May" = tautology. HIGH-RISK: complex multi-element conditional.

Natural_Language: Direct result of a specific term or condition of a Government contract; or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_d_1: Costs were direct result of specific Government contract term/condition
Validation_Notes: Atomic basis for CO determination. Government contract caused the legal exposure.

Natural_Language: Result of compliance with specific written direction of the contracting officer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_d_2: Costs resulted from compliance with specific written CO direction
Validation_Notes: Atomic basis for CO determination. Government directed the action that led to the proceeding.

Natural_Language: Costs incurred in connection with proceedings described in paragraph (b) of this section which are not made unallowable by that paragraph, may be allowable to the extent that conditions (e)(1)-(3) are met.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Conditional allowability for proceeding costs not disqualified by (b). Three conjunctive conditions. "May" = permissive. HIGH-RISK: complex conditional.

Natural_Language: The costs are reasonable in relation to the activities required to deal with the proceeding and the underlying cause of action;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_e_1: Proceeding costs must be reasonable relative to required activities and underlying cause
Validation_Notes: Reasonableness condition. Proportionality test between costs and proceeding scope.

Natural_Language: The costs are not otherwise recovered from the Government or a third party, either directly as a result of the proceeding; and
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_e_2: Costs not otherwise recovered from Government or third party
Validation_Notes: Anti-double-recovery condition. Cannot charge Government if already recovered elsewhere.

Natural_Language: The percentage of costs allowed does not exceed the percentage determined to be appropriate considering the complexity of procurement litigation, generally accepted principles governing the award of legal fees in civil actions involving the United States as a party.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_e_3_a: Allowed cost percentage must be appropriate per litigation complexity and legal fee principles; P_31_205_47_e_3_b: Subject to (e)(3)(i) 80% cap and (e)(3)(ii) agreement limitations
Validation_Notes: Percentage limitation with two sub-provisions establishing specific caps.

Natural_Language: Such percentage must not exceed 80 percent of the legal costs incurred.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_e_3_i: Legal cost recovery capped at 80% of incurred legal costs
Validation_Notes: Hard cap. 80% ceiling on legal cost recovery. Contractor always bears at least 20%.

Natural_Language: Agreements reached under paragraph (c) of this section must be subject to this limitation. If, however, an agreement described in paragraph (c)(1) of this section explicitly states the amount of otherwise allowable incurred legal fees and limits the allowable recovery to 80 percent or less of the stated legal fees, no additional limitation need be applied.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_e_3_ii_a: (c) agreements subject to 80% limitation; P_31_205_47_e_3_ii_b: Exception if (c)(1) agreement explicitly states fees and limits to <= 80%, no additional limitation needed

Validation_Notes: Default application of 80% cap to (c) agreements, with exception for agreements that self-impose the limit. Prevents double-limiting. HIGH-RISK: conditional with negation.

Natural_Language: The amount of reimbursement allowed for legal costs in connection with any proceeding described in paragraph (c)(2) of this section must be determined by the contracting officer but must not exceed 80 percent of otherwise allowable legal costs incurred. No additional limitations need be applied.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_e_4_a: Legal costs for (c)(2) proceedings determined by CO; P_31_205_47_e_4_b: Must not exceed 80% of otherwise allowable legal costs; P_31_205_47_e_4_c: No additional limitations needed
Validation_Notes: Specific provision for (c)(2) proceedings. CO has determination authority with hard 80% cap. Simplified: no further percentage analysis needed beyond the 80% cap.

Natural_Language: Costs not covered elsewhere in this section are unallowable if incurred in connection with the categories in (f)(1)-(9).
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Catch-all unallowability provision. Nine disjunctive categories. "Not covered elsewhere" = residual provision. HIGH-RISK: complex disjunctive conditional.

Natural_Language: Defense against Government claims or appeals or the prosecution of claims or appeals against the Government;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_f_1: Costs of defending against or prosecuting claims/appeals involving the Government
Validation_Notes: Atomic unallowable category. Both defensive and offensive litigation against Government.

Natural_Language: Organization, reorganization, (including mergers and acquisitions) or resisting mergers and acquisitions (see 31.205-27);
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_f_2: Costs of organization/reorganization/M&A or resisting M&A (see 31.205-27)
Validation_Notes: Atomic unallowable category. Cross-reference to 31.205-27 organization costs.

Natural_Language: Defense of antitrust suits;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_f_3: Antitrust defense costs are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Atomic unallowable category.

Natural_Language: Defense of suits brought by employees or former employees of the contractor under 18 U.S.C. 1031, where the contractor was found liable or settled;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_f_4: Defense costs for employee/former employee suits under 18 U.S.C. 1031 where contractor found liable or settled

Validation_Notes: Conditional unallowability. Suit type + adverse outcome both required. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Costs of legal, accounting, and consultant services and directly associated costs incurred in connection with the defense or prosecution of lawsuits or appeals between contractors arising from teaming/JV/shared interest agreements or dual sourcing/coproduction programs (with exceptions).

Validation_Notes: Parent for inter-contractor litigation costs. Two sub-categories. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: An agreement or contract concerning a teaming arrangement, a joint venture, or similar arrangement of shared interest; or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_f_5_i: Litigation from teaming/JV/shared interest arrangements
Validation_Notes: Atomic sub-category. Teaming/JV disputes.

Natural_Language: Dual sourcing, coproduction, or similar programs, except when incurred as a result of compliance with specific terms and conditions of the contract or subcontract or written instructions from the contracting officer or when agreed to in writing by the contracting officer;
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_f_5_ii_a: Dual sourcing/coproduction litigation costs unallowable; P_31_205_47_f_5_ii_b: Exception for contract/subcontract compliance; P_31_205_47_f_5_ii_c: Exception for CO written instruction/agreement
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Default unallowability with three disjunctive exceptions. Government-directed or contract-required litigation costs carved out. HIGH-RISK: complex negated conditional.

Natural_Language: Patent infringement litigation, unless otherwise provided for in the contract.

Validation_Notes: Default unallowability with contract-specific exception. "Unless" = negated condition. HIGH-RISK: double negation.

Natural_Language: Representation of, or assistance to, individuals, groups, or legal entities that the contractor is not legally bound to provide arising from an action where the party was convicted of the violation of a law or regulation or was found liable in a civil or administrative proceeding.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_f_7_a: Costs of representing/assisting parties contractor not legally bound to support; P_31_205_47_f_7_b: Where party convicted or found liable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive antecedent: no legal obligation AND adverse outcome. Prevents charging Government for voluntary legal aid to convicted/liable parties. HIGH-RISK: complex conditional.

Natural_Language: Protests of Government solicitations or contract awards, or the defense against protests of such solicitations or contract awards, unless the costs of defending against a protest are incurred pursuant to a written request from the contracting officer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_f_8_a: Protest costs (offensive or defensive) are unallowable; P_31_205_47_f_8_b: Exception: defense costs pursuant to written CO request
Validation_Notes: Default unallowability with narrow exception for CO-requested protest defense. Note: offensive protest costs have no exception. HIGH-RISK: negated conditional.

Natural_Language: A Congressional investigation or inquiry into an issue that is the subject matter of a proceeding resulting in a disposition as described in paragraphs (b)(1) through (5) of this section (see 10 U.S.C. 3744(a)(17)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_f_9: Congressional investigation/inquiry costs where subject matter relates to (b)(1)-(5) proceeding disposition
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Unallowability for Congressional investigation costs linked to adverse proceedings. Statutory reference: 10 U.S.C. 3744(a)(17). HIGH-RISK: conjunctive conditional.

Natural_Language: Parent for cost segregation and payment withholding provisions.
Validation_Notes: Parent for cost segregation requirement and pending proceeding payment rules.

Natural_Language: Costs that may be unallowable under 31.205-47, including directly associated costs, must be segregated and accounted for separately by the contractor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_g_1: Potentially unallowable proceeding costs (and directly associated costs) must be segregated and separately accounted
Validation_Notes: Mandatory segregation ("must"). Applies to costs that "may be" unallowable, not just those determined to be. Proactive accounting requirement. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_g_2_a: Pending proceeding under (b), (f)(4), (f)(7); P_31_205_47_g_2_b: CO must withhold payment or may conditionally pay with security
Validation_Notes: Parent for two payment options during pending proceedings. (i) is mandatory, (ii) is discretionary alternative. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must withhold payment of such costs; or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_g_2_i: CO must withhold payment of potentially unallowable proceeding costs
Validation_Notes: Default action: mandatory withholding. "Must" = no discretion.

Natural_Language: When determined to be in the best interests of the Government, the contracting officer may provide for conditional payment upon provision of adequate security, or other adequate assurance, and agreement by the contractor to repay all unallowable costs, plus interest, if the costs are subsequently determined to be unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_47_g_2_ii_a: CO may provide conditional payment if in Government best interest; P_31_205_47_g_2_ii_b: Requires adequate security/assurance; P_31_205_47_g_2_ii_c: Requires contractor repayment agreement for unallowable costs plus interest
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive alternative to withholding ("may"). Three conjunctive conditions: best interest, security, repayment agreement. Includes interest on repayment. HIGH-RISK: nested implication with tautology.

Natural_Language: Research and development costs. This section addresses R&D costs sponsored by grants or required by contract performance.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating R&D definition and excess cost unallowability.

Natural_Language: Definition. Research and development, as used in this section, means the type of technical effort described in 31.205-18 but sponsored by a grant or required in the performance of a contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_48_a: R&D = technical effort per 31.205-18 when grant-sponsored or contract-required
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Distinguishes from IR&D (31.205-18) by funding source: grant or contract requirement vs. contractor-initiated.

Natural_Language: When costs are incurred in excess of either the price of a contract or amount of a grant for research and development, the excess is unallowable under any other Government contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_48_b: R&D costs exceeding contract price or grant amount are unallowable on any other Government contract
Validation_Notes: Prevents cross-subsidization of R&D overruns across contracts. "Either...or" = disjunctive trigger (price or grant amount). HIGH-RISK: implication with negation.

Natural_Language: Goodwill. This section defines goodwill and establishes that its costs are unallowable.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating goodwill definition, description, scope, and cost prohibition.

Natural_Language: Goodwill is an unidentifiable intangible asset that originates under the purchase method of accounting for a business combination when the price paid by the acquiring company exceeds the sum of the identifiable individual assets acquired less liabilities assumed, based upon their fair values.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_49_a: Goodwill = unidentifiable intangible asset from purchase-method business combination where price exceeds net fair value of identifiable assets less liabilities
Validation_Notes: Technical accounting definition. Goodwill = purchase price minus net fair value of identifiable assets/liabilities.

Natural_Language: The excess amount paid is commonly referred to as goodwill.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_49_b: The excess purchase price is commonly called goodwill
Validation_Notes: Clarifying/descriptive provision. Restates (a) in plain language.

Natural_Language: Goodwill may arise from the acquisition of a company as a whole or a portion thereof.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_49_c: Goodwill can arise from whole or partial company acquisition
Validation_Notes: Scope expansion. Goodwill not limited to whole-company acquisitions. "May" = possibility, not permission. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: Any costs for amortization, expensing, write-off, or write-down of goodwill are unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_49_d: All goodwill cost recovery methods (amortization, expensing, write-off, write-down) are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Comprehensive prohibition. "Any costs" + four enumerated methods = total ban on goodwill cost recovery. No exceptions.

Natural_Language: [Reserved]
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_50: Section reserved; no current regulatory content
Validation_Notes: Reserved section. No extractable content. Logged and passed.

Natural_Language: Costs of alcoholic beverages are unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_51: All costs of alcoholic beverages are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Categorical prohibition. One of the simplest and most absolute cost principles in the FAR. No exceptions, no conditions, no cross-references.

Natural_Language: Asset valuations resulting from business combinations. This section establishes cost principles for tangible and intangible capital asset valuations arising from business combinations using the purchase method.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating tangible and intangible capital asset valuation rules.

Natural_Language: For tangible capital assets, when the purchase method of accounting for a business combination is used, whether or not the contract or subcontract is subject to CAS, the allowable depreciation and cost of money must be based on the capitalized asset values measured and assigned in accordance with 48 CFR 9904.404-50(d), if allocable, reasonable, and not otherwise unallowable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_52_a_a: Tangible assets in purchase-method combinations; P_31_205_52_a_b: Depreciation/cost of money based on values per CAS 404-50(d); P_31_205_52_a_c: Applies regardless of CAS coverage; P_31_205_52_a_d: Must be allocable, reasonable, and not otherwise unallowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Mandatory CAS 404 valuation for tangible assets regardless of CAS applicability. Four conjunctive requirements. "Whether or not subject to CAS" extends applicability broadly. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: For intangible capital assets, when the purchase method of accounting for a business combination is used, allowable amortization and cost of money must be limited to the total of the amounts that would have been allowed had the combination not taken place.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_205_52_b: Intangible asset amortization/cost of money limited to pre-combination allowable amounts
Validation_Notes: Cost ceiling for intangible assets. Prevents business combinations from inflating intangible asset costs charged to Government. "Had the combination not taken place" = counterfactual baseline. HIGH-RISK: implication.

Natural_Language: This subpart provides the principles for determining the cost of work performed by educational institutions under contracts and contract modifications with the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_301_a: This subpart provides cost principles for educational institution contracts and contract modifications with the Government
Validation_Notes: Declarative purpose statement. Single atomic proposition. No conditional or modal structure. Straightforward scope declaration.

Natural_Language: The OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200, subpart E and appendix III, provides principles for determining the costs applicable to work performed by educational institutions under contracts with the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_302_a: OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200, subpart E and appendix III provides cost determination principles for educational institution contracts
Validation_Notes: Declarative reference to external authority (2 CFR 200). Single atomic. Cross-reference to OMB guidance is external dependency.

Natural_Language: 31.303 Requirements. Contracts referring to this subpart must comply with OMB Uniform Guidance and agencies are not expected to add restrictions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_303_a: Requirements for educational institution contracts per 31.303(a); P_31_303_b: Agency restriction limitation per 31.303(b)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating two subsections. Both requirements apply conjunctively.

Natural_Language: This subpart provides the principles for determining allowable cost of contracts, subcontracts, and modifications to contracts and subcontracts with State, local, and federally recognized Indian tribal governments.
