Natural_Language: In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3744, 41 U.S.C. 4304, 31 U.S.C. 3730, and 41 U.S.C. 4310, the following are unallowable:
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_parent: Per statutory authority (10 U.S.C. 3744, 41 U.S.C. 4304, 31 U.S.C. 3730, 41 U.S.C. 4310), costs enumerated in (c)(1) through (c)(15) are unallowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Parent for 15 unallowable cost categories. Statutory mandate (four U.S.C. citations) triggers blanket unallowability. HIGH-RISK due to implication from statutory authority to prohibition. All 15 items are conjunctively unallowable.

Natural_Language: Costs of entertainment, including amusement, diversion, and social activities, and any costs directly associated with such costs (such as tickets to shows or sports events, meals, lodging, rentals, transportation, and gratuities).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_1_a: Costs of entertainment (amusement, diversion, social activities) are unallowable; P_31_603_c_1_b: Costs directly associated with entertainment (tickets, meals, lodging, rentals, transportation, gratuities) are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Two atomics: direct entertainment costs and associated costs. Both unallowable. Parenthetical lists are illustrative examples, not exhaustive.

Natural_Language: Costs incurred to influence (directly or indirectly) legislative action on any matter pending before Congress, a State legislature, or a legislative body of a political subdivision of a State.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_2_a: Costs to influence legislative action (directly or indirectly) before Congress, State legislatures, or political subdivision legislative bodies are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive scope: both direct and indirect influence costs are captured. Applies to all levels of legislature.

Natural_Language: Costs incurred in defense of any civil or criminal fraud proceeding or similar proceeding (including filing of any false certification) brought by the United States where the contractor is found liable or has pleaded nolo contendere to a charge of fraud or similar proceeding (including filing of a false certification).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_3_a: Costs of defending civil/criminal fraud proceedings brought by the US are unallowable; P_31_603_c_3_b: Unallowability applies where contractor is found liable or pleads nolo contendere
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional unallowability: defense costs are unallowable only when the contractor is found liable or pleads nolo contendere. The proceeding must be brought by the US. HIGH-RISK due to conditional structure requiring specific disposition outcomes.

Natural_Language: Payments of fines and penalties resulting from violations of, or failure to comply with, Federal, state, local, or foreign laws and regulations, except when incurred as a result of compliance with specific terms and conditions of the contract or specific written instructions from the contracting officer authorizing in advance such payments in accordance with applicable regulations in the FAR or an executive agency supplement to the FAR.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_4_a: Fines and penalties from law/regulation violations are unallowable; P_31_603_c_4_b: Exception when incurred from compliance with specific contract terms; P_31_603_c_4_c: Exception when incurred from specific written CO instructions authorizing advance payment per FAR or agency supplement
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Default unallowable with two disjunctive exceptions. Exception requires either specific contract terms or advance written CO authorization per FAR. HIGH-RISK: conditional with negated exception structure.

Natural_Language: Costs of any membership in any social, dining, or country club or organization.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_5_a: Membership costs in social, dining, or country clubs/organizations are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. No exceptions. Covers social, dining, and country clubs disjunctively.

Natural_Language: Costs of alcoholic beverages.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_6_a: Costs of alcoholic beverages are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. No exceptions. Single atomic.

Natural_Language: Contributions or donations, regardless of the recipient.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_7_a: Contributions or donations are unallowable regardless of recipient
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. 'Regardless of the recipient' eliminates any recipient-based exception.

Natural_Language: Costs of advertising designed to promote the contractor or its products.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_8_a: Advertising costs designed to promote the contractor or its products are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Prohibition scoped to promotional advertising only. Advertising for other purposes (e.g., recruitment) not addressed here.

Natural_Language: Costs of promotional items and memorabilia, including models, gifts, and souvenirs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_9_a: Costs of promotional items and memorabilia (models, gifts, souvenirs) are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. Parenthetical list is illustrative.

Natural_Language: Costs for travel by commercial aircraft which exceed the amount of the standard commercial fare.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_10_a: Travel costs by commercial aircraft exceeding standard commercial fare are unallowable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional: only the excess above standard fare is unallowable. Commercial air travel at or below standard fare is not addressed. HIGH-RISK due to implication.

Natural_Language: Costs incurred in making any payment (commonly known as a golden parachute payment), which is--
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_11_parent: Golden parachute payments are unallowable when both conditions in (i) and (ii) are met
Validation_Notes: Parent for golden parachute definition. Both sub-conditions (i) and (ii) must be met conjunctively for the payment to be classified as unallowable golden parachute.

Natural_Language: In an amount in excess of the normal severance pay paid by the contractor to an employee upon termination of employment; and
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_11_i_a: Payment exceeds normal severance pay upon employment termination
Validation_Notes: First conjunctive condition for golden parachute classification. The 'and' connector confirms both (i) and (ii) are required.

Natural_Language: Paid to the employee contingent upon, and following, a change in management control over, or ownership of, the contractor or a substantial portion of the contractor's assets.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_11_ii_a: Payment is contingent upon and follows a change in management control or ownership of the contractor or substantial portion of contractor assets
Validation_Notes: Second conjunctive condition. Disjunctive trigger: either management control change or ownership change. Payment must be both contingent on and following the change.

Natural_Language: Costs of commercial insurance that protects against the costs of the contractor for correction of the contractor's own defects in materials or workmanship.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_12_a: Commercial insurance costs protecting against contractor's own defect correction costs are unallowable
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. Scoped to insurance against own defects only, not general commercial insurance.

Natural_Language: Costs of severance pay paid by the contractor to a foreign national employed by the contractor under a service contract performed--
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_13_parent: Foreign national severance pay under service contracts is unallowable under conditions in (i) or (ii)
Justification_Rules: Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Parent for foreign national severance pay. Two disjunctive conditions in (i) and (ii) -- either triggers unallowability.

Natural_Language: Outside the United States, to the extent that the amount of the severance pay paid in any case exceeds the amount paid in industry involved under the customary or prevailing practice for firms in that industry providing similar services in the United States, as determined in accordance with the FAR; or
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_13_i_a: Severance pay to foreign national outside the US is unallowable to the extent it exceeds customary US industry practice for similar services as determined per FAR
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional: unallowable only to the extent of the excess. Requires comparison to US industry standard. 'Or' connector with (ii) confirms disjunctive relationship. HIGH-RISK due to conditional with comparative benchmark.

Natural_Language: In a foreign country, if the termination of the employment of the foreign national is the result of the closing of, or curtailment of activities, at a United States facility in that country at the request of the government of that country.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_13_ii_a: Severance pay in foreign country is unallowable if termination results from closing/curtailment of US facility at request of host government
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive conditions in antecedent: foreign country location, termination from facility closure/curtailment, and host government request. All three must be met. HIGH-RISK due to triple-condition implication.

Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_14_parent: Legal proceeding costs governed by conditions in (i) and (ii)
Validation_Notes: Structural parent for legal proceedings cost provisions. No independent content -- subsections (i) and (ii) carry the substantive rules.

Natural_Language: Unless an exception at 31.205-47(c) or (d) applies, costs incurred by a contractor in connection with any criminal, civil, or administrative proceedings that result in dispositions described at 31.205-47(b)(1) through (5) commenced by: (A) A Federal, State, local, or foreign government, for a violation of, or failure to comply with, law or regulation by the contractor (including its agents or employees); (B) A contractor or subcontractor employee submitting a whistleblower complaint of reprisal in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 4712 or 10 U.S.C. 4701; or (C) A third party in the name of the United States under the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. 3730.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_14_i_a: Costs of legal proceedings are unallowable when resulting in dispositions per 31.205-47(b)(1)-(5); P_31_603_c_14_i_b: Exception exists at 31.205-47(c) or (d); P_31_603_c_14_i_c: Applies to proceedings by government, whistleblower complainants, or False Claims Act third parties
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex conditional with negated exception. HIGH-RISK due to multi-condition implication with exception carve-out.

Natural_Language: For any proceedings in paragraph (c)(14)(i) of this section that does not result in a disposition described at 31.205-47(b)(1) through (5), or to which exceptions at 31.205-47(c) apply, the cost of that proceeding must be subject to the limitations in 31.205-47(e).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_14_ii_a: If proceeding under (c)(14)(i) does not result in disposition per 31.205-47(b)(1)-(5) or an exception at 31.205-47(c) applies, then costs are subject to limitations in 31.205-47(e)
Validation_Notes: Fallback provision: when (c)(14)(i) unallowability does not apply (either no adverse disposition or exception applies), costs are not fully allowable but subject to 31.205-47(e) limitations. Disjunctive antecedent. Cross-references P_31_603_c_14_i and 31.205-47. HIGH-RISK.

Natural_Language: Costs incurred in connection with a Congressional investigation or inquiry into an issue that is the subject matter of a proceeding resulting in a disposition as described at 31.205-47(b)(1) through (5).
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_603_c_15_a: Costs of Congressional investigation/inquiry are unallowable when the issue is subject of a proceeding with disposition per 31.205-47(b)(1)-(5)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional unallowability: Congressional investigation costs are unallowable only when linked to a proceeding with adverse disposition per 31.205-47(b). Cross-reference to 31.205-47. HIGH-RISK.

Natural_Language: Nonprofit organization means a business entity organized and operated exclusively for charitable, scientific, or educational purposes, of which no part of the net earnings inure to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual, of which no substantial part of the activities is carrying on propaganda or otherwise attempting to influence legislation or participating in any political campaign on behalf of any candidate for public office, and which are exempt from federal income taxation under section 501 of the Internal Revenue Code.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_701_a: Nonprofit org is organized/operated exclusively for charitable, scientific, or educational purposes; P_31_701_b: No net earnings inure to private shareholders/individuals; P_31_701_c: No substantial propaganda, legislative influence, or political campaign activity; P_31_701_d: Exempt from federal income tax under IRC section 501
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional: all four conditions must be met conjunctively for an entity to qualify as a nonprofit organization. 'Means' = definitional equivalence. Four atomics capture the exclusive purpose, earnings restriction, activity restriction, and tax exemption requirements.

Natural_Language: The OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200, subpart E and appendix IV, sets forth principles for determining the costs applicable to work performed by nonprofit organizations (as defined in the OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200) under contracts with the Government. See 31.108 for exceptions to the cost principles for nonprofit organizations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_31_702_a: OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200, subpart E and appendix IV provides cost principles for nonprofit organization contracts; P_31_702_b: Exceptions to nonprofit cost principles are at 31.108
Validation_Notes: Two atomics: affirmative guidance reference and cross-reference to exceptions at 31.108. External dependency on 2 CFR 200 and internal dependency on 31.108.

Natural_Language: 31.703 Requirements. Contracts must comply with OMB guidance and agencies generally should not add restrictions, with statutory exception for 31.603(c) costs.

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating two subsections. Both apply conjunctively.

Atomic_Propositions: P_31_703_a_1: Contracts referring to this subpart must be deemed to refer to OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200, subpart E and appendix IV; P_31_703_a_2: Allowability must be determined by CO in accordance with that guidance; P_31_703_a_3: Applicable version is the one in effect on the date of the contract
Validation_Notes: Parallel structure to 31.303(a) and 31.603(a). Conditional with three mandatory conjunctive requirements. HIGH-RISK due to implication.
